It is seen as a dynamic configuration process. A key driver for the decision process is the product life cycle.

items.control_description: 4. To what level does your business operate off a profit focused operations strategy?
items.remarks: Basic: The operations strategy is based mainly on cost or service vs. a profit lens.  ||  Emerging: Profitability metrics are in place, i.e., ROIC, profitability by channel, etc. Benchmarking with other operations does not exist.  ||  Advanced: Profitability drivers are defined by functional area, customer segment and package / brand. Metrics that are in place have a history of data. Response to the data is reactive in nature and corrective actions are in place to mitigate decreases in profitability  ||  Differentiated: Total delivered cost and margin are documented for key accounts / segments. Profitability drivers are defined across the integrated operation. Response to the data is proactive, though preventative measures are not well defined.  ||  Best In Class: Profitability metrics that are in place have a history of data. Response to the data is proactive and strategic in nature and preventive actions are in place to maximize profitability. Strategic initiatives are built into the business plan that account for total delivered cost and profitability.

items.control_description: 5. To what extent do you integrate competitive benchmarking to your strategy development?
items.remarks: Basic: Current services are not positioned relative to the competition.  ||  Emerging: Current services are clearly positioned relative to the competition.  ||  Advanced: There is a defined process to identify competitors competitor’s distribution network and capacities are well understood and benchmarked. A basic notion of metrics is used to compare competitors and own performance.  ||  Differentiated: Measures are established to determine competitive position. Service improvement is driven in part by competitor’s position. Little competitive intelligence provided by customers, suppliers and strategic alliance partners. Competitive analysis focused on the immediate competitors (same industry).  ||  Best In Class: Measures are established to determine competitive position. Service improvement is driven in part by competitor’s position. Customers, suppliers, and strategic alliance partners provide competitive intelligence. Promotional plans are developed to reduce competitor’s ability to respond profitably (logistics as competitive weapon). Competitive analysis goes beyond the immediate competitors (same industry) and is extended to other industries for true best in class performance.

items.control_description: 6. What are the design objectives for your supply chain strategy?
items.remarks: Basic: Ad hoc: The supply chain has evolved without a clear design strategy, and is largely in reactive and "firefighting" mode.  ||  Emerging: Cost and service optimization: The company optimizes its own supply chain costs consistent with meeting existing customer service requirements.  ||  Advanced: Company profit maximization: The company seeks to maximize its own profit contribution by optimizing supply chain cost, speed and service.  ||  Differentiated: Supply chain profit maximization: The company seeks to maximize the profit contribution of itself and key supply chain partners by optimizing supply chain cost, speed and service across multiple enterprises.  ||  Best In Class: Flexibility and sustainability: The company and its key suppliers and customers also build-in capabilities to satisfy changing demands, minimize waste, adapt quickly to optimal cost and service level, and make maximum use of information along the entire supply chain.

items.control_description: 7. How well-defined is your supply chain strategy?
items.remarks: Basic: No documented supply chain strategy.  ||  Emerging: Ad hoc strategy exists.  ||  Advanced: Partial value chain strategy but not fully aligned with limited evidence of implementation.  ||  Differentiated: Mostly complete value chain strategy; some evidence of implementation and buy-in.  ||  Best In Class: Total value chain strategy defined and implemented, providing supply chain structure necessary to realize business strategy.

items.control_description: 8. How mature is your supply chain strategy?
items.remarks: Basic: Limited strategic alignment among internal functions, not linked to corporate strategy.  ||  Emerging: A defined supply chain strategy exists, but functional alignment to the strategy is partial or inconsistent, link to corporate strategy inconsistent.  ||  Advanced: A clearly communicated and understood supply chain strategy, built from the business strategy used as the basis for internal functional alignment.  ||  Differentiated: A defined supply chain strategy for the end-to-end supply chain is used to align key customers, suppliers, and supply chain partners, IT / Digitalization as enabler for the execution.  ||  Best In Class: A defined supply chain strategy for the end-to-end supply chain is used to align key customers, suppliers, and supply chain partners, IT / digitalization as key driver for success.

items.control_description: 9. To what level is your supply chain a strategic enabler of the business?
items.remarks: Basic: Supply chain lacks well-defined strategy to address cost or performance improvement.  ||  Emerging: Supply chain wide performance improvements focusing on cost-efficiency.  ||  Advanced: Collaborative supply chain decision making is linked to marketing / sales (focus on internal collaboration).  ||  Differentiated: Integration across the extended supply chain to drive profitable demand fulfillment.  ||  Best In Class: Profitable creation of customer value by translating innovation into execution across extended networks.

items.control_description: 10. How well does your supply chain strategy integrate with functions / business partners?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Functional strategies are developed by functional leaders. Strategy focus is on department-level budgeting. Functional areas implement IT point solutions as they see fit.  ||  Emerging: Individual functional strategies (manufacturing, procurement, and physical distribution) are aligned as part of a formal supply chain strategy. The impact of shifts in sales and marketing strategy on supply chain strategy is largely not incorporated.  ||  Advanced: Individual functional strategies (manufacturing, procurement, and physical distribution) are aligned as part of a formal supply chain strategy The impact of shifts in sales and marketing strategy on supply chain strategy is identified and appropriate changes to functional strategies are coordinated Internal IT roadmap is in place and enables the supply chain strategy.  ||  Differentiated: Supply chain strategies are developed in collaboration with key suppliers and customers. Supply chain strategies identify business objectives and major actions required to implement the strategy over a minimum 12-month horizon External IT roadmap is in place and enables the supply chain strategy.  ||  Best In Class: Supply chain strategies and information technology strategies are integrated across key business partners. The information technology architecture supports various business models and relationships. The targeted levels of internal and external integration are clearly articulated within the supply chain strategy.

items.control_description: 11. To what level do you implement regular assessment of make vs. buy?
items.remarks: Basic: In-house production processes are well established; alternatives are not regular.  ||  Emerging: Outsourcing is considered on an ad hoc basis when major changes are needed.  ||  Advanced: Outsourcing is an option that is regularly considered in production planning.  ||  Differentiated: Operational efficiency is evaluated at regular intervals, with limited support of sourcing tools and processes which are not well-defined.  ||  Best In Class: Operational efficiency is constantly under evaluation in order to identify the optimal production / sourcing mix; sourcing tools and processes are in place to identify alternatives.

items.control_description: 12. How advanced is your supplier risk assessment capability?
items.remarks: Basic: There is no formal process for risk management. No predictive monitoring in place.  ||  Emerging: Risk management guidelines are in place for procurement but there is limited evidence of a consistent approach and is typically only done for new suppliers; reactive analysis and mitigation.  ||  Advanced: Risk monitoring and ongoing assessment in place for critical suppliers only.  ||  Differentiated: Detailed risk management processes have been rolled out across procurement, supported by best practice templates, training and tools that monitor all suppliers. Robust failure safeguards in place.  ||  Best In Class: Alert / sensing driven automated risk assessment, predictive capabilities managed in real-time with future mitigation.

items.control_description: 13. How advanced is your environmental risk assessment capability?
items.remarks: Basic: There is no formal process for risk management. No predictive monitoring in place.  ||  Emerging: Risk management guidelines are in place for markets / countries but there is limited evidence of a consistent approach and is typically only done for new suppliers; reactive analysis and mitigation.  ||  Advanced: Risk monitoring and ongoing assessment in place for critical markets / countries.  ||  Differentiated: Detailed risk management processes have been rolled out for markets / countries and environment, supported by best practice templates, training and tools that monitor all suppliers. Robust failure safeguards in place.  ||  Best In Class: Alert / sensing driven automated risk assessment, predictive capabilities managed in real-time with future mitigation.

items.control_description: 14. Do you have a risk mitigation plan in place?
items.remarks: Basic: In case of any supplier delivery delays, or force majeure no alternative solution is in place.  ||  Emerging: For key suppliers alternative solutions are in place.  ||  Advanced: Alternative solutions are known, manual process.  ||  Differentiated: Alternative solutions are proactively developed.  ||  Best In Class: Alternative solutions and mitigation plans are proactively automated calculated.

items.control_description: 15. How complete is your supply chain process architecture?
items.remarks: Basic: A supply chain “process architecture” (clearly documenting activities (processes), data, metrics, applications, etc.) does not exist or exists in an unconsolidated and manually maintained format.  ||  Emerging: The process and information systems architecture is not explicitly linked to the basis of competition as described in the supply chain strategy.  ||  Advanced: The process architecture exists for some but not all supply chain sub-processes (Plan, Source, Make, Deliver, Return), data, metrics, and applications. The architecture is linked to support the strategy of the functions it supports.  ||  Differentiated: The process architecture integrates all supply chain sub-processes (Plan, Source, Make, Deliver, Return), data, metrics, and applications / the architecture is linked to the basis of competition as described in the supply chain strategy.  ||  Best In Class: The process architecture integrates all supply chain sub-processes (Plan, Source, Make, Deliver, Return) and describes the links with other core processes (e.g., Product Development, Marketing, Sales, Finance).

items.control_description: 16. How well defined and maintained are your supply chain processes?
items.remarks: Basic: Discrete supply chain processes (Plan, Source, Make, Deliver) are not documented.  ||  Emerging: Internal supply chain processes are consistently followed and well understood Accurate and approved work instructions / process plans are available through a controlled document management system Data models are not well-defined and a central data warehouse / data mart does not exist.  ||  Advanced: Internal supply chain process and data models are consistently followed and well understood Accurate and approved work instructions/ process plans are available through a controlled document management system A data warehouse / data mart is the source of all planning (master) data, business rules and transaction data Repository of current regulatory requirements is maintained.  ||  Differentiated: External process and data models are consistently followed and implemented with key customers and suppliers to support collaboration. Key requirements for data sharing with customers and suppliers are identified. Analytical tools enable the ongoing maintenance and improvement of the business rules based on actual data. Automated generation and submission of regulatory documents.  ||  Best In Class: Changes in other core processes that affect supply chain workflow are automatically identified for action reliable continuous improvement process and methodology is implemented effectively planning data, business rules and transaction data are synchronized electronically across supply chain partners.

items.control_description: 17. How good is your process effectiveness and execution?
items.remarks: Basic: Performance measures are partially established but are not evaluated in a structured manner throughout the network.  ||  Emerging: Performance measures are established and regularly evaluated but there are not explicit links to business performance.  ||  Advanced: Structured business metrics are in place to monitor key business factors and identify potential areas to improve supply chain processes; however, actions are not consistently taken to make improvements.  ||  Differentiated: Structured business metrics are in place with regular actions to make improvements, but there is not a well-defined balanced scorecard or risk mitigation approach.  ||  Best In Class: Highly detailed metrics, key performance indicators (KPI), and scorecards are utilized to regularly evaluate and adjust business performance, identify areas for improvement, and minimize exposure to risk.

items.control_description: 18. What mechanisms are in place to control the differentiated supply chains in your business?
items.remarks: Basic: No real strategy in place supply and demand chains managed purely at an operational level.  ||  Emerging: Some level of policy setting by senior management – some ad-hoc scheduling attempts to resolve forecast error and imbalances. Chain still managed at operational level. Forecast errors still can impact planning.  ||  Advanced: Strategy document in place. Levels of control (policies, short term planning, scheduling) are not fully integrated.  ||  Differentiated: Strategy document in place three integrated hierarchical levels of control – policy setting, short-term planning and scheduling with different resolution and time horizons.  ||  Best In Class: Strategy links with and is supported by broader BU / corporate strategy. Strategic, tactical and operational linkages which extend to customer and supplier.

items.control_description: 19. What level of an overarching supply chain innovation strategy is in place?
items.remarks: Basic: No supply chain innovation strategy is in place. Innovation operates separately from the supply chain group. No anticipatory conflict handling methodology or people who have these kind of capabilities is in place.  ||  Emerging: Innovation and supply chain engage in an ad hoc manner, as issues arise.  ||  Advanced: Innovation and supply chain have formal touchpoints in place to deal with new product development and introduction. The process lacks anticipatory conflict handling with supply chain engaged at later stages.  ||  Differentiated: Innovation and supply chain are integrated through formal processes. An anticipatory conflict handling methodology and people who have these kind of capabilities is in place.  ||  Best In Class: Innovation and supply chain are integrated through formal processes. Advanced tools to speed collaboration and time-to-market are used.

items.control_description: 20. How well developed is your supply chain technology roadmap?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: No roadmap in place. Equipment is bought based on individual requirements. AGVs, automated sensor information, Barcode, pick-by light.  ||  Emerging: Technologies within plants are standardized. AGVs, silo based augmented reality solutions at some plants.  ||  Advanced: Technology roadmap in place. Piloting of new technologies by individual project teams. AGVs, 3D printing, augmented reality solutions, smart devices to receive and confirm tasks across all plants.  ||  Differentiated: Digital technology 3-5 year roadmap in place. Standardization, piloting and global rollout as standard procedure for adapting new technologies. augmented / virtual reality solutions, AGVs, 3D printing, collaborative robotics, smart robots, robotic process automation (RPA), smart devices to communicate across all plants.  ||  Best In Class: Digital technology 3-5 year roadmap in place. Standardization, piloting and global rollout as standard procedure for adapting new technologies. AI, augmented / virtual reality solutions, AGVs, 3D printing, collaborative robotics, smart robots, robotic process automation (RPA), smart devices used to communicate.

items.control_description: 21. How well developed is your innovation collaboration roadmap?
items.remarks: Basic: Unclear strategy with highly dispersed systems.  ||  Emerging: Tools and systems vary by organization / business / team.  ||  Advanced: Well-defined strategy and roadmap.  ||  Differentiated: Single system for increased communication and collaboration.  ||  Best In Class: Delivery-focused roadmap with integrated systems.

items.control_description: 22. To what level is mass customization included in your supply chain strategy?
items.remarks: Basic: Mass production with goal of long run, few changeovers. Change overs are time consuming, customization is thought of as value-destroying.  ||  Emerging: Limited customization takes place through an inefficient process or leveraging separate production capabilities or co-manufacturers.  ||  Advanced: There is some capability to customize, however, the COGS is at least 25% higher than with standard product. Some product / service bundling is offered.  ||  Differentiated: Mass customization is viewed as a goal of the company but the operations are not yet fully in place to deliver on this. A small, but increasing, percentage of the volume is customized.  ||  Best In Class: Ability to mass customize is viewed as a competitive strength and operations have been modified to accomplish this. A substantial percentage of the company's output is customized in some fashion. Cost of customization has been driven to within +10% of the average production cost of items which are not customized.

items.control_description: 23. To what level is postponement included in your supply chain strategy?
items.remarks: Basic: Products are completed by the end of the manufacturing process. No value added activities occur during the distribution process.  ||  Emerging: Modifications to products after primary production are done in an ad hoc manner, requiring significant cost.  ||  Advanced: There are some modifications in products that can be made in the distribution channel, but they are limited. These modifications are done to assuage customer demands for product rather than viewed as a competitive advantage. Customer order instructions are freeform in a “special instructions” section of the order.  ||  Differentiated: Postponement strategies have been defined for a limited set of SKUs. The postponement approach is largely reactive, based on adjustments to existing products vs. incorporated early on in the design process.  ||  Best In Class: Postponement is considered an integral part of the design process, with supply chain included in the development process. The number of SKUs available to customers is a multiple of the number of SKUs held in primary warehouses. Inventories are reduced through various means (e.g., building custom display mods in the distribution channel, completion of the production by the customer or consumer, customizing the product in the retail store, etc.).

items.control_description: 24. How well integrated are your process technology choices to your supply chain strategy?
items.remarks: Basic: Information, manufacturing, and operations technology provide basic functionality to run a business. Errors and breakdowns from technology and processing choices result in low yield and high rework, thereby increasing costs.  ||  Emerging: Process technology is evaluated in the context of the supply chain strategy in a reactive way, resulting in incomplete ability to deliver on the strategy (e.g., service, cost, customization).  ||  Advanced: Technology capabilities meet minimum business needs, but opportunities to enhance automation and sophistication of systems exist.  ||  Differentiated: Technology capabilities deliver competitive advantage to a limited extent but do not fully support the supply chain strategy.  ||  Best In Class: Technology is used to strategically create excellence in multiple processes, in support of the end-to-end supply chain strategy. Investments in technology drive excellence, consistent IT, and manufacturing processes, consistently maximizing efficiency, functionality and system usability.

items.control_description: 25. How well defined and implemented is your partnering strategy?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: All suppliers / partners are managed the same way. Suppliers / partners are mainly managed on a purely transactional basis with no or only a few key partnerships or alliances in place. Goals and objectives are non-existent, metrics are unexplored.  ||  Emerging: Goals and objectives for strategic partners and suppliers are considered and metrics explored. Partnering guiding principles based on processes, objectives, governance arrangements, KPIs and continuous development requirements are only partially defined. Core vs. non-core assessment is done based on personal opinion rather on a data driven approach.  ||  Advanced: Partnering strategy is in place and includes clearly defined relationship types, processes, governance arrangements, KPIs and continuous development plans. Limited involvement in key relationships. Core vs. non-core assessment is done with a data driven approach.  ||  Differentiated: Partnering strategy includes clearly defined relationship types linked to differentiated objectives, governance arrangements, KPIs and continuous development plans. Fully involved in all key relationships. Core vs. non-core assessment is regularly reviewed. For key business areas big data analytics are used.  ||  Best In Class: Partnering strategy and process is continuously evolved, successes and failures are identified, vision and direction of partnering approach is continually aligned. New / current employee direction is reaffirmed. Core / non assessment is based on big data analytics and continuously reviewed.

items.control_description: 26. How collaborative are the supply chain processes?
items.remarks: Basic: Forecasts generated by internal teams with little to no engagement of customers / suppliers.  ||  Emerging: Forecasts from customers are used in planning. Forecasts are shared with key suppliers.  ||  Advanced: Trading partners share forecast and planning information. It is possible to question a trading partner’s forecast if it cannot be fulfilled from a supply point of view.  ||  Differentiated: Trading partners utilize and trust each other’s information and plans. Joint capacity planning is performed to a limited extent. Management of potential issues tends to be reactive.  ||  Best In Class: Trading partners utilize and trust each other’s information and plans. Joint capacity planning is performed. There is proactive management of potential issues within a supply chain or channel. Performance measurements are assessed across all partners in an open system.

items.control_description: 27. How synchronized is the supply chain?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Synchronization is limited to annual planning cycles or processes within a single manufacturing facility.  ||  Emerging: Processes within functions are synchronized. Lot sizes and operations are not fully synchronized.  ||  Advanced: Processes within functions are synchronized. Operations and lot size are synchronized to prevent buildup of excessive work in process or buffer inventories within an entity. Planning cycles are compatible between functions.  ||  Differentiated: Planning cycles and time periods are compatible across functions. Operations and lot sizes are sync to prevent buildup of excessive work in process or buffer inventories within each entity. Cash transfers are timely, efficient and consistent with the transfer of value.  ||  Best In Class: Planning cycles and time periods are compatible across functions and trading partners. Operations and lot sizes are sync to prevent buildup of excessive work in process or buffer inventories both within each entity and between trading partners. Cash transfers are timely, efficient and consistent with the transfer of value.

items.control_description: 28. How seamless is the integration of external partners to the supply chain?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Some operations are outsourced, however, the hand off of information is clumsy, and the whole supply chain is not optimized. The outsourced functionality operates on a transactional rather than an integrated operations basis.  ||  Emerging: Outsourced operations have good integration of information flows. Incentives are not aligned, resulting in inefficient behaviors.  ||  Advanced: Outsourced operations are managed smoothly. There may still be some discontinuity at handoff points. Incentives are partially but not completely aligned.  ||  Differentiated: Trading partners are tightly integrated, with well-aligned incentives. Service is still not seamless and there is some redundancy of inventory or functions.  ||  Best In Class: Trading partners operate as one entity, providing seamless service to customers / consumers. There is no redundancy of inventory or functions.

items.control_description: 29. To what level are detailed cost analyses incorporated to how you optimize your supply chain?
items.remarks: Basic: Cost analysis is done and available by function on an ad hoc basis at the physical case level. No integration of cost per case across functions. No activity based costing. Productivity is measured for major processes. Cost targets developed for awareness of mid-level management. Cost target occasionally met. Budgets developed with input from mid management.  ||  Emerging: Cost analysis is done and available by function on regular basis at the physical case level. Limited integration of cost per case across functions.  ||  Advanced: Detailed reports and tracking of cost trends by case and by process. Decisions are made based on common process and case cost data detailed make vs. buy analysis is done. Detailed costing enables piecemeal project infrastructure improvements awareness of cost targets at shop floor level cost target met more than 90% of the time budgets obtained with cross functional participation.  ||  Differentiated: Activity-based costing and make vs. buy analysis are regularly used, with modeling for both done on an ad hoc basis. Basic to mid-level costing / modeling tools are used. Limited accountability for cost at individual worker level.  ||  Best In Class: Activity-based costing and make vs. buy analysis are regularly used as vehicles to understand cost to serve. Modeling for both is regularly updated. Reports are done down to SKU and customer level for at least warehouse to outlet cost to serve. ABC includes warehouse, transportation, pallet building, delivery options, merchandising, order management, etc. Sophisticated costing / modeling tools are used. Full accountability for cost at individual worker level. Cost targets always met budgets determined with joint planning process with input from all levels.

items.control_description: 30. How do you optimize your supplier network?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Warehouse / regional warehouse location was optimized / defined once and then executed.  ||  Emerging: Tandem, triangle and regional warehouse solutions are modeled offline and improved on a regular basis.  ||  Advanced: Advanced scenario assessment is in place, evaluating, costs, capacity utilization, service level & delivery time and risks.  ||  Differentiated: Near time optimization of network structure on a SKU level based on forecasts, promotions etc..  ||  Best In Class: Near time optimization of network structure on a SKU level based on forecasts, promotions based on continuously conducted big data analytics.

items.control_description: 31. How well developed and integrated is your production strategy?
items.remarks: Basic: Cost-optimized, centralized / regionalized production network optimum of transport and warehouse vs. production & invest vs. inventory cost.  ||  Emerging: Production locations have been selected close to market / customers to ensure visibility on market trends and customer requirements and increase flexibility.  ||  Advanced: Production network allows for ad hoc footprint setup and removal for project purposes to increase flexibility for relevant business areas.  ||  Differentiated: Production network has been optimized according to differing business requirements (e.g. stronger focus on outsourcing to increase flexibility and in-house production for cost-driven businesses).  ||  Best In Class: Production network has been optimized according to differing business requirements and including supplier and customer ecosystem (e.g. stronger focus on outsourcing to increase flexibility and in-house production for cost-driven businesses).

items.control_description: 32. To what level have you implemented strategic network planning as part of your supply chain strategy?
items.remarks: Basic: No strategic network planning is done.  ||  Emerging: First approaches have been made towards strategic network planning.  ||  Advanced: Strategic network planning has been partially realized.  ||  Differentiated: Strategic network planning has been realized for major business areas.  ||  Best In Class: Strategic network planning is done in line with product portfolio planning and further external conditions as part of corporate strategy on a regular basis.

items.control_description: 34. What level of segmentation is used to develop your supply chain strategy?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: No segmentation existing for customers, products or demand.  ||  Emerging: Single segmentation approaches exist, e.g., within production or warehouse.  ||  Advanced: A significant part of the supply chain is based on segmentation of demand as well as an intelligent segmentation of supply processes, beginning from customer service level to demand and order management as well as production and inventory / warehouse management. Segmentation criteria are evaluated continuously (annually).  ||  Differentiated: Segmentation is used to drive supply chain strategy across some functions but it is not implemented end-to-end.  ||  Best In Class: The entire supply chain is based on segmentation of demand as well as an intelligent segmentation of supply processes, beginning from customer service level to demand and order management as well as production and inventory / warehouse management. Segmentation criteria are evaluated continuously (annually).

items.control_description: 35. To what level is your supply chain tailored to the market?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Ad hoc: Standard supply chain strategies, policies and processes are incomplete or not well-defined.  ||  Emerging: One-size fits-all: Standard supply chain strategies, policies and processes exist but are not differentiated by customers /segments.  ||  Advanced: Adaptive: Standard supply chain strategies, policies and processes exist, but are adapted to accommodate the requirements of certain customers / segments.  ||  Differentiated: Tailored to key customers: tailored supply chain strategies, policies and processes are developed for key customers reflecting their unique requirements; standard supply chain strategies, policies and processes exist for other customers / segments.  ||  Best In Class: Tailored to customers and products: supply chain strategies, policies and processes exist that reflect unique characteristics and requirements of customers, as well as unique manufacturing and distribution characteristics, demand variability and volume of groups of products.

items.control_description: 36. What level of policies are in place to operate the differentiated supply chains in your business?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Undifferentiated supply policies – all products made to meet short-term demand Uniform levels of customer service.  ||  Emerging: Selective supply policies – e.g., some seasonal build strategies. Policies developed at operational and tactical levels through ad-hoc process.  ||  Advanced: Policies developed based on economic alternate source, inventory, utilization and service trade-offs.  ||  Differentiated: Policies developed based on economic alternate source, inventory, utilization and service trade-offs. Customers are given differentiated service levels. Policies applied for end products.  ||  Best In Class: Policies articulated for end products, intermediate products and raw materials in terms of supply lead times, reliability, batch size and supply source. Policies developed at senior management level via trade-offs.

items.control_description: 37. To what level is product segmentation used in how you operate the supply chain?
items.remarks: Basic: Inventory is classified by velocity but not criticality, value or volatility. Replenishment decisions are not differentiated between inventory classes.  ||  Emerging: Inventory is classified by a broad range of criteria (e.g., velocity, value, volatility, criticality). Replenishment decisions are differentiated based on inventory classes..  ||  Advanced: Products are segmented by velocity and stage of life cycle.  ||  Differentiated: Products segmentation incorporates profitability. Product line is regularly pruned based on contribution.  ||  Best In Class: Products are segmented by profitability, channel, stage of product life cycle, ability to customize, etc..

items.control_description: 38. To what level is consumer segmentation used in how you operate the supply chain?
items.remarks: Basic: Consumer segments are not considered in supply chain design.  ||  Emerging: Consumer segments drive operations variability on an ad hoc basis, rather than proactively.  ||  Advanced: Product and service options are based on the needs of broadly defined consumer segments.  ||  Differentiated: Products and services are tied to the needs of narrow, well defined consumer segments. Variability is not well controlled within those segments.  ||  Best In Class: Products and services are tied to the needs of narrow, well defined consumer segments. Variability is controlled within narrow bounds for each segment.

items.control_description: 39. To what level is customer segmentation used in how you operate the supply chain?
items.remarks: Basic: No segmentation of customers.  ||  Emerging: Limited segmentation of customers based on volume.  ||  Advanced: Some differentiation between consumers and customers.  ||  Differentiated: Customers are segmented based on a limited set of criteria (e.g., service).  ||  Best In Class: Customers are segmented by a complete set of criteria, e.g., service requirements, channel, profitability, etc.

items.control_description: 40. To what level is supplier segmentation used in how you operate the supply chain?
items.remarks: Basic: No segmentation of suppliers.  ||  Emerging: Limited segmentation of suppliers based on purchase volume.  ||  Advanced: Some segmentation of suppliers and strategic supply partners, with limited differentiation in treatment.  ||  Differentiated: Suppliers are segmented based on strategic importance and capabilities with clear differentiation in how those suppliers are leveraged and engaged with.  ||  Best In Class: Suppliers are classified by strategic importance, degree of integration, ability to leverage, degree of permanence, etc.

items.control_description: 41. To what level is segmentation used in your production strategy?
items.remarks: Basic: Operations strategy emphasizes target customers or consumers by type and not by segmentation based on needs.  ||  Emerging: Operations strategy incorporates limited segmentation of customer needs. Cost information is based on allocations vs. activity based.  ||  Advanced: Costs are well understood and activity based to drive profitability based segmentation.  ||  Differentiated: Segmentation is use to a limited extent, not fully connecting across customers, products and suppliers.  ||  Best In Class: Segmentation of customers, products and suppliers is utilized as the basis for investment, joint operations improvement, product development, etc.

items.control_description: 1. To what extent do you use data analytics and AI in order to improve current and future designs / software solutions / value offerings?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Product development is mainly driven by innovation of internal product development team. Product performance feedback is used for product development / refinement at the most.  ||  Emerging: R&D receives manual notifications about product failures in the field, machine breakdowns or quality issues. Issues can be manually linked to design issues of certain components / combinations, however these are not yet incorporated into digital solutions or applications. Internal functions like sales, service, procurement or production suggest improvements.  ||  Advanced: Product performance data have already delivered successful improvements to existing products and services.  ||  Differentiated: Product performance data have already delivered successful new digital products and services.  ||  Best In Class: AI is in place to analyze current designs and to provide recommendations for future component designs, e.g. features not used at all, errors due to user unfriendliness, component cost can be reduced since performance is not a user requirement. Data on product performance and usage along the entire product lifecycle and from the ecosystem (# produced items, maintenance, product variants produced etc.) is completely integrated in the development of digital products and services, making it possible to derive new innovative products and services, to improve design for value and to reduce cost.

items.control_description: 2. To what extent are you using data analytics to integrate customer / consumer and partner data into new product development?
items.remarks: Basic: At maximum, feedback from customers / consumers is used for product development / refinement.  ||  Emerging: R&D receives feedback from internal functions like sales, service, procurement or production that suggest improvements, however this information is not yet incorporated into digital solutions or applications. Customer / consumer complaints are managed reactively to improve product features.  ||  Advanced: B2B customer / consumer feedback has already delivered successful improvements of existing products and services.  ||  Differentiated: B2B customer / consumer feedback and data have already delivered successful new digital products and services.  ||  Best In Class: AI is in place to analyze current designs and to provide recommendations for future component designs, e.g. feature not used at all, errors due to user unfriendliness, component cost can be reduced since performance is not required. Data on customer / consumer and componentr feedback is completely integrated in the development of digital product and services to derive new innovative products and service and to improve design for value and to reduce cost.

items.control_description: 3. To what extent are you using data analytics to integrate social media data into new product development?
items.remarks: Basic: At maximum, social media internet research is conducted manually by R&D and then used for product development / refinement.  ||  Emerging: R&D receives manual notification from marketing and other internal departments about social media trends and has started to redesign products based on the feedback received, however this process is not yet incorporated into digital solutions or applications.  ||  Advanced: Social media feedback has already delivered successful improvements of existing products and services.  ||  Differentiated: Social media and influencer feedback has already delivered successful new digital products and services.  ||  Best In Class: AI is in place to analyze current designs and to provide recommendations for future component designs, e.g. feature not used at all, errors due to user unfriendliness, component cost can be reduced since performance is not required. Social media and influencer feedback is completely integrated into the development of digital product and services to derive new innovative products and service and to improve design for value and to reduce cost.

items.control_description: 4. How do you collect and analyze end-customer / consumer behaviour data?
items.remarks: Basic: End-customer / consumer surveys are regularly conducted with new products and services.  ||  Emerging: Portals and platforms are used to assess customer / consumer expectations and to gather and access customer/ consumer feedback. Customer/ consumer feedback is constantly gathered.  ||  Advanced: Customer / consumer feedback is reguarly collected through a digital collaboration solution.  ||  Differentiated: Direct, fully digital customer / consumer access. AI is introduced to generate customer / consumer insights.  ||  Best In Class: Real time, fully digital and systemic customer / consumer integration.

items.control_description: 5. At what level are your IIoT machine connectivity capabilities? Do you use edge and cloud technology?
items.remarks: Basic: No such capabilities yet.  ||  Emerging: We are connecting our machines to the internet. Our electrical engineering and software team is fully capable of developing these solutions.  ||  Advanced: With regards to our own machines, we combine latest edge technology (e.g. basic data visualization, basic data analytics and short term data historian features, data caching, buffering and streaming, data pre-processing, cleansing, filtering and optimization, some data aggregation, device to device communications/M2M) with latest cloud technologies (e.g. complex analytics, Big Data mining, sources of business logic, machine learning rules, advanced visualizations, long term data storage / warehousing).  ||  Differentiated: We expand IIoT to all equipment and machines related to our products (incl. competitors).  ||  Best In Class: All our key components are connected to the Internet providing key information about their condition etc. Our control tower e.g. manages spare components and gathers key data for predictive maintenance. Our development team and suppliers are at the forefront of IIoT solutions.

items.control_description: 6. How do you collect and analyze product performance data in the field?
items.remarks: Basic: Basically no client data is systematically collected.  ||  Emerging: Customer / consumer surveys are conducted with new products and services.  ||  Advanced: IoT or equivalent solutions for latest products to gather valuable data. Performance data of products in the field is collected in a standardized and systematic way for majority of the current product portfolio, e.g. Sensor data like vibration, heat etc. data from each installed machine or customer / consumer usage data is collected (e.g. sonos loudspeaker).  ||  Differentiated: Advanced sensors / IoT is fully deployed to obtain better customer / consumer understanding. Performance data of products in the field is collected already since the last generation of products. Performance and usage data is available for most of the products in real time.  ||  Best In Class: Performance and usage data along the entire product lifecycle and from the ecosystem are collected. All information is available in real time and is transparently visualized.

items.control_description: 7. To which extend has R&D access to field data?
items.remarks: Basic: R&D has no access to field data.  ||  Emerging: Service crew can provide access to data.  ||  Advanced: Alert dashboard shows key errors and high level related costs that happened in the field.  ||  Differentiated: Machine breakdowns automatically analyzed (big data) for engineering relevant failure pattern and notifications are automatically generated, prioritized and provided to R&D.  ||  Best In Class: Full remote accessibility to all key machines. Sensor data provide product development relevant insights and can be used for further R&D improvement.

items.control_description: 8. To what extend are you using data analytics to integrate end-customer / consumer behaviour into new product development?
items.remarks: Basic: Limited / no use of customer / consumer data to improve next generation products.  ||  Emerging: Gained knowledge has not been incorporated in digital developments yet. R&D receives manual reported feedback through the customer / consumer claim management process of products.  ||  Advanced: Customer / consumer feedback has already delivered successful improvements of existing products and services.  ||  Differentiated: Customer / consumer feedback has already delivered successful new digital products and services.  ||  Best In Class: AI is in place to analyze current designs and to provide recommendations for future component designs, e.g. feature not used at all, errors due to user unfriendliness, component cost can be reduced since performance is not required. Data of product performance and usage along the entire product lifecycle and from the ecosystem (# produced items, maintenance, product variants produced etc.) is completely integrated in the development of digital product and services to derive new innovative products and service and to improve design for value and to reduce cost.

items.control_description: 9. How do you collect and analyze social media and influencer data?
items.remarks: Basic: No social media monitoring in place. Manual reactive research due to customer / consumer complaints.  ||  Emerging: Social media monitoring is conducted manually on corporate and brand reputation level or dedicated topics e.g. sustainability feedback; but not on product level.  ||  Advanced: Social media is monitored at product level but analyzed manually on a case-by-case basis.  ||  Differentiated: Social media is analyzed automatically. Key influences are integrated in the analysis.  ||  Best In Class: Fully integrated analytics solutions provide near real time analysis of social media. Social media real time AI supports and drives interaction with influencers and communities to get regular feedback.

items.control_description: 10. How do you collect and analyze B2B data?
items.remarks: Basic: B2B surveys are regularly conducted with new products and services. Ad-hoc meetings to manage customer / consumer product complaints.  ||  Emerging: Portals and platforms are used to assess customer / consumer expectations and to gather and access customer feedback. Customer / consumer feedback is constantly gathered. Customer/ consumer exchange meetings take place in a regular cadence.  ||  Advanced: Customer / consumer feedback is regularly collected through a digital collaboration solution.  ||  Differentiated: Direct, fully digital customer / consumer access. AI is introduced to generate customer insights.  ||  Best In Class: Real time, fully digital and systemic customer / consumer integration.

items.control_description: 11. How sophisticated are your product simulation capabilities?
items.remarks: Basic: Limited simulation capabilities inhouse. Physical testing and prototyping is the default solution.  ||  Emerging: CAE (FEM, CFD, CAE, MKS) solutions are frequently used across R&D / product development. Critical components are simulated. Final physical testing of products is still an essental part of the development process.  ||  Advanced: Complex simulation of complete assemblies / products conducted based on expected field usage. Strong movement towards digital testing.  ||  Differentiated: Testing results / production results and simulation results are constantly exchanged / fully integrated. “Digital testing” / simulation as the preferred option.  ||  Best In Class: Nearly all tests are virtually conducted / simulated. Processes in place to certify digital testing when physical testing is required.

items.control_description: 12. How sophisticated are your process simulation capabilities?
items.remarks: Basic: Limited simulation capabilities inhouse. Manufacturing process development is based on experience and physical testing. CAD / CAM Is used only during a highly manual design process.  ||  Emerging: Key assembly and service steps are simulated in advance. Many manufacturing / process related improvements are still first revealed during the prototyping process.  ||  Advanced: Critical manufacturing / production steps are simulated before the first prototype is built. Simulation results directly impact product development / product design.  ||  Differentiated: Complete manufacturing and service processes are simulated in advance (during the product development phase) to improve DfX. Simulation of full production lines / processes provides product improvements before the first prototype is build.  ||  Best In Class: In addition to the situation described for the digital innovator, virtual reality is used simulate assembly and service processes and to train the workforce. CAD / CAM fully automated and integrated.

items.control_description: 13. How sophisticated are your capabilities with regard to digital twins?
items.remarks: Basic: Generic digital version of the product may be available, e.g. 3D or other types of models. There is no product information available that is mapped to a specific serial number and used in product development.  ||  Emerging: Full visibility of serial numbers / batch numbers / unique identifiers that were used to build / process the product within the factory. Data is leveraged for root cause analyses and EOL-related topics in product development.  ||  Advanced: Full visibility of serial numbers / batch numbers / unique identifiers that were used to build / process the product along the entire product lifecycle (incl. suppliers and service). Data is leveraged for root cause analyses and EOL related topics, future product strategy and features in product development.  ||  Differentiated: Full digital twin along the entire product lifecycle for every product. All product relevant data along the entire lifecycle connected to the twin, e.g. manufacturing parameters, field operations data. Data from all digital twins is aggregated and analyzed for future product improvements.  ||  Best In Class: Digital twin is used to simulate production and field operations in advance. Data from the twin is holistically leveraged to improve current and future products.

items.control_description: 14. How sophisticated is your data management process / your usability of data?
items.remarks: Basic: Multiple data sources with partially or fully conflicting / duplicating data. Data from various data sources has to be manually linked to facilitate data integration/ usage across sources.  ||  Emerging: All product development relevant data are managed in one central system. All product development relevant data digitally captured, organized / strutured and easily accessible.  ||  Advanced: Clear data management process to facilitate seamless integration of manufacturing / process / service and product develoment data. Manual data cleansing and preparation still required. Data quality is good and mainly without errors.  ||  Differentiated: Clear data management process to facilitate seamless integration of supplier and customer / consumer data. The need for manual data cleansing and preparation is limited.  ||  Best In Class: Single source of truth. Data across the entire product lifecycle is fully integrated / linked / linkable. Limited data cleansing required.

items.control_description: 15. What type of data do you, in general, leverage for your product development process?
items.remarks: Basic: Only department internal data / information is leveraged.  ||  Emerging: Production / manufacturing data is leveraged.  ||  Advanced: Supplier data is leveraged through offline data analytics.  ||  Differentiated: Product data from the field is leveraged through the use of real time data analytics.  ||  Best In Class: Data from the entire value chain are constantly assessed and leveraged. Big data and AI are leveraged to extract value adding information.

items.control_description: 16. To what extend do you use data analytics and AI in optimizing DfX requirements?
items.remarks: Basic: Not applicable.  ||  Emerging: Processes and procedures in place to ensure DFX compliance. Processes are mainly manually triggered by an internal release process of all related stakeholders.  ||  Advanced: Concept to describe products and services based on key features and functionalities is under development. Database to easily compare products and services for e.g. Design for Service, design for value, design for manufacturing is available.  ||  Differentiated: Advanced database provides value adding insights to the DFX based on experience with similar products. Based on features and functional requirements, products can be compared with existing solutions. Design for service, design for value, design for manufacturing are all key criteria that are assessed. Categorization of products is an essential / fully integrated step in the product development.  ||  Best In Class: Simulations are conducted to ensure and optimize DFX. The optimized compromise is found and / or deviations from the ideal state are automatically highlighted. AI is applied to further optimize the DFX process in future.

items.control_description: 17. To what level are your simulations used for product verification and validation?
items.remarks: Basic: Simulation is not at all used for verification and validation.  ||  Emerging: Verification of selected components done through simulation. Limited physical testing for final verification required.  ||  Advanced: Verification of selected components done without physical testing. Digital validation projects initiated with key customer / consumer.  ||  Differentiated: Product verification and validation to the largest extend conducted through simulation / with limited physical testing.  ||  Best In Class: Product verification and validation is certified by official agencies / government bodies etc.

items.control_description: 18. How does your data provision / availability from suppliers and within your factories look like?
items.remarks: Basic: No real time data available. Data are only available on demand.  ||  Emerging: Key product related production and quality data are provided on a daily basis.  ||  Advanced: Key product related production and quality data are provided in near real time. Supplier data structured and easily accessible on demand.  ||  Differentiated: Full accessibility to key product and process related data in real time. Supplier data shared through a common database - aligned data management.  ||  Best In Class: Real time data of all products across the entire value chain available.

items.control_description: 19. How do you analyze cost of designed products in the development phase?
items.remarks: Basic: Mainly experience-based. Highly dependend on capabilities of the development engineers.  ||  Emerging: Early integration of production and suppliers allow for ealy cost transparency and understanding of key cost drivers.  ||  Advanced: Concept to describe products and services based on key features and functionalities is in development. Database to easily compare products and services for e.g. should cost analysis in place.  ||  Differentiated: Comprehensive database for should cost analysis in place. Based on features and functional requirements, products can be compared with existing solutions. Categorization of products is an essential / fully integrated step in the product development.  ||  Best In Class: Should cost analysis runs in parallel to the product development. AI supported tools provide feedback on expected costs based on costs of existing products.

items.control_description: 20. How do you prototype and test your digital products and services?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Same principles apply as with our standard products. Use of POCs (proof of concepts) and prototypes that are already close to the final solution. Tests are done internally.  ||  Emerging: Concept of testing early prototypes with customers / consumers is beginning to gain acceptance and is applied by the development team.  ||  Advanced: Partially functional elements of future products and services used to validate entire user experience through high experience proximity.  ||  Differentiated: Fully functional elements of future products and services used to validate entire user experience through high experience proximity. Prototypes are recyclable and offer the opportunity to test new paradigms of use.  ||  Best In Class: Principle of fail early is practiced. Clickable / partially functional prototypes (e.g. marketing screens, wire-frames, mock-ups, click-apps, videos) are frequently built and tested with clients. Allow early usability tests and a partial evaluation of the user experience. Limited ability to map and evaluate interaction processes or environmental conditions.

items.control_description: 21. How do you leverage data analytics in your testing process?
items.remarks: Basic: Prior test results are mainly used to plan tests and to refine test procedures.  ||  Emerging: Tool-driven testplans are developed e.g. according to Design of Experiments (DOE) (= six sigma for product development) principles to minimize tests and to maximize output. Basic analyses are performed based on test results.  ||  Advanced: All test results are stored and linked to the most important product and service attributes. Clear strategy for storing test results, designed to provide the basis for future advanced analytics.  ||  Differentiated: Test results of key product features are predicted on the basis of earlier test results. Verification tests ensure the correctness and accuracy of assumptions and / or enable extrapolation of other test results.  ||  Best In Class: AI is used to predict test results based on historical tests of similar components and processes. The number of tests performed is significantly reduced, as previous test results are combined and linked to the current product and service to be tested.

items.control_description: 22. How do you use MVPs (Minimum Viable Product) that are tested with clients?
items.remarks: Basic: No use of MVP. Development of proof of concepts and prototypes for internal testing. At most, prototypes close to serial product quality are given to selected test clients.  ||  Emerging: MVPs are currently tested in selected areas / for selected products - however everything is at an early stage.  ||  Advanced: The majority of new digital products and services is tested with customers/ consumers using MVPs. Feedback is used to develop a more customer / consumer centric / digital solution, using design for value principles.  ||  Differentiated: Concept of MVPs refined with customer / consumer is common practice through the entire product portfolio.  ||  Best In Class: Concept of MVPs includes supplier components and products of companies within the product and service ecosystem (holistic product and service offering of several companies to provide an holistic and fully integrated solution to the customers / consumers).

items.control_description: 23. What kind of attributes does your prototyping usually cover and how do you test them?
items.remarks: Basic: Essential functionalities and attributes of products and services are tested by running traditional test protocols.  ||  Emerging: Servicing of the product in the field and selected manufacturing processes are tested with the help of Virtual Reality (VR).  ||  Advanced: Key processes including manufacturability and serviceability are tested, e.g. with the help of virtual reality and advanced simulation programs.  ||  Differentiated: Prototypes are equipped with additional sensors and cameras to observe users and their behavior in a structured way.  ||  Best In Class: Various excitement attributes are included in tests with customers / consumers. Testing focuses on customer / consumer needs. Advanced sensors and big data analytics methodologies are applied to better understand future customer / consumer needs and to gather and analyze their feedback on product and service features.

items.control_description: 24. To what extent are partners or customer / consumer involved in the prototyping process?
items.remarks: Basic: No partners, suppliers or customers / consumers involved in prototyping process.  ||  Emerging: Co-creation, starting in the prototyping phase, is carried out with key suppliers / strategic partners.  ||  Advanced: In the test phase, in order to develop and test prototypes at an early stage together with key partners (suppliers and selected customers / consumers). Feedback is used to enhance the product (design for value).  ||  Differentiated: Prototypes are jointly developed and tested at an early stage with key partners (suppliers and selected customers / consumers). Feedback is used to enhance the product (design for value).  ||  Best In Class: Co-creation is fully lived. Development and testing also initiated by customers / consumers and suppliers as well as third parties.

items.control_description: 25. How do you leverage 3D printing in your prototyping process?
items.remarks: Basic: Limited use of 3D printing / additive manufacturing technologies.  ||  Emerging: Some components are printed to test their functionalities at an early stage.  ||  Advanced: If possible, tools and fixtures are printed.  ||  Differentiated: Complex assembly components and performance-enhanced components are also printed to test disrupting manufacturing processes.  ||  Best In Class: The impact of 3D printing is automatically evaluated using data analytics. Impact on total cost of ownership and functionality of 3D printed components is considered.

items.control_description: 26. What kind of prototyping principles do you follow?
items.remarks: Basic: Standard waterfall approach applied for all projects.  ||  Emerging: V-model is comprehensively used to simultaneously develop and validate products and services.  ||  Advanced: V-model, spiral model and waterfall model are used by leveraging the individual advantages of each development method.  ||  Differentiated: Agile development is used within the V-model and leveraged for internal product development.  ||  Best In Class: Agile development is fully leveraged with suppliers and customers.

items.control_description: 27. How do you leverage mixed reality in your prototyping process?
items.remarks: Basic: No mixed reality solutions used for prototyping.  ||  Emerging: Mixed Reality was used to present and test new products at a high level with management and selected customers / consumers.  ||  Advanced: Complex assemblies and system upgrades are tested through mixed reality.  ||  Differentiated: Mixed reality is used to test manufacturability, serviceability and customer / consumer acceptance for critical / selected elements.  ||  Best In Class: Mixed reality holistically used to test manufacturability, serviceability and customer / consumer acceptance.

items.control_description: 28. How do you prioritize development projects?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Projects are not prioritized.  ||  Emerging: Project priorities are functionally defined so that there are many sets of priorities across the business. Priorities reflect the value drivers for each function. Resources are often used for projects that are not authorized. There is no concept of “authorization”. Project priorities are set annually (or periodically) through budgeting. Planned projects are not taken into account. The impact of project / feature prioritization decisions on other projects / features is rarely analyzed.  ||  Advanced: There is one set of project priorities that is developed by a cross-functional team, however these apply only to some project types, and these priorities are not fully accepted by all functions within the business. Only some project priorities reflect the real value drivers for project buckets. Project priorities are set during cadenced portfolio reviews. Planned projects are authorized but not prioritized. The impact of project / feature prioritization decisions on other projects / features is sometimes analyzed and reconciled. Project authorization and prioritization are communicated manually.  ||  Differentiated: There is one set of project priorities that is developed by a cross-functional team, applies across all project types, includes all projects, and is shared across all functions in the business. Project priorities are made real through the willingness to “steal” resources from lower priority projects. Functional managers always use project priorities to make staffing decisions on individual projects. Planned projects are authorized and prioritized. The impact of project / feature prioritization decisions on other projects / features is always analyzed and reconciled. Web-enabled portfolio management tools facilitate communication of project authorization and project priorities.  ||  Best In Class: In addition prioritization is systematically supported by big data and AI, taking key company parameters into account. Project priorities are adapted cross-functionally based on e.g. changing customer / consumer expectations.

items.control_description: 29. What does your platform / product architecture strategy and execution look like?
items.remarks: Basic: No platform / architecture strategy. Use of same components / software solutions / components is mainly based on the experience of development engineers.  ||  Emerging: Software solutions support use of the same components / software solutions. Database allows smart filtering of designed components (e.g. material, application, machine type etc.). Standard components / ingredients are managed in a system to avoid duplications. Platforms exist for a few selected solutions (software, hardware, electronics).  ||  Advanced: Modular platform concepts are used for key development projects (software, products, packaging, digitization, etc.). System automatically scans for potential duplications of materials. Percentage of same components and software solutions is automatically tracked (KPIs). Trend analysis of number of same components / platforms - breakdown into different machine types possible.  ||  Differentiated: Modular platform concepts are used for all development projects (software, products, packaging, digitization, etc.). Suppliers are fully integrated and follow the platform strategy.  ||  Best In Class: Architecture-based platform strategy for full flexibility and compatibility across product lines and services. Data analytics / AI provides suggestions on how to improve existing variances in product architecture. The architecture enables virtually seamless customization.

items.control_description: 30. How do you manage your product complexity?
items.remarks: Basic: Complexity is managed by individuals. No KPIs to measure complexity. Impact of complexity is not understood.  ||  Emerging: Guidelines and trainings to reduce product portfolio complexity. Digital catalogue / tool to optimize / reduce complexity. Complexity of standard components is managed by dedicated teams.  ||  Advanced: System automatically scans for potential duplications of materials. Percentage of same components and software solutions is automatically tracked (KPIs). Complexity reduction projects are run on a regular basis. Product strategy and customer / consumer expectations closely linked to complexity management.  ||  Differentiated: Data analytics and advanced dashboards provide an overview of the revenue tail or the potential impact on revenue if revenue tail is discontinued. Implications of cost savings incl. potential procurement savings etc. are linked to each part. Costs of complexity are visible and understood across functions. Product complexity is benchmarked on a regular basis with competitors' product complexity and performance (market share, revenue incl. trends).  ||  Best In Class: AI / big data analytics is used to automatically detect components which should be discontinued. Data analytics/ AI provides suggestions on how to improve existing variances / complexity. Value of complexity for customer / consumer is constantly measured.

items.control_description: 31. How does your company manage customization / personalization?
items.remarks: Basic: Standard product and services are sold. Customization and personalization is only done for large / important customers / consumers. Experience based costing ensures profit margin for customized products and services.  ||  Emerging: Products are customized based on customer / consumer requirements. Clear guidelines on customization supported by basic evaluation tools, e.g. for costing to ensure profitable projects.  ||  Advanced: Customization strategy is part of the platform strategy and developed at an early stage of the product / service development. Core products and services remain mainly unchanged to minimize product complexity.  ||  Differentiated: Customization strategy is part of the platform strategy and developed at an early stage of the product / service development - also with key suppliers. Modular platforms facilitate a high level of flexibilityand customization with limited development effort.  ||  Best In Class: Architecture based platform strategy facilitates high level of customization across products and services. Customer / consumer requirements for customization become a key element of the product architecture.

items.control_description: 32. To which extend are all designed vs. standardized components / software modules listed and digitally documented in a central repository maintained by a cross-functional team of purchasing and engineering?
items.remarks: Basic: No central data base in place.  ||  Emerging: Central component data base of component components available and can be automatically included into the CAD system.  ||  Advanced: Searchable database allows smart filtering of designed components e.g. material, application, machine type etc. Use of new standard components has to be signed off by a dedicated team / by dedicated SMEs. components / software / ingredients / recipe categorization allow easy comparison of existing solutions and provide recommendations on potential same components/ similar components.  ||  Differentiated: Suppliers are fully connected to the data base and include part attributes to the designed components.  ||  Best In Class: AI solutions highlight potential design overlaps and recommends similar components. Feedback of users constantly improve the feedback and learning of the AI solution. Digital controls are in place to ensure architecture / modularity and complexity requirements.

items.control_description: 33. How do you manage to limit complexity whilst customizing your products?
items.remarks: Basic: Complexity during customization not managed.  ||  Emerging: Your product managers, sales reps and service crews support us in our product development process / help us define the required features.  ||  Advanced: We analyze sales and service data to get a better understanding when we develop our next products. Advanced project tracking allows comparison with past projects.  ||  Differentiated: We are digitally connected to our customers and therefore have a profound understanding of their current and future requirements. Using customer insights, we reduce the complexity of our machines by truly designing for value. Data base supported by analytics allows better assessment on complexity impact and related cost.  ||  Best In Class: AI is applied to understand to assess customization impact on product portfolio, complexity and TCO cost.

items.control_description: 34. How do you ensure that your product portfolio has the right balance between risk, investment, innovation, technology and customer / consumer requirements?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Portfolio balancing is not performed / reflected in company processes. Department heads perform portfolio balancing individually.  ||  Emerging: Portfolio investments are sporadically balanced by functional management on an event-based basis. Portfolio balance is sometimes, if at all, examined across dimensions on the basis of functional value drivers to identify overweighting and missed opportunities. Portfolio Balancing is performed using Excel or other point solution only for the function in question.  ||  Advanced: Portfolio investments are balanced by a cross-functional executive team on an event-based basis. Targets are not explicitly developed, or are incomplete in terms of project category or market category. Portfolio balance is sometimes, if at all, examined across dimensions based on cross-functionally developed value drivers to discover overweighting and missed opportunities. Portfolio Balancing is performed using Excel or other point solution.  ||  Differentiated: Portfolio investments are balanced by a cross-functional executive team on a continuing basis using project category and / or market category-based targets derived from product strategy. Portfolio balance is routinely examined across dimensions based on value drivers to discover overweighting and missed opportunities. Portfolio Balancing is performed using a portfolio management system. The portfolio balance is tracked system-based via KPIs.  ||  Best In Class: Portfolio balancing is analytically driven and determines the right mix of high-risk and low-risk projects, available resources and expected revenues and profits.

items.control_description: 35. How do you ensure that your products and services are up to date with regards to the latest technology?
items.remarks: Basic: Development engineers visit fairs to ensure build-in of latest technologies in the latest products. Product managers scan products of competitors.  ||  Emerging: A technology radar with potential implications is managed by a dedicated team. Workshops with developers are conducted on a regular basis. Technology innovation is incentivised.  ||  Advanced: Relevant start-ups are closely followed and partnerships are established. Dedicated team is assessing and testing the latest technologies.  ||  Differentiated: Digital labs are implemented to test latest technologies across industries and to build early prototypes. Labs are open for all development related functions. Technology innovation is driven by each individual.  ||  Best In Class: Clear technology leadership based on partnerships with start-ups, universities, etc. Impact assessment of latest technologies and current product portfolio is assessed by data analytics on customer / consumer and technology.

items.control_description: 36. How does your prioritization reflect your resource availability?
items.remarks: Basic: There are many more projects than available resources.  ||  Emerging: There are still more projects than resources.  ||  Advanced: Project priorities are not made real through the willingness to “steal” resources from lower priority projects. Resources are sometimes applied to projects that are not authorized. There are still some resource shortages in key functions, but the number of projects is approximately what the resources can support.  ||  Differentiated: Only authorized projects can have resources. The number of authorized projects matches the capacity of the organization. This capability matching is done at the skill set level for all relevant skill sets.  ||  Best In Class: Only authorized projects can have resources. The number of authorized projects matches the capacity of the entire developer ecosystem. This capability matching is done at the skill set level for all relevant skill sets.

items.control_description: 37. How do you determine and track project / portfolio value drivers?
items.remarks: Basic: Project / portfolio value drivers are not identified beyond financial measures.  ||  Emerging: Project / portfolio value drivers are developed for each function. Value drivers are used qualitatively in project review presentations. Values are measured and tracked in Excel based tools. Value drivers take into account primarily financial and time factors. Value drivers are partially represented in the individual project charts and aggregate portfolio views residing in functional files. Each function updates project value drivers at irregular intervals based on perceived need.  ||  Advanced: Project or portfolio value drivers do not distinguish between project types, but are developed by a cross-functional team. Value drivers are tracked in detailed excel sheets or presentations. Value drivers take into account primarily strategic, financial, and time factors. Value drivers are partially represented in the individual project charts and aggregate portfolio views residing in cross-functional Excel spreadsheets and other point solutions. A cross-functional team updates project / portfolio value drivers at irregular intervals based on perceived need.  ||  Differentiated: Value drivers are identified and uniquely developed for each project bucket by a cross-functional team. Value drivers are combined into a project scoring model that serves as a preliminary project prioritization aid. The model is fully system based. Value drivers take into account strategic, financial, market category, time, risk, viability, project category, and project status factors. Value drivers are fully represented in the individual project charts and aggregate portfolio views in a web-enabled Portfolio Management System. A cross-functional team updates project / portfolio value drivers at regular intervals to keep cadence with the market.  ||  Best In Class: Key value drivers are updated automatically and fully system-based. System provides recommendations for value drivers based on project / portfolio categories and former projects. Workforce incentives are fully linked to the scoring of the value drivers.

items.control_description: 38. How do you track the performance of your portfolio and related development projects?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: No standard model (NPV, capital recovery, etc.) or format exists to value projects.  ||  Emerging: Projects are manually valued on the basis of a baseline date only including some cross-functional expenditures.
