No cycle time or project cost standards are used. Project timelines and financials are not explicitly linked. Project financials are maintained in separate databases or files. They are not consolidated. Projects are valued but not using a standard model. Project financials are updated sporadically. Pull-through revenue and product cannibalization concepts are not used.  ||  Advanced: Projects are only valued based on remaining investment and revenue, and include only some cross-functional expenditures. This is done manually. Estimated cycle times and project costs are not grounded by peers. Some standards are used. Project timelines and financials must be manually linked, and reflect only differences in product launch timing. Project financials are partially consolidated in an Excel file or other point solution. Limited aggregate financial break-downs by project and market categories are available. Projects are valued using a standard model and format. Project financials are updated only prior to executive reviews. Pull-through revenue and product cannibalization are manually compensated on case-by-case basis. Some projects will not reflect this analysis when they should.  ||  Differentiated: Projects are valued based on remaining investments and revenue, and include all cross-functional expenditures. This is done automatically. Estimated cycle times and project costs are grounded by peers and a set of well-defined standards. Project timelines and financials are automatically linked, and reflect penalties for product launch outside the market window. Project financials are fully consolidated in real time in a Portfolio Management System which enables aggregate financial breakdowns by project and market categories. Projects are valued using standard models that differ and apply across different project types as needed. Project financials are updated as changes occur. Pull through revenue and product cannibalization are automatically handled by an intelligent model. Real options are used to value projects with large investments or large expected pay-offs.  ||  Best In Class: TCO modelling of variants fully integrated in development process along the project and product lifecycle. Cost can be easily broken down to each department and module that was developed (incl. supplier cost). Impact of changes occurred during the project, e.g. management decisions are visible. System / tool facilitates forward looking analyses based on historical data to provide input for future projects.

items.control_description: 39. How do you deal with the different development cycles of software, electronics and traditional machines?
items.remarks: Basic: Software updates are performed regularly, but cannot be carried out remotely. Changes in hardware, software and electronics occur with new product releases.  ||  Emerging: Software updates can be performed fully remotely.  ||  Advanced: Modular platform concepts allow for nearly fully independent development of the different areas. Updates and upgrades of different frequency are possible across key products.  ||  Differentiated: Suppliers are fully integrated in the Bi-modal development concept. Updates of key supplier products can be seamlessly integrated in the existing solutions.  ||  Best In Class: Update and upgrades of existing machines in the field are almost seamlessly - "plug & play" is applied for software as well as hardware components. Hardware, software and electronics can be updated / upgraded independently. Bi-modal product development is part of the product architecture.

items.control_description: 40. How often and in which way are portfolio / complexity and technology reviews conducted?
items.remarks: Basic: Reviews are not conducted.  ||  Emerging: Reviews are primarily functional conducted but not company wide driven.  ||  Advanced: Reviews are used as forums to drive improved project options. Reviews are supported by company wide defined KPIs.  ||  Differentiated: Reviews are used as forums to drive improved project options, to leverage platform synergies, and to optimize portfolio value. Project option effects are modelled in portfolio management system.  ||  Best In Class: Reviews are facilitated by data analytics. Committee  uses data / results for example to adjust targets, initiate mitigation strategies or enable changes.

items.control_description: 41. How do you digitally manage and analyze product variances?
items.remarks: Basic: No active monitoring.  ||  Emerging: Standard analyses on same components are conducted and reported on a non regular basis. We monitor our active components.  ||  Advanced: Trend analysis of the number of same components / platforms - breakdown into different machine types possible.  ||  Differentiated: Data analytics and advanced dashboards provide an overview of our revenue tail, potential impact on revenue if revenue tail is discontinued. Implications of cost savings, trends etc.  ||  Best In Class: AI / big data analytics is used to automatically propose harmonization of components portfolio.

items.control_description: 42. How do you allocate your resources?
items.remarks: Basic: Prioritization and workforce allocation are primarily carried out by the department heads (each department prioritizes largely independently).  ||  Emerging: Prioritization is linked to available resources, skills and project duration within a department and supported by software solutions. Limited adequate emphasis on cross-functional issue resolution and resource allocation.  ||  Advanced: Prioritization is linked to available resources, skills and project duration and optimized across all departments. Dynamic Portfolio Management practices are cross-functional with formal mechanisms established to resolve issues associated with assigning resources to individual projects. Advanced software solutions enable a fact-based prioritization across departments.  ||  Differentiated: Prioritization done fully cross-functional considering all resources and capabilities across all functions. Expected EBIT and project risks are integrated in the prioritization solution. Changes in prioritization are tracked in KPIs.  ||  Best In Class: Prioritization considers all resources and capabilities across all functions including key suppliers. Software solutions highlight if resources are not working according to allocation / prioritization.

items.control_description: 43. How and in which team are you setting the targets of the project / portfolio?
items.remarks: Basic: Portfolio goals are not established.  ||  Emerging: Functional goals are sometimes translated into performance and investment targets for the portfolio. Strategic preferences, if defined at all, are functional. Tracking of portfolio progress vs. goals is functionally-based and manual.  ||  Advanced: Business goals are translated into performance and investment targets for the portfolio. Goals that cannot be easily calculated, or that depend on project consolidations are overlooked. Strategic preferences are sometimes defined. Tracking of portfolio progress vs. goals is a manual process.  ||  Differentiated: Business goals are translated into performance and investment targets for each type of project bucket. Strategic preferences are well-defined and integrated into a system-based portfolio management system through use of a project prioritization algorithm. Tracking of portfolio progress vs. goals is automated by a web-enabled portfolio management system.  ||  Best In Class: Business goals are translated into performance and investment targets for each type of project bucket. Strategic preferences are well-defined and integrated into a web-enabled portfolio management system through the use of a project prioritization algorithm. Tracking of portfolio progress vs. goals is automated by a web-enabled portfolio management system.

items.control_description: 44. Which systems are used to manage the project prioritization process?
items.remarks: Basic: No system in place. Mainly Excel based.  ||  Emerging: Excel / project management tools or equivalent project dashboards are used to visualize and manage projects.  ||  Advanced: Business Intelligence (BI) dashboards are used to manage and visualize resource utilization and availability. Dashboards quickly highlight capability shortfalls.  ||  Differentiated: Project priorities are based on value / cost drivers. Project priorities are continuously evaluated in web-enabled portfolio management tool.  ||  Best In Class: One fully integrated tool for project prioritization and capability matching including suppliers and co-developers.

items.control_description: 45. Through which tool are standards and best practices documented and exchanged within your company?
items.remarks: Basic: Standards and best practices are not documented. Tacit knowledge stays within teams and individuals.  ||  Emerging: Best practices are stored on a server that is accessible to all development engineers.  ||  Advanced: Central database of best practices and standards across the entire product development process for all relevant functions.  ||  Differentiated: Easy searchable repository of best practices and standards across the entire product development process and the whole partner network. Filters allow easy search functionalities.  ||  Best In Class: AI-driven database with best practices and standards across the entire product lifecycle and the whole partner network.

items.control_description: 46. How and through which tool is the performance of the product development process tracked?
items.remarks: Basic: Performance and status is not tracked.  ||  Emerging: Performance is measured based on high level KPIs, e.g. on-time delivery, development cost, product cost, etc.. Manual data input required.  ||  Advanced: Business Intelligence (BI) dashboard includes high level development KPIs and is automatically generated. Full transparency of development costs and resource capacity.  ||  Differentiated: BI dashboard is extended to include the performance of suppliers and development partners.  ||  Best In Class: All product relevant KPIs (e.g. # of ECNs at which state, time spend vs. time planned for key components / assemblies, comparison of cost on a part level, number of same components as a percentage of total components, time spent on ECNs, quality issues during product lifecycle etc.) are automatically gathered and evaluated. Data analytics is used to compare development performance to other projects.

items.control_description: 47. How and in which tool is the product development / gate status process managed?
items.remarks: Basic: No formal gate process in place.  ||  Emerging: Formal gate process in place and standardized. Formal personal release meetings.  ||  Advanced: Segmented gate process according to development requirements (e.g. innovation, renovation etc.). Formal Gate process conducted in virtual meetings.  ||  Differentiated: Collaborative digitized release process including all product development partners.  ||  Best In Class: Fully digitized gate release process in one integrated collaboration platform along the entire product lifecycle.

items.control_description: 48. How seamlessly is your product development data transferred between R&D and operating systems and vice versa?
items.remarks: Basic: Product Specs, BOM, recipes manually transferred into procurement, production.  ||  Emerging: CAD / CAM / PDM solutions to transfer products from development to procurement, production service. The design rules ensure that we use the right mills etc. to minimize the amount of different tools needed.  ||  Advanced: 3D CAD models include all PMI (Product and Manufacturing information - 70% (time reduction) of our NC programming is done automatically by our programs.  ||  Differentiated: Also suppliers use 3D CAD models that include all PMI (Product and Manufacturing information - 70% (time reduction) of our NC programming is done automatically by our programs.  ||  Best In Class: Design for feature, not design for BOM. AI driven CAD design. 90% time reduction due to seamless transfer of our CAD data into NC programming data. Minor part changes do not require any manual adaptions.

items.control_description: 49. Through which tool are digital ideas recorded, assessed, evaluated and prioritized?
items.remarks: Basic: No formal process.  ||  Emerging: Individual processes on a department level in place.  ||  Advanced: One common database for all ideas in place. Management drives execution of most promising ideas.  ||  Differentiated: Ideas are systematically recorded, explored and tracked from all sources and regularly evaluated and prioritized in order to take them into the development phase.  ||  Best In Class: Digital AI driven database where all historical and future ideas are recorded, explored and tracked from all sources and are regularly evaluated and prioritized in order to take them into the development phase.

items.control_description: 50. How and through which tool do you conduct the engineering change process management?
items.remarks: Basic: Change requests are not formally captured, approved or tracked.  ||  Emerging: Changes are captured and tracked but approval is informal and distributed.  ||  Advanced: Formal Change Control Board (CCB) assesses and approves all changes and makes adjustments to scope and schedule as needed.  ||  Differentiated: Cross-functional release team incl. All critical development partner functions as CCB and prioritizes change requests based on business value. Historical database and AI driven platform supports the decision process.  ||  Best In Class: AI driven digital Change Control Board (CCB) platform.

items.control_description: 51. What type of communication and workflow documentation tools are in place?
items.remarks: Basic: No formal communication and documentation tool in place.  ||  Emerging: Team operates through meetings emails, video conferences and phone calls. Key documents, decisions etc. are stored on a common network drive in a standardized way.  ||  Advanced: Structured and integrated engineering process and communication platform is in place. All key decisions and tasks are recorded in a structured way. Tools like "WebEx" are used to discuss designs etc.  ||  Differentiated: Structured and integrated engineering process and collaborative communication platform includes key development partners.  ||  Best In Class: Fully digital sign-off process provided on a collaboration platform. Collaboration platform is used across functions.

items.control_description: 52. How are your documents archived and managed?
items.remarks: Basic: No central document management system. Documents are stored on individual share drives.  ||  Emerging: Central server within the product development department for all relevant documents.  ||  Advanced: Central database where all documents are centrally stored.  ||  Differentiated: Easy searchable repository where all documents are centrally stored across the entire product development process and the whole partner network, with different security levels. Filters allow easy search functionalities.  ||  Best In Class: AI-driven database where all relevant documents are stored across the entire product lifecycle and the whole partner network.

items.control_description: 53. How is the Application Lifecycle Management (ALM) conducted?
items.remarks: Basic: No software lifecycle management in place. Software solutions are standalone  ||  Emerging: Software solutions are regularly updated but no central tool in place to manage lifecycle. Design principles are in place.  ||  Advanced: Software lifecycle management in place but not fully linked to hardware portfolio management. Core architecture available but still legacy solutions in place.  ||  Differentiated: Hardware and software lifecycle management are aligned. PLM and ALM are in place. Majority of software modules are integrated in a central software platform.  ||  Best In Class: Multidisciplinary lifecycle management in place. Only one integrated software architecture which can consist of various decentralized modules (e.g. microservices).

items.control_description: 54. How automated are your PLM workflows?
items.remarks: Basic: No automation. No PLM guidelines followed.  ||  Emerging: Key workflows within product development are automated.  ||  Advanced: Key workflows across R&D, quality, supply chain and manufacturing are automated.  ||  Differentiated: Fully automated and integrated PLM processes.  ||  Best In Class: Fully automated and integrated PLM processes including processes with key suppliers and co-developers.

items.control_description: 55. How harmonized is your / are your PLM (Product Lifecycle Management) solution(s)?
items.remarks: Basic: Highly fragmented PLM landscape across all entities.  ||  Emerging: Fragmented PLM landscape but key data can be shared across systems.  ||  Advanced: One PLM solution provider but different set-ups. Data can be shared across systems. Master data management still not well governed / managed. No automated updates.  ||  Differentiated: One harmonized, fully connected PLM solution across all entities and corporate divisions. All underlying processes and workflows are aligned to the highest possible degree.  ||  Best In Class: One harmonized PLM solution where key suppliers / co-developers are fully integrated.

items.control_description: 56. To what extent do you use your product lifecycle management solution?
items.remarks: Basic: System to manage drawings, designs, data.  ||  Emerging: As a single source of accurate, complete and timely product-centric data.  ||  Advanced: For methods, data, and workflows for key business decisions. Quality execution of product development process.  ||  Differentiated: As foundation for collaboration, partnering, and outsourcing.  ||  Best In Class: To manage product information from inception to obsolescence.

items.control_description: 57. How sophisticated is your product data management?
items.remarks: Basic: Process and product data in disparate formats and databases within functions. No formal tools in place.  ||  Emerging: Foundational capabilities on product data management. BOM, item attributes, change work flows and process attributes in each function and division.  ||  Advanced: Product data and processes integrated between R&D, quality, supply chain and manufacturing. All managed in a common development database.  ||  Differentiated: Product data and processes integrated across all functions such as marketing, project and portfolio management and sales. All divisions with visibility across enterprise systems.  ||  Best In Class: Globally deployed system. Fully integrated with back-office applications and external partners and external data sources.

items.control_description: 58. Which processes do you manage within your PLM solution?
items.remarks: Basic: Product development related to drawings and designs.  ||  Emerging: In addition, PLM solution is used for concept development, product definition and project resource management.  ||  Advanced: In addition, PLM solution is used for product and service strategy, ideation processes and product release processes.  ||  Differentiated: In addition, PLM solution is used for product assurance, supplier management, process authorization & management.  ||  Best In Class: In addition, PLM solution is used for service and product performance as well as product and service obsolescence.

items.control_description: 59. How integrated is your PLM solution?
items.remarks: Basic: Stand alone system.  ||  Emerging: Full integration with ERP.  ||  Advanced: Full ERP integration, limited integration with SCM, MES, SCM, CRM.  ||  Differentiated: Real time integration with SCM, MES, SCM, CRM.  ||  Best In Class: Real time integration with PLM of key suppliers and co-developers as well as with selected customer / consumer systems.

items.control_description: 60. What is your current approach for innovating new products and internal processes and / or services?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Product improvement and changes are done (incrementally) by a dedicated innovation / R&D department. There is no specified way for other employees to participate in the innovation process.  ||  Emerging: Product improvement and changes are done (incrementally) by a dedicated innovation / R&D department. There is a specified way for other employees to participate in the innovation process.  ||  Advanced: Product improvement and changes are developed by a dedicated cross-functional team, led by the innovation / R&D team. There is a specific process and cross-functional innovation management team in place to develop, vet and implement ideas. Employees are allowed to participate in the innovation process and bring ideas to the table.  ||  Differentiated: Product improvements and changes are developed by a dedicated cross-functional team, led by the innovation / R&D team. There are regular events encouraging employees to contribute ideas. Innovation is not confined to a separate business unit.  ||  Best In Class: There is a dedicated process in place to foster innovation which enables and encourages all employees to raise their ideas. There is a dedicated and independent business unit to explore innovations. Focus lies rather on radical innovations than on incremental innovations. There are regular events to collaborate on innovations with employees from all business units.

items.control_description: 61. To what extent do you use open innovation or crowd sourcing platforms to drive innovation?
items.remarks: Basic: No use of open innovation or crowd sourcing at all.  ||  Emerging: Use of external development capabilities provided by engineering companies and / or platforms for open innovation, e.g. for software solutions/ apps.  ||  Advanced: Open innovation platforms are used to solve development problems, first experiences gained in data exchange for development topics.  ||  Differentiated: Open innovation platforms are used to solve development problems, multiple experiences gained in data exchange for development topics. Crowd sourcing initiated to achieve higher impact by taking advantage of additional innovation capabilities, e.g. hackathons are used to enhance products.  ||  Best In Class: Intensive use of open innovation platforms and crowd sourcing as a fundamental part of the innovation process, e.g. challenges are assigned to development topics. Basically, "any" company can take part and develop value added services for our customers.

items.control_description: 62. How do you involve your partners / suppliers in the product / process development?
items.remarks: Basic: No or only very few partners / suppliers are involved in product development and innovation activities.  ||  Emerging: Partners / suppliers such as co-manufacturers or co-developers are systematically integrated in regular development and innovation activities.  ||  Advanced: Prototypes are tested in an early stage together with partners / suppliers. Feedback is used to enhance the product.  ||  Differentiated: Sales team and planning teams work with partners to co-develop products.  ||  Best In Class: Partners contribute directly to product development (open innovation, co-creation of the products).

items.control_description: 63. How does your digital innovation process look like?
items.remarks: Basic: Digital Innovation happens in silos. Independent teams within our company are developing digital solutions to enhance our existing product portfolio.  ||  Emerging: Digital Innovation happens centrally coordinated covering digital products, new digital services and new digital business models.  ||  Advanced: Digital innovation makes more and more use of joint co-creation processes with partners.  ||  Differentiated: Digital Innovation lab. Digital business model team drives innovation within the company e.g. in innovation workshops.  ||  Best In Class: Open innovation initiative incorporating (potential) customers / consumers, universities, start-ups and further collaboration partners. This is coordinated by a dedicated team within the company.

items.control_description: 64. To what extent are customers / consumers involved?
items.remarks: Basic: No systematic integration of customers / consumers in development and innovation activities.  ||  Emerging: A two-way communcation has been established to get customers / consumers involved, e.g. through a community forum.  ||  Advanced: Customers / consumers are more and more involved, e.g. they can submit ideas through idea contests, which are then evaluated, selected and eventually refined by the company.  ||  Differentiated: Customers / consumers are allowed to submit and rank / select ideas based on their preferences. The company then develops the final product / service based on customer's / consumer's choice, e.g. through idea contests. Customer / consumer involvement has already helped to improve products / services substantially before the final market launch.  ||  Best In Class: Customers / consumers are systematically involved during the entire development and innovation cycle and actively co-design their products, e.g through self-configurators. The company only provides a few restrictions for the design process. These co-creation initiatives have already led to successful new product / service releases.

items.control_description: 65. To what extent do you parallelize your development processes / make use of simultaneous engineering?
items.remarks: Basic: No use of simultaneous engineering. Usually a linear process, where each phase starts after the previous one has been completed.  ||  Emerging: First pilot tests to parallelize selected process in selected development projects. Much effort is still needed to implement simultaneous engineering in those projects.  ||  Advanced: First pilot tests performed. Broader roll-out of simultaneous engineering for additional processes and in a more regular fashion. Managing the communication effort between the departments remains a challenge.  ||  Differentiated: Advanced use of simultaneous engineering for all new development projects. Selected processes are parallelized and the departments involved increasingly collaborate with each other  ||  Best In Class: Make full use of simultaneous engineering. Processes are widely parallelized which has already lead to substantial time savings. Departments start working together at an early stage and communication runs smoothly.

items.control_description: 66. Which stakeholders are typically involved in simultaneous engineering?
items.remarks: Basic: Engineering is solely coordinated by our development engineers. Handovers between departments take place as soon as the previous department has completed its work.  ||  Emerging: Technical departments collaborate with each other at an early stage in the development process. Commercial functions are widely ignored.  ||  Advanced: Commercial departments such as procurement are integrated irregularly and on an on-demand basis.  ||  Differentiated: Internally all technical and commercial departments are constantly involved in the development process.  ||  Best In Class: In addition to internal stakeholder, external stakeholders such as key suppliers, development partners or even customers are involved in the development process from the beginning.

items.control_description: 67. To what extent are all components listed in a central repository maintained by a cross-functional team including purchasing, engineering?
items.remarks: Basic: No central component repository, component selection is based on engineering experience.  ||  Emerging: Very few (almost centralized) component repositories with limited capabilities and still requires engineering experience to a certain degree.  ||  Advanced: Central repository that is only sparsely updated from engineering and offers limited ease of use.  ||  Differentiated: Central repository for components, regularly updated from engineering only and limited ways to identify components, e.g. identification number.  ||  Best In Class: Central repository for components, regularly updated, linked to design best practice, accessible from purchasing / engineering, with various ways to identify components, e.g. identification number, name, supplier, etc.

items.control_description: 68. Which tools and technologies are in place to support simultaneous and agile product development?
items.remarks: Basic: No specific tools or technologies in place.  ||  Emerging: Central data and component repository in place for all participants of the product development process.  ||  Advanced: Kanban boards are used to organize and visualize product development process.  ||  Differentiated: Various methods and software tools like JIRA or Trello are used to support agile and simultanoeus product development process on individual and team level across the organization.  ||  Best In Class: Standardized tools and data repositories are introduced on an organizational level across business units, departments or teams.

items.control_description: 69. How do conduct your stage gate release process?
items.remarks: Basic: Release methodology not distinguished from development methodology.  ||  Emerging: Defined release methodology that guides preparation of code for release and LA / GA distribution.  ||  Advanced: Release governance, milestones, decisions, artifacts and tools are consistently applied to all programs; stakeholders are held accountable to the same milestones and deliverables.  ||  Differentiated: Release governance linked to cross-functional product and release lifecycle process. Digital tools and advanced visualizations ensure an efficient release process.  ||  Best In Class: Collaborative and fully digitized release process. Digitally embedded controls allow for the highest degree of flexibility and a lean release process.

items.control_description: 70. What is your current approach for innovating new products and internal processes and / or services?
items.remarks: Basic: Product improvement and changes are done (incrementally) by Innovation / R&D department. There is no specified way for other employees to participate in the innovation process.  ||  Emerging: Product improvement and changes are done (incrementally) by Innovation / R&D department. There is a specified way for other employees to participate in the innovation process.  ||  Advanced: Product improvement and changes are developed by a dedicated cross-functional team, led by the innovation / R&D team. There is a specific process and cross-functional Innovation management team in place to develop, vet and implement ideas. Employees are allowed to participate in the innovation process and bring ideas to the table.  ||  Differentiated: Product improvement and changes are developed by a dedicated cross-functional team, led by the Innovation / R&D team. There are regular events for employees to bring in ideas. Innovation does not exist in a separate business unit.  ||  Best In Class: There is a dedicated process in-place to foster innovation which enables all employees to raise their ideas. There is a dedicated and independent BU to explore innovations. There are regular events to work on innovations with employees from all business units.

items.control_description: 71. How complete are your requirements documented?
items.remarks: Basic: Requirements are not well documented. Requirements that exist are created by engineering.  ||  Emerging: Key customer feature requirements are documented at a high level by product management. Engineering fills in the blanks to complete the product.  ||  Advanced: Detailed feature / functionality requirements are documented by product management and agreed to by all other functions. Product requirements are all managed with a dedicated software solution e.g. PLM.  ||  Differentiated: All product requirements, including non-functional requirements such as portability, maintainability, and testability are defined and agreed with all product development partners, components of the process are done in sprints. Key requirements are digitally linked to the stage gate process / are integrated as digital controls.  ||  Best In Class: All product requirements, including non-functional requirements such as portability, maintainability, and testability are defined at the beginning of the product development process and continuously refined in sprints to meet the customer / consumer requirements.

items.control_description: 72. How are dependencies between requirements managed?
items.remarks: Basic: Relationships between requirements are neither understood nor documented.  ||  Emerging: Relationships between requirements are understood, but not formally documented.  ||  Advanced: Relationships between requirements are formally documented but not actively managed.  ||  Differentiated: Relationships between requirements are actively managed throughout the development cycle / sprints. Impact on requirement changes can be seamlessly visualized in an easy to understand manner.  ||  Best In Class: Real time transparency of all interdependencies between requirements and actively managed throughout the development sprints. Advanced analytics allow for impact assessment on changes in requirements.

items.control_description: 73. How seamless is the integration of  product development and manufacturing (CAD / CAM-PLM MES etc.?)
items.remarks: Basic: Mainly manual processes - hand over is the 2D drawing.  ||  Emerging: Mainly manual processes - hand over is the 3D model supported by the 2D drawing.  ||  Advanced: CAM modelling is done based on 3D models. Only tolerances and difficult areas need to be manually addressed. 3D CAD models include all PMI (Product and Manufacturing Information). 70% (time reduction) of our NC programming is done automatically by our programs.  ||  Differentiated: 3D CAD models include all PMI (Product and Manufacturing Information). 90% (time reduction) of our NC programming is done automatically by our programs. Suppliers use 3D CAD models that include all PMI (Product and Manufacturing information. Underlying processes,  procedures and controls ensure seamless handover.  ||  Best In Class: Fully integrated. Standard designs are automatically converted (CAD/ CAM). 90% time reduction due to seamless transfer of our CAD data into NC programming data. Minor part changes do not require any manual adaptions. Development engineer receive automated feedback on their design quality based on similar designs.

items.control_description: 74. How do you align different development cycles / gate reviews for software, electronics and mechanical components / formulas, recipes and ingredients?
items.remarks: Basic: No structured alignment between the different component development teams. Components are tested together in validation phase.  ||  Emerging: Differentiation between software and hardware / recipes and ingredients. Software and recipes are much more often reviewed and updated. Gate review process is integrated in design phase.  ||  Advanced: Gate review process between hardware and software / recipes and ingredients is fully integrated and aligned along the complete product development cycle.  ||  Differentiated: Integrated gate reviews with continuous digitized interdependency checks along all product components and partners. Combined with a modular platform concept each product component can be developed nearly independently.  ||  Best In Class: Fully digitized review process with real time progress status update allows to continuously check the development progress and drives alert based review. Modular platform strategy allows autonomous development of components. Next generation components update products in the field almost seamlessly - all modules work on a "plug and play" basis.

items.control_description: 75. How are hardware / software module interfaces managed?
items.remarks: Basic: Interfaces are not clearly defined or managed.  ||  Emerging: Interfaces are loosely defined and managed informally through direct communication between individual developers.  ||  Advanced: Interfaces are formally defined with published specifications. Changes are managed through a lightweight process.  ||  Differentiated: Interfaces are formally defined with published specifications and coordinated across development partners.  ||  Best In Class: Interfaces have clear and testable contracts which enable parallel development of components with minimal dependencies on state, function, data.

items.control_description: 76. How integrated are your processes from sales to manufacturing (Design to Order)?
items.remarks: Basic: Integration done in a non-structured way. No rigit controls/ processes/ procedures in place to ensure end-to-end compliance.  ||  Emerging: Non-standard sales offers are signed off by key stakeholders in the company e.g. by product development. Process is rather manual and often not as responsive as needed.  ||  Advanced: Clear guidelines, procedures and controls in place that provide sales considerable amount of freedom whilst ensuring that offers are checked by the required stakeholders. Digital tracking tools are in place to harmonize the release process.  ||  Differentiated: Fully digitized process integrated in the CRM solution. Dedicated people and supporting resource management facilitate the right and quick support for sales. Advanced database allow to compare similar offers based on key product characteristics and therefore enable sales to make better decisions. Selected products are paraemterized and therefore do not need any feedback loop with production and product development.  ||  Best In Class: Parameterized configuration allows for touchless sales to production processes. AI solutions support sales with their offer development - e.g. similar solution required xx amount of engineering time etc. Digital tools allow for fast end seamless integration of all key stakeholders.

items.control_description: 77. How does your cross-program development process look like?
items.remarks: Basic: Programs planned and executed in isolation – operating in silos.  ||  Emerging: Best effort, ad hoc cross-program collaboration dependent on program manager; limited to aligning schedules across programs; point-to-point delivery and simple handoffs.  ||  Advanced: Tactical cross-program PMO coordinates deliverables and activities across programs during execution.  ||  Differentiated: Tactical cross-program PMO coordinates deliverables and activities across programs during execution. Development partners are fully integrated into the process.  ||  Best In Class: Cross-program management PMO also heavily involved in coordinating planning to avoid resource contention and bottlenecks across the ecosystem of partners.

items.control_description: 78. How mature are you in defining release criteria?
items.remarks: Basic: Release criteria are not defined or applied.  ||  Emerging: Release criteria are defined but often ignored in the face of release pressures.  ||  Advanced: Release criteria are defined and consistently applied; software does not allow shipping of goods unless release criteria are met.  ||  Differentiated: Fully digitized controls embedded in the digitized release processes ensure full compliance and instantly highlight shortfalls.  ||  Best In Class: Advanced analytics and integrated processess e.g. connected measurement results and process data facilitate a fully automated release of products and services. Release criteria can be updated near real time, if customer / consumer requirements have been changed.

items.control_description: 79. How testable are the requirements defined?
items.remarks: Basic: Requirements are high level and vague. Definition is not adequate to develop test cases.  ||  Emerging: Requirements are inconsistent – some are testable, some are not.  ||  Advanced: Requirements are mostly well written and measurable. Test cases can be developed for most of the requirements.  ||  Differentiated: Test cases can be developed for all requirements. Requirements are written in a way that allows testing, digital controls and QA to measure the final product to the original requirement. Testing is partially done in sprints.  ||  Best In Class: Tests are digitally supported and easily updated from sprint to sprint.

items.control_description: 80. To what extent is a traceability matrix used?
items.remarks: Basic: No traceability matrix links test cases to requirements.  ||  Emerging: Traceability matrix is manually created / used for only key requirements.  ||  Advanced: Traceability matrix is manually created / used for all requirements.  ||  Differentiated: A tracing tool is used to automate the creation / usage of a traceability matrix for all requirements.  ||  Best In Class: Fully integrated digital tracing tool automatically creates the requirements traceability matrix and validates it back to the evolving customer / consumer requirements.

items.control_description: 81. How mature is your project and program excellence?
items.remarks: Basic: Key project management practices are missing or very weak.  ||  Emerging: Project management is instituted functionally, without adequate emphasis on planning, control and execution. Functional orientation hinders cross-functional coordination.  ||  Advanced: Project management is cross-functional with well established plans, but is not optimized for proactive planning, cycle-time reduction and issue resolution.  ||  Differentiated: With necessary skill, discipline and alignment in place, project management is fully optimized for critical path management, execution, planning and risk management. Web-enabled product development tools allow real time analysis, management, and decision making, and efficient collaboration, using data that is integrated across the enterprise.  ||  Best In Class: Digital support program management directly linked to resource and pipeline and portfolio management. Latest tools are applied to facilitate cross-functional and global project alignments in real time.

items.control_description: 82. How do you assess your ability to execute digital initiatives efficiently?
items.remarks: Basic: Execution is based on project prioritization. Digital capabilities are limited in-house (lack of skills and experience).  ||  Emerging: Lack of internal capabilities is compensated with the support of suppliers. Manageable amount of digital projects is limited.  ||  Advanced: Well developed capabilities in-house. Manageable amount of digital project and project execution is good.  ||  Differentiated: Key digital innovations are developed in-house (high level of digital capabilities). Good project execution performance.  ||  Best In Class: Digital Initiatives have a high prioritization within the company. Internal digital capabilities paired with external supplier deliver fast and agile results.

items.control_description: 83. How is the hardware / electronics / software module ownership managed?
items.remarks: Basic: Undefined hardware / electronics / software ownership results in uncoordinated changes and increased defect injection rates.  ||  Emerging: Hardware / electronics / software modules are owned by a single developer who understands the code and makes all changes. Developers are reluctant to make touch code they don’t own.  ||  Advanced: Hardware / electronics / software modules are owned by a single primary developer but a second developer is also assigned.  ||  Differentiated: Hardware / electronics / software modules are owned by two or more developers who understand the code well.  ||  Best In Class: Interactive collaborative development tools allows to have dedicated owners and a large base of community contributors to optimize results.

items.control_description: 84. How is the quality assurance secured?
items.remarks: Basic: Quality assurance does not exist as a defined function. QA policy largely informal or undefined.  ||  Emerging: Quality assurance is a distinct role within Engineering and lacks independence. QA policies are defined.  ||  Advanced: Quality Assurance is an independent function (peer to Engineering) and takes a strong position as the overall owner of quality (i.e. stops release if quality goals are unmet).  ||  Differentiated: Quality assurance scope includes architecture, product / release and process.  ||  Best In Class: Quality assurance is an independent function (peer to Engineering) and takes a strong position as the overall owner of quality (i.e. stops release if quality goals are unmet, architecture / module guidelines are not met, etc.).

items.control_description: 85. How does the leadership prepare the organization for changes in digitalization?
items.remarks: Basic: Little to no awareness within the organization.  ||  Emerging: Low level of understanding resulting in over analysis and stalled progress. Senior management do not value Industry 4.0 and have no expertise in the area.  ||  Advanced: Defined methodology and processes that support cultural and organizational change.  ||  Differentiated: Strategic processes in place to assess revise and drive organizational best practices. Sponsorship from senior management who fully understand and master Industry 4.0 initiatives. Specialist experience is also represented at a senior level (in particular at the board level), with all senior management fully knowledgeable and aware of the importance, workings and implication of Industry 4.0.  ||  Best In Class: Leadership led with a high level of understanding and full acceptance across the organization.

items.control_description: 86. How would you rate your digital capabilities of your organization's culture?
items.remarks: Basic: Limited understanding.  ||  Emerging: The organization is making limited attempt to embrace digital. The company values and culture don't support the digital transformation. Lack of clarity on the presence or location of capabilities and absence of or confused responsibilities regarding I 4.0.  ||  Advanced: The organisation has a basic understanding of digital capabilities provided by outside-in perspectives, best practice sharing as well as first internal pilots.  ||  Differentiated: Special units are anchored in the organization with overarching responsibilities for Industrie 4.0 topics (e.g. a cross-functional ‚digital factory‘-unit) and collaborate across partners. The organizational culture is enabled to be digital-centric. The companys' values and culture support the digital transformation in very good manner.  ||  Best In Class: Digital woven into DNA of organization and every employee fully understands and identifies with it. Entire organization is digitally "affine". Communications and relevant, up to date and market leading training is in place and available for all staff who may benefit from it. Organizational culture reflects openness and embraces change and a certain level of risk taking. The company is seen as a digital leader within the ecosystem of partners.

items.control_description: 87. How are competencies and personnel development strategies managed?
items.remarks: Basic: Knowledge and competences of employees are not captured systematically. A balance check with the requirements of the company cannot be done due to lack of the relevant data base. No Qualification and Personnel development plans are in place.  ||  Emerging: Knowledge and competencies of employees is captured within hiring process and complemented with specific training activities. A relevant data base or process to identify the entire knowledge is not existing.  ||  Advanced: A relevant data base or process to identify the entire knowledge is existing. A defined process for capturing and continuously updating of the knowledge of all employees exists and is implemented. A review of this process is done on a demand basis. A balance check with the requirements of the company is also done on a demand basis. Qualification and personnel development plans exist for a share of the employees, but only on the individual level, neglecting the needs of the company.  ||  Differentiated: Constant on-the-job and formal training is performed to improve skills and capabilities over time. Trainings are not only focused on formal skills such as planning algorithms and controlling techniques, but foremost provide a practical day-to-day working knowledge of existing software systems and their potential applications in, e.g. internal KPI benchmarking. A direct link between individual R&D targets, performance and appraisal is established.  ||  Best In Class: Knowledge is mapped vs. future strategic requirements. New resources are hired based on gap analysis. A direct link between individual supply chain targets, performance and appraisal is established. Qualification and personnel development plans exist for all employees, on the individual level, also reflecting the needs of the company. Plans are implemented, monitored and updated continuously.

items.control_description: 88. To what extent is your R&D organization centralized?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: R&D functional leaders reside within business units or regions. The R&D function does not oversee the full product development and product lifecycle flow.  ||  Emerging: R&D functional leaders reside within business units or regions. Product Development happens per region / business unit. Region first to market leads, other follow. The R&D function does oversee the full product development flow, but not the full PLM.  ||  Advanced: Cross-functional decision making exists across the internal R&D organisation, with limited Centers of Excellence. The R&D function oversees the full product development and lifecycle flow and includes other areas such as production, order processing, procurement, supply chain.  ||  Differentiated: The head of R&D participates in corporate strategy as an end-to-end process owner. All units which integrate product development and product lifecycle relevant processes have active stakeholders from the R&D functions. R&D oversees the innovation, product development and product lifecycle flow and include interaction with third parties.  ||  Best In Class: The head of R&D shapes the ecosystem together with sales and supply chain. All three value chains (SCOR, CCOR, PLCOR) are fully linked along the complete value chain from supplier to end-customer.

items.control_description: 89. How does the rewards system look like?
items.remarks: Basic: There is limited, enterprise-wide formal rewards and recognition system. Ad-hoc rewards and recognition linked mainly to each functional groups’ near-term goals.  ||  Emerging: A formal reward system is in place but not based on objective criteria and only loosely tied to individual and business performance.  ||  Advanced: Reward system linked to team and business’ performance.  ||  Differentiated: Rewards system measures contribution of internal and external teams (suppliers and business partners).  ||  Best In Class: Rewards system measures contribution of internal and external teams working in the ecosystem towards the corporate and ecosystem strategy.

items.control_description: 90. To what extend do you ensure that talents are developed and the right resources are hired?
items.remarks: Basic: Recruiting, staffing, and education / training plans are driven by functional department priorities.  ||  Emerging: Specific competencies and roles needed to enable effective supply chain management are documented as part of formal job descriptions.  ||  Advanced: Hiring and development plans explicitly integrate the required competencies for R&D management professionals.  ||  Differentiated: A forward-looking talent roadmap, aligned to strategic capabilities, guides the hiring and development of R&D professionals.  ||  Best In Class: A forward-looking talent roadmap, aligned to strategic capabilities and digitalization capabilities, guides the hiring and development of R&D professionals.

items.control_description: 91. How agile is your culture?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Low competencies and skill level in agile. Undefined roles and responsibilities with no shared ownership or accountability. Lack of individual incentives for agile adoption. Limited use of agile practices and tools for managing user stories, builds and testing.  ||  Emerging: Skill level in Agile varies by project team and functional department. Agile roles and responsibilities are inconsistent. Agile team leverage tools for build and test automation, managing users stories and have flexibility in installing new tools.  ||  Advanced: Consistent level of skill and competency in agile across project teams, well defined roles and responsibilities and shared sense of ownership at the team level. Agile teams are co-located, can support offshore team members to adopt key agile practices and leverage continuous integration of DevOps practices in place.  ||  Differentiated: Department leaders have ownership in and support Agile. Agile tools are adopted across divisions and supported at the enterprise level.  ||  Best In Class: Enterprise performance metrics support and encourage agile collaboration. Adoption of agile practices such as continuous delivery is pervasive in agile projects.

items.control_description: 92. To what extent are R&D responsibilities well-defined and managed?
items.remarks: Basic: A clear definition of responsibilities for roles within the R&D organization does not exist.  ||  Emerging: Responsibilities are partially defined for roles (e.g. only within a business unit).  ||  Advanced: Responsibilities are clearly defined for all roles across the R&D organization.  ||  Differentiated: Responsibilities are clearly defined for all roles across the R&D organization and key external product development partners.  ||  Best In Class: Explicit process owners are assigned and in-place with end-to-end responsibility in the ecosystem to hold all involved parties and partners accountable to their responsibilities.

items.control_description: 93. To what extent is R&D integrated into the supply chain process (degree of collaboration)?
items.remarks: Basic: Ad-hoc meetings to identify requirements and capabilities needed for new products. Escalation meetings during NPI process if errors occur. Sharing of best practices.  ||  Emerging: R&D has the capability to develop based on central and local supply chain specific requirements and capabilities.  ||  Advanced: R&D process is aligned with the supply chain and manufacturing capabilities to develop products optimized for different supply chains (high volume / low mix, low volume / high mix). A dedicated NPI supply chain exits.  ||  Differentiated: R&D process is optimized in terms of business strategy and integration with partners and suppliers.  ||  Best In Class: R&D and sites are optimized in terms of business strategy and integration with partners and suppliers within the ecosystem based on big data holistic calculations.

items.control_description: 94. To what extent are required trainings standardized and communicated across the organization?
items.remarks: Basic: Roles and responsibilities are not clearly assigned to employees. Knowledge is highly dependent on individual employees.  ||  Emerging: Roles are assigned (maybe covered by multiple employees). Trainings are not systematically assigned and conducted (only upon request).  ||  Advanced: All roles are clearly assigned to an employee. Trainings in existing processes & tools are conducted for all roles based on a tailored training plan. Potential changes and additional requirements due to digital disruption are considered in capability profiles.  ||  Differentiated: All roles and trainings are systematically assigned and progress is tracked throughout the individual development of each employee. Potential changes and additional requirements due to digital disruption are considered in capability profiles.  ||  Best In Class: All roles and trainings are systematically assigned and progress is tracked throughout the individual development of each employee. Potential changes and additional requirements due to digital disruption are considered in capability profiles. Training are conducted within the partnering / supplier network.

items.control_description: 95. How are your project teams enabled to be successful?
items.remarks: Basic: Little to no direct communication between business and development teams, no formal agile training.  ||  Emerging: Some involvement between business and development teams. Limited business support for Agile, limited willingness to make the changes needed.  ||  Advanced: Business stakeholders communicate directly and frequently with the development teams. Sufficient agile training.  ||  Differentiated: Organizational structure supports the alignment of agile teams within the organization.  ||  Best In Class: Organizational policies and procedures support agile adoption. Key stakeholders are actively involved in the success of agile. The organization is adaptable and collaborative towards agile and embraces change.

items.control_description: 96. To what extent do you coordinate R&D initiatives across different functions?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: There is an awareness in R&D of initiatives in other functions that impact R&D.  ||  Emerging: R&D initiatives are coordinated with other internal functions (e.g. Marketing, Sales, Manufacturing).  ||  Advanced: R&D initiatives are owned by the head of R&D as a part of broader governance that synchronizes all internal initiatives.  ||  Differentiated: R&D initiatives are syncronized between all internal stakeholders and external development partners.  ||  Best In Class: Initiaties are identified and optimized on a cross- or -multi-enterprise ecosystem level with joint value proposition and realization.

items.control_description: 97. How standardized is the process architecture?
items.remarks: Basic: A R&D “process architecture” (clearly documenting associated activities, data, metrics, applications, etc.) does not exist or exists in an unconsolidated and manually maintained format.  ||  Emerging: A process and systems architecture exists, but is not explicitly linked to the basis of competition as described in the supply chain strategy. Development and maintenance of the supply chain “process architecture” is led mainly by the IT function and viewed as an “IT Issue”.  ||  Advanced: “Process architectures” have been defined, but their content differs by country or region based on history or organizational control, not actual business needs. The process architecture integrates all supply chain sub-processes (Plan, Source, Make, Deliver, Return), data, metrics, and applications.  ||  Differentiated: “Process architecture” content is standardized globally to support geographically dispersed teams, enabling the unified sharing and transfer of work across locations. The process architecture integrates all supply chain sub-processes (Plan, Source, Make, Deliver, Return) and describes the links with other core processes (e.g. Product Development, Marketing, Sales, Finance).  ||  Best In Class: “Process architecture” content is harmonized across the ecosystem.

items.control_description: 98. To what extent is your product development process centralized?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Development pipelines are created across different business units or regions.  ||  Emerging: A single development pipeline, resulting from a regular R&D leadership meeting, is used to drive the product development process.  ||  Advanced: Use of a centralized development pipeline function to generate a single development pipeline.  ||  Differentiated: Central development pipeline integrated with key development partners and selected customers.  ||  Best In Class: A dedicated, centralized development pipeline group owns the development planning process with all key functional areas, partners and customers contributing to the development process.

items.control_description: 99. What are the key drivers of the leadership team?
items.remarks: Basic: The leadership team focuses on functional / technical skills of resources, timely decision making and is action oriented.  ||  Emerging: The leadership team focuses on decision quality, intellectual horsepower and total work systems.  ||  Advanced: The leadership team focuses on business acumen, problem solving and process management.  ||  Differentiated: The leadership team focuses on driving creativity and managing through systems.  ||  Best In Class: The leadership team focuses on strategic agility combined with innovation management, dealing with ambiguity and organizational agility.

items.control_description: 100. How is leadership enabling an organization to collaborate?
items.remarks: Basic: Leadership is directive, based on authority.  ||  Emerging: Collaborative decision making and problem solving.  ||  Advanced: Collaborative negation skills are enabled.  ||  Differentiated: Leaders facilitate and build teams.  ||  Best In Class: Leaders are coaches and full organization is enabled to take leadership on individual level.

items.control_description: 101. To what extend are employees flexible?
items.remarks: Basic: Fixed work time and wage models.  ||  Emerging: Flexible work time agreements.  ||  Advanced: Flexible work time agreements, capacity flexibility increase realized with lease personnel.  ||  Differentiated: Work time agreements possible on basis of order book. Frame contracts for lease personnel.  ||  Best In Class: Work time agreements possible on basis of order book. Frame contracts for Lease personnel, involving supplier and partner network.

items.control_description: 102. How mature is the management commitment to a Industry 4.0 transformation of the business model?
items.remarks: Basic: There is no management commitment.  ||  Emerging: The management has a basic understanding of digital. Value add of digital is not fully bought into. Digital topics are tried out tested in small pilots, if any, mostly investigated internally and outcomes are foreclosed towards external organizations.  ||  Advanced: Management has a clear understanding of required digital capabilities to drive further performance improvements. Management already prepared first steps (e.g. conducted pilots) to enable the organisation to digitize the business and establish new business models.  ||  Differentiated: There is a very high management commitment to a digital backed up by board of directors with a vision and roadmap across partners. Digital innovation is fostered within open platforms designed for cross-industry research (e.g. ‘Smart Factory’ environments, open laboratories for customers).  ||  Best In Class: There is a strategic commitment to continue being a digital leader in the ecosystem and cross-industry. Organisation is driving for the ecosystem success rather than corporate performance.

items.control_description: 103. How does your team structure looks like?
items.remarks: Basic: Limited visibility into team capacity. Team members are not accountable for outcomes.  ||  Emerging: Team members have some accountability for outcomes.  ||  Advanced: Team tracks actual vs. planned releases.  ||  Differentiated: There is visibility into team capacity across departments.  ||  Best In Class: Teams frequently report progress against the plan directly to the senior leadership.

items.control_description: 104. How is the communication structure setup?
items.remarks: Basic: Communication mainly within the department and from manager to next level hierarchies.  ||  Emerging: Project based communication across teams.  ||  Advanced: Stakeholder communication to development teams (department leader directly to employees).  ||  Differentiated: Regular exchange cross hierarchies, not limited to projects.  ||  Best In Class: Direct communication from senior leadership to project teams and reverse.

items.control_description: 105. How mature is your digital change management?
items.remarks: Basic: Little or no change management applied.  ||  Emerging: Some elements of change management are being applied in isolated projects.  ||  Advanced: Comprehensive approach for managing change is being applied in multiple projects.  ||  Differentiated: Organization-wide standards and methods are broadly deployed for managing and leading change. Project management is rigorous but this is balanced with agility to deliver change on time and to budget. Transformation projects take advantage of appropriate technologies and methodologies to deliver change.  ||  Best In Class: Change management competency is evident in all levels of the organization and is part of the organization's intellectual property and competitive edge.

items.control_description: 106. Do you have a Security Development Program (SDP) in place?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: No formal Secure Development Program (SDP) in place.  ||  Emerging: Within digital product development controls are in place to ensure data security including the supply chain of software.  ||  Advanced: SDP is a function of project management with an informal gate review at each stage of the product lifecycle.  ||  Differentiated: SDP is a dedicated program applying standardized risk ratings to help determine and deploy the appropriate level of security.  ||  Best In Class: SDP categorizes the implemented controls based on our organization's risk tolerance profile.

items.control_description: 107. How is Intellectual Property (IP) assessed, evaluated and prioritized?
items.remarks: Basic: No central IP management. IP is stored on paper and IP generation is not centrally documented or tracked.  ||  Emerging: IP is regularly reviewed, IP assessment and validation of patents is performed on an exceptional basis.  ||  Advanced: Central patent portfolio management in place, patents are mapped to products and IP strategy is in place.  ||  Differentiated: Central patent portfolio management across partners, IP licensing on regular basis with partners, automated IP due diligence, major patents are protected and secured.  ||  Best In Class: Ecosystem patent portfolio management, all patents are protected and secured globally.

items.control_description: 108. How high is your budget for innovating new products (as a percentage of Revenue)
items.remarks: Basic: 0-0.5%  ||  Emerging: 0.5 - 1%  ||  Advanced: 1-3%  ||  Differentiated: 3-5%  ||  Best In Class: >5%

items.control_description: 109. New technologies and ways of collaboration have an impact on questions regarding IP, IP share and /or if e.g. a digital asset is replacing the physical product. Have you already involved your legal and IT departement to derive strategies & compliance?
items.remarks: Basic: No strategy developed. Business as usual.  ||  Emerging: First understanding of the changing environment. Need to act identified.  ||  Advanced: Based on competitors and peers review of "how others are doing it" started. Responsibility assigned to start the process.  ||  Differentiated: Set up of a strategy on legal topics around IP, digital assets and new technologies initiated as well as building up of capabilities.  ||  Best In Class: Strategy on legal topics around IP, digital assets and new technologies in place. Relevant responsibilities assigned and capabilities built up.

items.control_description: 1. How is the SC strategy linked to the manufacturing, distribution and collaboration strategy?
items.remarks: Basic: Business objectives and policies defined based on integrated demands, executed manually.  ||  Emerging: Business priorities defined based on horizontal integrated demands. Most important business objectives and policies are automatically taken into consideration. Exceptions managed manually.  ||  Advanced: Business objectives and policies are automatically taken into consideration during detailed daily planning. Exceptions managed manually based on formal process.  ||  Differentiated: Business objectives and policies are automatically taken into consideration. Exceptions managed by the system to ensure compliance to formal process.  ||  Best In Class: Execution of objectives and policies inclusive customer and supplier requirements are managed real time based on changing customer and supplier information.

items.control_description: 2. How effective is your end to end IBP process?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Planning is conducted in silos (e.g. marketing & sales, SC, production, procurement etc.) based on S&OP on a monthly rolling forecast.  ||  Emerging: Company has an internally integrated planning process based on one common or highly integrated software solution. Changes in the plan are automatically / digitally communicated in real time.  ||  Advanced: Cross company, integrated planning of e.g. plant A,B,C etc. Planning considers overall efficiency improvement instead of local (per production facility). Resources and inventory levels are optimized across plants.  ||  Differentiated: System based end-to-end planning and horizontal collaboration using cloud based planning platforms including all key suppliers and if applicable customers.  ||  Best In Class: The end-to-end real-time planning, execution, optimization and supply chainenario planning. Capable to promise: ability to promise and deliver products based on end to end assessment in real time.

items.control_description: 3. How aligned is the business strategy to the financial and operations planning processes?
items.remarks: Basic: Planning strategy not linked to business strategy.  ||  Emerging: Planning strategy manually adapted on a yearly base to the business strategy.  ||  Advanced: Planning strategy regularly adjusted to business strategy.  ||  Differentiated: Planning strategy regularly adjusted to business strategy, regularly exchanged with suppliers, partners and customers.  ||  Best In Class: Planning strategy automatically adjusted to business strategy and priorities include customer, supplier and product requirements.

items.control_description: 17. How do you use demand planning outcomes in your supply and inventory planning process?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Outcomes from demand planning are not used for supply planning on a regular basis.  ||  Emerging: Demand and supply balancing conducted on a regular basis.  ||  Advanced: Dedicated demand driven abnormalities are automatically forwarded to inventory planning process.  ||  Differentiated: Demand and supply balancing integrated into one automatic process.  ||  Best In Class: Demand and supply balancing are near real-time.

items.control_description: 18. How many IT systems are used for the planning process?
items.remarks: Basic: Multiple IT systems and manual transfers of planning data are necessary. Data sharing via manual tools e.g. Excel  ||  Emerging: Multiple IT system and macro enabled data transfers (no manual input needed).  ||  Advanced: Integrated end to end (E2E) planning process are in fully integrated systems (sales, planning departments). Fully automated use of data.  ||  Differentiated: Integrated end to end (E2E) planning process is in fully integrated systems across functions.  ||  Best In Class: There is a single source of truth; an integrated IT system (e.g. sales, planning) uses the same data base.

items.control_description: 19. How well does the planning organization leverage advanced analytics?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Limited capabilities. Data analytics is used to optimize silos e.g. to optimize warehouse footprint, to optimize stock considering all warehouses independently, etc.  ||  Emerging: Big data analytics capabilities is in the process of being established considering the end to end supply chain.  ||  Advanced: Data analytics is used to "filter" and connect data tailored to the specific end-user.  ||  Differentiated: Fully established end to end data analytic capabilities also including e.g. social media data.  ||  Best In Class: Self learning algorithms are in place to optimize all operations across the supply chain providing the planner with needed insights and recommendations.

items.control_description: 21. How are the IBP roles and responsibilities shared & defined?
items.remarks: Basic: Limited engagement outside operations, S&OP process is largely ad hoc, with no formal leadership.  ||  Emerging: S&OP engages functional leaders, but has limited engagement from executive leadership. S&OP process leadership is a part-time responsibility of a functional leader.  ||  Advanced: Executive leadership participates in S&OP, but on an irregular basis. S&OP Process has a clearly defined, full-time leader who coordinates and facilitates process execution.  ||  Differentiated: Executive leadership participates in S&OP on a regular basis and treats it as another process.  ||  Best In Class: The C-Suite prioritizes and leads Executive S&OP (IBP) as a critical business process, linking sales, operations, and finance to achieve competitive advantage. Executive S&OP (IBP) process has a clearly defined, executive-level leader with deep business understanding who actively participates in Executive S&OP (IBP) decisions.

items.control_description: 23. To which extent do you directly link your planning results to execution processes (e.g. replenishment)?
items.remarks: Basic: Planning and execution processes only linked via regular traditional exchange processes (e.g. Excel sheets).  ||  Emerging: Planning and execution only partially linked within certain business processes.  ||  Advanced: Planning and execution partially linked in one region / area.  ||  Differentiated: Planning and execution linked also in collaboration with selected external partners.  ||  Best In Class: Planning and execution real-time linked in collaboration with external partners performed (e.g. production optimized based on real-time planning changes).

items.control_description: 24. What is your meeting cadence?
items.remarks: Basic: Meet on an ad hoc basis.  ||  Emerging: Process and calendar defined but regular compliance is poor.  ||  Advanced: Process and calendar driven by Operations and include limited sales, marketing, and finance engagement.  ||  Differentiated: Formal cadenced and structured meetings culminating in executive SIOP meeting.  ||  Best In Class: Supplemental meetings for contingency / risk planning.

items.control_description: 25. How reactive or proactive is S&OP?
items.remarks: Basic: No formal planning process.  ||  Emerging: Planning is reactive and focuses on tactical issues.  ||  Advanced: SIOP meetings focus on current quarter demand-supply disconnects and near-term financial plans.  ||  Differentiated: Tactical SIOP used effectively to resolve disconnects / identify strategic issues to escalate.  ||  Best In Class: Demonstrated use of demand-driven supply network planning to optimize profitability, customer sat. and cost to serve.

items.control_description: 26. What organizational function leads the S&OP process?
items.remarks: Basic: Supply chain executes to their own plans.  ||  Emerging: Sales / Financial plan drives operations.  ||  Advanced: Consensus achieved based on top down approach and often by a single functional group.  ||  Differentiated: Continuous info sharing across internal functions and some key suppliers and customers.  ||  Best In Class: CXOs participate / endorse process, provide guidance and drive continuous improvement.

items.control_description: 27. How do planning functions share information?
items.remarks: Basic: Informal cross-functional discussions.  ||  Emerging: Communication across functions on a casual basis.  ||  Advanced: Strategic priorities/plans and key partner inputs captured in a business assumptions package.  ||  Differentiated: Continuous info sharing across internal functions and some key suppliers and customers.  ||  Best In Class: Selective customers and suppliers provide current / timely information.

items.control_description: 28. How are various functions coordinating?
items.remarks: Basic: Limited co-ordination between internal functions.  ||  Emerging: Activities between internal functions.  ||  Advanced: Key resources and performance objectives are jointly managed.  ||  Differentiated: Visibility, information sharing and integration of key activities between supply chain partners.  ||  Best In Class: Cohesive planning team that is able to adapt the supply chain to frequent changes in the value chain.

items.control_description: 29. What IT systems are you using to drive the S&OP process?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Extensive use of spreadsheets and data extracts from disparate sources.  ||  Emerging: Minimal integration of independent spreadsheets.  ||  Advanced: Limited, but increasing, use of ERP system for supply chain planning.  ||  Differentiated: Integrated systems in place to provide critical data for effective performance management / reporting in SIOP meetings.  ||  Best In Class: Integrated, end-to-end systems provide holistic views to make proactive, fact-based decisions for optimizing margins and supply chain performance.

items.control_description: 30. How do you capture data needed for the S&OP process?
items.remarks: Basic: Information is developed as required.  ||  Emerging: Poor visibility to end-to-end planning data ; limited useful information.  ||  Advanced: Excel used to aggregate and analyze demand-supply data.  ||  Differentiated: Information flow is synchronized with meetings cadence.  ||  Best In Class: Dynamic dashboards can be instantly modified to enable real-time analysis.

items.control_description: 31. How is information aggregated for reporting?
items.remarks: Basic: Information reporting does not exist.  ||  Emerging: Information reporting is driven by individual user needs.  ||  Advanced: Functional groups have their own data extracts and analytical tools.  ||  Differentiated: Information reporting enables effective strategic decision-making across the organization.  ||  Best In Class: Information and reports are strategic assets that give the business a competitive edge.

items.control_description: 32. How many database systems are used to collect S&OP information?
items.remarks: Basic: Data maintained in multiple systems and is inconsistent or incomplete. Low confidence in data quality.  ||  Emerging: Some common data elements in different systems but still has significant inconsistencies requiring reconciliation.  ||  Advanced: Centralized master data management in place, but not consistently applied across the organization. Increasing trust in data accuracy.  ||  Differentiated: Capabilities in place to drill-down and link across multiple levels of information.  ||  Best In Class: Single source of data serves the entire organization providing high data integrity.

items.control_description: 33. What organizations are involved in the S&OP process?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: No SIOP organization or function; silo culture.  ||  Emerging: Supply chain executes to its own plans.  ||  Advanced: Some sales, marketing and finance engagement.  ||  Differentiated: Supply chain organization is responsible for inventory management and accountability is shared with supply chain, sales and product management.  ||  Best In Class: Key suppliers and customers enlisted as active participants in SIOP process.

items.control_description: 34. What level of involvement does the c-suite have in the S&OP process?
