items.remarks: Basic: Sourcing decisions based on price.  ||  Emerging: Sourcing decisions based on price plus landed costs.  ||  Advanced: Sourcing decisions based on price plus landed costs, plus key operational parameters such as inventory and improvements to quality & delivery.  ||  Differentiated: Sourcing decisions based on total cost of ownership and lifecycle costs across the entire supply chain including product quality and performance and warranty considerations.  ||  Best In Class: Sourcing decisions based on business value and include explicit considerations of risks such as technological obsolescence, service disruption, supplier market power.

items.control_description: 54. How are negotiations conducted?
items.remarks: Basic: No formal RFP process, little understanding of negotiating practices.  ||  Emerging: Basic RFP / RFQ process in place with domestic suppliers; negotiation focused on price and to a lesser degree, quality.  ||  Advanced: Sophisticated RFP / RFQ process in place with global reach; good negotiation practices consistently deployed.  ||  Differentiated: Sourcing teams trained in negotiations and use data driven analysis to prove arguments and drive improvements.  ||  Best In Class: Comprehensive negotiation strategies (including "should cost") planned and executed for all major sourcing events.

items.control_description: 55. How is compliance to the sourcing strategy managed?
items.remarks: Basic: No sourcing strategy and / or limited or no mechanisms to control expenditures.  ||  Emerging: Awareness of sourcing strategy but limited compliance; compliance not tracked.  ||  Advanced: Compliance tracked but residual "problem areas" that do not comply.  ||  Differentiated: Strong compliance to sourcing strategy, with "exceptions" openly debated ad understood.  ||  Best In Class: Compliance with the sourcing strategy across all business units / geographies. Non-Compliance is well understood and has own sourcing strategy.

items.control_description: 56. How is data used to drive sourcing strategies?
items.remarks: Basic: Spend data understood on a "Big Picture" level only (e.g., aggregate spend by site). Minimal understanding of spend by category and associated characteristics.  ||  Emerging: Global category / commodity management in place. Buyers are responsible for categories / commodities and not for vendors. Difficult to get current spend data in a format to drive improvements and decisions.  ||  Advanced: Automated spend cube assessment and updates. Vendor performance analytics in place and used to drive supplier performance discussions and negotiations.  ||  Differentiated: Commodity prices such as copper, steal oil prices etc., exchange rates, are automatically included in the spend analysis. Savings potentials are automatically highlighted. Make v. Buy analytics can be quickly assessed and used to drive decisions.  ||  Best In Class: All strategic sourcing decisions are based on big data analytics which take business priorities into account.

items.control_description: 57. How are sourcing events run and managed?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: No standard process, sourcing events are run ad hoc leveraging prior experience and tend towards including "the usual suspects".  ||  Emerging: Standardized RFx process which is designed to include existing and new suppliers. Use of web-based tools, like share file for posting drawings, in place.  ||  Advanced: Dependent on category, customizable RFx templates which leverage a common standardized quote package. Vendors have to complete RFx online. RFx is `only accepted when mandatory fields are filled out correctly and e.g. delivery conditions are accepted.  ||  Differentiated: Responses are automatically evaluated based on TLC. Top X suppliers are automatically invited for negotiations. Automated rejection of other suppliers.  ||  Best In Class: The RFx process is completely automated and digitized using web-based platforms. Complete visibility as to where any supplier stands in the process.

items.control_description: 1. What are the key dimensions of the manufacturing strategy?
items.remarks: Basic: Manufacturing is very reactive with constantly shifting priorities based on the “hot order” of the day.  ||  Emerging: Manufacturing is demand-driven in a well conceived and structured manner; make-to-order is the predominant manufacturing strategy (if appropriate).  ||  Advanced: Demand-pull mechanisms are pervasive and control the majority of manufacturing activities. Digitalization seen as enabler to drive further efficiencies and effectiveness.  ||  Differentiated: Demand-pull mechanisms and mass customization techniques allow almost all products to be configured or produced to order with competitive customer lead times, digitalization established as enabler for further efficiencies and effectiveness  ||  Best In Class: Demand-pull mechanisms and mass customization techniques allow almost all products to be configured or produced-to-order with competitive customer lead times, digitalization is a core discipline.

items.control_description: 2. How integrated / collaborative are key departments to support manufacturing operations?
items.remarks: Basic: Limited alignment between support functions and manufacturing strategy, functional boundaries are high and collaboration is low, limited alignment of R&R.  ||  Emerging: Support functions are well aligned with the manufacturing strategy within the site, for key processes and interfaces R&R are locally defined.  ||  Advanced: Engineering and manufacturing collaborate from the initial phases of the product life cycle, enabling Design for Manufacturing (DFM), R&R are defined for all processes.  ||  Differentiated: Engineering and manufacturing collaborate globally from the initial phases of the product life cycle, enabling design for manufacturing (DFM), R&R and workflows are standardized where possible on a global level.  ||  Best In Class: All departments (including partners) collaborate from the initial phases of the product life cycle, enabling Design for Manufacturing (DFM) and product enhancement lifecycle planning, R&R and workflows are standardized where possible on a global level and regularly adapted.

items.control_description: 3. How flexible is your machine park?
items.remarks: Basic: Machine park is designed to produce high volume batches of only a small number of product variants.  ||  Emerging: Majority of machine park is design to produce high volume batches of only a small number of product variants, some machines allow quick change of dies and provides a high level of flexibility.  ||  Advanced: Machine park allows quick changeovers and provides a high level of flexibility whilst keeping the productivity on a high level.  ||  Differentiated: Machine park allows quick changeovers and provides a high level of flexibility whilst keeping the productivity on a high level; effort to actively drive standardization at lower levels forward to allow for more flexibility.  ||  Best In Class: Standardization on a low level makes production highly flexible. Machines can easily be adapted to new requirements and product personalization (best case: batch size 1). Plug and produce.

items.control_description: 4. What kind of business priorities do you have in place?
items.remarks: Basic: Business objectives and policies defined based on integrated demands and executed manually. In general, delivery dates (MTO) or stock levels (MTS) are the standard priorities.  ||  Emerging: Business priorities defined based on horizontal integrated demands. Most important business objectives and policies are automatically taken into consideration Exceptions managed manually.  ||  Advanced: Business objectives and policies are automatically taken into consideration during detailed daily planning. Exceptions managed manually based on formal process.  ||  Differentiated: Business objectives and policies are automatically taken into consideration. Exceptions managed by the system to ensure compliance to formal process.  ||  Best In Class: Execution of objectives and policies is managed real time based on changing customer and supplier information.

items.control_description: 5. How integrated is your demand, supply and production planning?
items.remarks: Basic: Supply constraints and sales and demand orders are separate process that are not integrated or require significant manual consolidation to produce production schedules.  ||  Emerging: Supply constraints and sales and demand orders are managed through enterprise systems but not fully integrated. Some manual interventions are required to produce final production schedules.  ||  Advanced: Supply constraints and sales and demand orders systems are fully integrated and automatically reflect changes and updates in each system. Production schedules are produced automatically based on defined business rules and logic.  ||  Differentiated: Supply constraints and sales and demand orders systems are fully integrated and automatically reflect changes and updates in each system. Production schedules are produced automatically based on defined business rules and logic and real-time material and asset availability information.  ||  Best In Class: Supply constraints and sales and demand order systems are automatically updated to reflect customer and production changes, with a live feed updating the production schedule and providing optimized production options based on real-time changes in labor, material, flow and machine.

items.control_description: 6. To which degree are supply chain partners integrated in the planning and scheduling process?
items.remarks: Basic: Plan is shared with suppliers in form of purchase orders.  ||  Emerging: Plan is shared with suppliers in form of purchase orders with accurate lead times, vendor managed inventory exists for c-parts.  ||  Advanced: Suppliers have visibility into current production plan and blanked purchase orders exist in line with volumes that are required to satisfy production plan.  ||  Differentiated: Suppliers have near real time, full, digital visibility into scheduling systems, actual performance against schedule. Changes to the plan are flagged and the responsible stakeholders are alerted to take action.  ||  Best In Class: Suppliers have near real time, full, digital visibility into scheduling systems, actual performance against schedule and any changes to the plan flow through in real time in both directions; suppliers own and manage inventory until it is pulled into production.

items.control_description: 7. How integrated is the factory within the factory network?
items.remarks: Basic: Downstream factory has little to no visibility into demand from feeder factory. Mainly ad hoc communications between factory schedulers / planners.  ||  Emerging: Downstream factory and feeder factory have regular (at least bi-weekly) planning to discuss forecast and potential ad hoc requests.  ||  Advanced: Network factories can access the MRP and planning systems of the other plants in addition to planning meetings.  ||  Differentiated: Network factories have realtime, full, digital visibility into scheduling systems, actual performance against schedule, but each plant optimizes their own operations. Network-wide optimization based on ad hoc intervention.  ||  Best In Class: Network factories have real-time, full, digital visibility into scheduling systems, actual performance against schedule, any changes to the plan flow through in real-time in both directions and use of sensor data which allows for network wide optimization.

items.control_description: 8. How mature is the new product introduction process integration?
items.remarks: Basic: NPI teams manually create production documentation and share it with planning teams via meetings and / or email. There is limited consideration for supply and demand planning constraints.  ||  Emerging: Some NPI teams use the same production systems as planners to design for manufacture and align forecasts with supply and demand planning constraints.  ||  Advanced: NPI teams across the business use the same production systems as planners to design for manufacture and sales forecasts are fully integrated with supply and demand planning.  ||  Differentiated: NPI teams across the business use the same production systems as planners to design for manufacture and sales forecasts are fully integrated with supply and demand planning. Design software is partially integrated with production, supply, and demand systems.  ||  Best In Class: Design software is fully integrated within production, supply and demand systems. RPA is used to complete common design and planning tasks.

items.control_description: 9. How do you create production schedules and release them?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Production schedules are created based on “tribal” knowledge using basic business tools such as excel and distributed to the shop floor manually.  ||  Emerging: Production schedules are semi-automated, created using purpose built tools and software. Supervisors can access the schedule from terminals on the shop floor.  ||  Advanced: Schedules are automatically produced at planning horizon, using tools and software that are to a large degree integrated with all necessary business systems. Operators have access to the schedule at work cells.  ||  Differentiated: Schedules are automatically produced at planning horizon, using tools and software that are integrated with all necessary business systems. Operators have access to the schedule at work cells and can provide feedback on the schedule.  ||  Best In Class: Schedules are automatically calculated and produced in real-time, updating the schedule and production routing to optimize the production flow.

items.control_description: 10. How do you perform your detailed planning / master scheduling / dispatching?
items.remarks: Basic: Offline planning with basic constraints integrated manually from ERP system including special operating modes (cleaning, startup). E.g. Excel based planning solutions.  ||  Emerging: Offline planning with basic constraints integrated manually from ERP system including special operating modes (cleaning, startup). MES systems with links to automation systems and ERP. Manual feedback into ERP system still needed.  ||  Advanced: Advanced online planning and production dispatch tools vertically integrated across plant systems.  ||  Differentiated: Planning and dispatch tools integrated across business processes and plant network E2E. Compatibility cross plant assured.  ||  Best In Class: Planning tool steers production dispatch in real time across company fully integrated planning tool.

items.control_description: 11. How regularly do you update your detailed planning / dispatching?
items.remarks: Basic: On a daily / weekly basis.  ||  Emerging: Updated manually in near time (within the day) as orders arrive.  ||  Advanced: Updated automatically mostly in real time as orders arrive electronically and plant and material status (e.g. shortages, unplanned stops) changes.  ||  Differentiated: Updated automatically mostly in real time as logistics status changes. Reschedules across company network / external capacity automatically in near time.  ||  Best In Class: Real time update production across plant, suppliers and customers.

items.control_description: 12. How is the production flow, routing and simulation setup?
items.remarks: Basic: Production sequencing is based on customer priority with the routing determined by “tribal” knowledge of the product, machines and operators. Production flow is modelled in traditional systems such as excel.  ||  Emerging: Planners use basic planning tools to manually create sequencing options and production flow. Data is based on historic data and standards held within business systems but there is no direct feed.  ||  Advanced: Planning tools and business systems are fully integrated with planning tools calculating and producing an optimized production flow. Customer orders can be split, tracked and scheduled in batches.  ||  Differentiated: Planning tools and business systems are fully integrated with planning tools calculating and producing an optimized production flow. Customer orders can be split, tracked and scheduled as a “lot size of 1”.  ||  Best In Class: There is a comprehensive virtual factory delivering a real-time state of the factory to predict, optimize and visualize the production process. The simulation provides information on the health of production resources as well as optimized system.

items.control_description: 13. Are you able to predict impacts of changes within your manufacturing schedule / planning system?
items.remarks: Basic: Evaluations on high level (not on the dispatching level) is possible. Accuracy is limited / dependent on how often the all systems are updated. E.g. simulation possible overnight since dependent on ERP update. Manual work needed to assess impacts on detailed planning.  ||  Emerging: Manual, time consuming work needed to assess impacts on detailed planning. Data are accurate and can be trusted (e.g. Inventory levels are up to date in near time).  ||  Advanced: Simulation down to the dispatching level can be done. Most critical vertical information about e.g. resources, asset configuration, quality, inventory levels, maintenance schedules are automatically included.  ||  Differentiated: Horizontal information e.g. delivery status of parts, capacity of key suppliers, etc. are included in the simulation.  ||  Best In Class: Planning tool enables "what if" simulations in real time. All horizontal and vertical data are precise. Scenarios are displayed and evaluated.

items.control_description: 14. How is manufacturing executed and how visible is your production?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Production is monitored by operators and escalated to supervisors / management for decisions. Data is updated within systems retrospectively.  ||  Emerging: All critical assets and resources are connected and monitored providing current state notifications, alerts and data visualization to inform shop floor staff / management to take action.  ||  Advanced: All major assets and resources are connected and integrated with business and operational control systems. Analytic platforms identify and suggest predictive and preventative actions before events. Full visibility to internal business partners in real time.  ||  Differentiated: Shop floor assets, resources and business systems are fully connected. Analytic platforms identify and suggest predictive and preventative actions before events. Analytics self service for shop floor staff is in place that allows data exploration to optimize process. Full visibility to internal business partners in real time. Visibility to select partners and suppliers  ||  Best In Class: Shop floor assets, resources and business systems are fully connected and integrated. Analytical platforms drive full automation of the shop floor using real-time data to update systems and optimize production controls. Visibility to major partners and suppliers.

items.control_description: 15. How mature is your manufacturing execution system?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Excel and analogue based manufacturing planning.  ||  Emerging: MES is in place with detailed manufacturing scheduling, optimization focusing on asset utilization.  ||  Advanced: MES is in place with detailed manufacturing scheduling, asset utilization and planning capabilities and quality management capabilities across key machines.  ||  Differentiated: MES is in place with detailed manufacturing scheduling, asset utilization and planning capabilities and quality optimization capabilities across all machines.  ||  Best In Class: MES with self-optimizing planning and quality management capabilities, incl. What-if analysis and simulations.

items.control_description: 16. How is equipment changed over / cleaned?
items.remarks: Basic: The employees are aware of the short notice procurement procedures for materials and personnel, work and test procedures and parameters.  ||  Emerging: Necessary components, materials, tools are procured and commissioned at short notice; work and test procedures and parameters are partially defined.  ||  Advanced: Necessary components, materials, tools are procured and commissioned at short notice; responsible staff are identified, work and test procedures and parameters are defined.  ||  Differentiated: Requirements lists are complete and available, necessary components, materials, tools are procured and commissioned at short notice, responsible staff are long-term blocked, work and test procedures and parameters are defined.  ||  Best In Class: Requirements lists are complete and digital available, necessary components, materials, tools are procured and commissioned at short notice, responsible staff are long-term blocked, work and test procedures and parameters are defined.

items.control_description: 17. How do you manage your tools?
items.remarks: Basic: Information around tool part number and location are available in a database.  ||  Emerging: Tools are managed within a database with location, maintenance schedule and “life span” manually logged.  ||  Advanced: All critical tools have their location and are digitally tracked. The tools “life span” is calculated and tracked based on predefined parameters i.e. number of operations or time. Notifications are sent to shop floor staff when tool is nearing end of life or fault is identified. Tool database manually updated.  ||  Differentiated: All major tools are digitally monitored and tracked using analytics to predict maintenance and failures. Tools are integrated with machines and resources to track tool performance based on changing characteristics due to tool ware. Databases and other systems, including planning tools are automatically updated.  ||  Best In Class: All tools are fully connected and data integrated with business systems. Tools are automatically loaded and analytical platforms track real-time tool condition altering processes as necessary to optimize production and prevent failures. Databases and other systems, including planning tools are automatically updated.

items.control_description: 18. What is the level of production automation?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Basic process control and automation systems, low level of sensors and automated actuators with manual loading of product and programs into a machine.  ||  Emerging: Automation system with extended functionality - all sensors relevant for planning electronically available. Use of visual scheduling and DNC to push.  ||  Advanced: Fully automated dispatching e.g. - data/ programs are directly send to the machines based on production schedules. Self-loading from previous work center, and self-recognition of product.  ||  Differentiated: Fully autonomous production line of multiple work centers and quality control.  ||  Best In Class: Totally automated and autonomous production based on online models including big data optimization. Lights out factory.

items.control_description: 19. How are your capabilities to track and trace of parts in your factory?
items.remarks: Basic: Operators manually insert completion of major process steps. Status and position of parts are visible but accuracy in terms of time dependent on the operator; within production: the approximate start time is given and the end time since we have a series productions process.  ||  Emerging: Status of parts / batches (standard parts excluded) is automatically reported though the use of scanners (handhelds) after the completion of key manufacturing steps.  ||  Advanced: Status of parts / batches is automatically reported. E.g. RFID chips enable a touchless status update. after the completion of key manufacturing steps.  ||  Differentiated: Integrated tracking system enables seamless tracking of parts. E.g. part passed automatic scanner, machine is now running at that point of the program, therefore, this production step will be finished in 30 minutes….  ||  Best In Class: Across functions (sales, production, connection to online platform for customers to check status) exact status of parts can be tracked. Within manufacturing: knowing that product x is No. y in queue of machine z. Predictions about real time throughput time are computed automatically.

items.control_description: 20. How do you perform your inventory and material management?
items.remarks: Basic: Material inventory is based on historical safety stock levels and quarterly confirmed orders. Inventory is manually entered and updated within the MRP system. Materials at work-cells are replenished manually from the warehouse via a Kanban system or visual indicator. WIP is stored at the workcell and manually moved by operators or material handlers once an order is complete.  ||  Emerging: Inventory calculations are based on weekly demand characteristics, dependency between different products, supplier constraints and account for seasonality. MRP is linked to critical suppliers enabling vendor managed inventory.  ||  Advanced: Inventory calculations are based on weekly demand characteristics, dependency between different products, supplier constraints and account for seasonality. MRP is linked to critical suppliers enabling vendor managed inventory. Critical material levels at work-cells are monitored using sensors with alerts sent to material handlers. For critical workcells WIP is transported via AGV or conveyor and automatically loaded into and from machines.  ||  Differentiated: MRP or material management system is fully integrated with internal business and operational systems and external customer systems. Inventory calculations are made in real-time with WIP inventory information is fed back to schedule (e.g. via RFID tags). Visibility into supply chain and ability to monitor and respond to disruptions Inventory management is highly automated and dynamically optimized in realtime.  ||  Best In Class: MRP or material management system is fully integrated with internal business and operational systems and external customer systems. Inventory calculations are made in real-time with WIP inventory information is fed back to schedule (e.g. via RFID tags). Visibility into supply chain and ability to monitor and respond to disruptions Inventory management is highly automated and dynamically optimized in real-time.

items.control_description: 21. How do you perform quality management?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Product quality is managed via manual checks and measurements. Batch and sample audits are routinely conducted by quality specialists. Data is manually updated within traditional business systems. Operators conduct root cause analysis to rectify quality issues.  ||  Emerging: Product quality is managed via manual checks and measurements. Batch and sample audits are routinely conducted by quality specialists. Testing equipment automatically transmits data to quality management system. Operators conduct root cause analysis to rectify quality issues.  ||  Advanced: All critical work cells are equipped with sensors and non conforming parts are rerouted to dedicated correction areas, where they are either reworked or scraped. Quality data is tracked by product type and machine and automatically updated within business systems.  ||  Differentiated: All major work cells are equipped with sensors tracking and managing non conforming products. Machine and resource characteristics are digitally monitored and correlated for impact on quality. Analytics such as SPC are used to control processes and identify root causes.  ||  Best In Class: All work cells are equipped with sensors to track and manage non conforming products and automatically alter machine and resource processes in real-time. Analytics are used to predict quality issues before they occur and take corrective action and update systems and databases in real-time.

items.control_description: 22. How is manufacturing linked to design and engineering?
items.remarks: Basic: Limited communication between engineering and manufacturing. Manufacturing is only involved when new product is ramping-up for production.  ||  Emerging: Engineering and manufacturing discuss new product introductions on a regular basis and review planned BOM and manufacturing process.  ||  Advanced: Well established Design for Manufacturability (DfX) program and systemic collaboration between engineering and manufacturing.  ||  Differentiated: End to end digital thread. DfX program is supplemented with fully integrated PLM, CAD / CAM, CNC / DNC and Tool Management systems. Central management of engineering specifications and machine programs.  ||  Best In Class: End to end digital thread. DfX program is supplemented with fully integrated PLM, CAD / CAM, CNC / DNC and tool management systems. Central management of engineering specifications and machine programs. Closed loop feedback from the shop floor, workflow and enterprise wide knowledge management of best practices.

items.control_description: 23. Is the production balanced for NPI launches?
items.remarks: Basic: No accounting is carried out for the individual pilot test.  ||  Emerging: A general calculation of times, quantities and general factors is carried out.  ||  Advanced: Defined pilot accounting is carried out with consideration given to the specific resources used (personnel, materials, fuel etc.).  ||  Differentiated: Defined pilot accounting is carried out, with consideration given to the specific resources used (personnel, materials, fuel etc.). The documentation is recorded in a knowledge management system.  ||  Best In Class: Defined pilot accounting is carried out, with consideration given to the specific resources used (personnel, materials, fuel etc.). The documentation is part of the digital twin along the PLM.

items.control_description: 24. How are recipe / work plans handled for the NPI?
items.remarks: Basic: Recipes are clearly defined for all products, working plans are standardized and not dependent on the product.  ||  Emerging: Recipes and working plans are clearly defined for all products.  ||  Advanced: Recipes and working plans are clearly defined for all products and are updated following every production run.  ||  Differentiated: Recipes and working plans are clearly defined for all products and are updated following every production run. A management system supports problematic situations, digital twins are not yet used.  ||  Best In Class: Recipes and working plans are clearly defined for all products and are updated following every production run. A management system supports problematic situations. Recipe and work plans are included in the digital twin.

items.control_description: 25. How do you manage your workforce?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: The shop floor flexes staffing levels using a paper based system dependent on forecasted demand. Overtime is monitored based on paper schedules and shift patterns. Staff are trained in designated processes and operations with limited cross training.  ||  Emerging: The shop floor flexes staffing levels using a paper based system dependent on forecasted demand. Overtime is monitored based on paper schedules and shift patterns. Staff are cross-trained and are able to work in different work cells and perform a variety of tasks.  ||  Advanced: The shop floor flexes staffing levels based on forecasted demand with employee shift data accurately captured electronically. Overtime is monitored and flagged through electronic prompts based on planned schedules and shift patterns. Staff training records are held electronically with some staff cross trained on critical processes and operations.  ||  Differentiated: Demand is integrated with staff scheduling platforms and training records, prepopulating shift patterns and providing options for staffing qualified staff for specific operations. Staff manually log into systems and workstations. Most staff are multiskilled and can be flexed across production operations. Training certification is monitored with supervisors alerted and staff automatically assigned retraining.  ||  Best In Class: Production scheduling is fully integrated with employee systems, automatically allocating and optimizing staffing. All staff are multi-skilled and can be flexed across production operations. Staff location is monitored in real-time, and use bio-metrics to log into work cells. Training certification is monitored with supervisors alerted and staff automatically assigned re-training.

items.control_description: 26. How are assets and machines managed?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Assets and machines are maintained based on a planned schedule or in a reactive manner when issues occur. The schedule is logged within a maintenance database and any findings or work conducted updated manually after work is complete. Machine availability is shared manually with planners.  ||  Emerging: Machine health characteristics for critical assets and machines are digitally monitored and tracked. Current state notifications, alerts and data visualization inform shop floor staff / management to take action. Maintenance database is updated manually.  ||  Advanced: Machine health characteristics for critical assets and machines are digitally monitored and tracked. Current state notifications, alerts and data visualization inform shop floor staff / management to take action. Alerts are sent to planners with planned and unplanned downtime duration and reason codes.  ||  Differentiated: All major assets and machines are monitored and tracked using analytics to predict maintenance requirements and wider impacts such as OTD, product quality etc. alerts and data visualization inform shop floor staff / management to take action well before issues arise. Databases and other systems, including planning tools are automatically updated.  ||  Best In Class: All assets and machines are fully connected and integrated with business systems. Analytical platforms drive performance and control of the assets and machines automatically, optimizing changeovers in real time.

items.control_description: 27. Which factors influence your maintenance routines / schedules?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Maintenance orders and execution is integrated in ERP. Maintenance management system defines maintenance routines such as shut down and preventive maintenance. Planning considers availability and qualification of personnel manually.  ||  Emerging: Maintenance orders and execution integrated in ERP. Visualization of maintenance orders on smart devices / dashboards for the dedicated maintenance personnel.  ||  Advanced: Automated definition of plant maintenance schedules based on broad set of plant inputs e.g. manufacturing schedules. Automatically considering availability of equipment and qualified personnel. Optimization in parallel with detailed planning and scheduling of production.  ||  Differentiated: Automated definition of maintenance tasks and schedules across site. Aligned with manufacturing schedules / product demands. External service providers are automatically aligned with production scheduling.  ||  Best In Class: Centralized unit steers maintenance. Algorithms defining most efficient maintenance tasks and schedules (including preventive maintenance time horizon) considering the whole vertical and horizontal value chains in near time.

items.control_description: 28. What kind of maintenance types do you have in place?
items.remarks: Basic: Preventive and corrective maintenance is defined.  ||  Emerging: Predefined actions for monitored abnormalities for selected equipment.  ||  Advanced: Predictive maintenance for critical equipment in place using big data analytics and / or interpretable statistical methods. Primary focus is on predicting failure of a specific machine.  ||  Differentiated: Predictive maintenance for broad set of equipment in place. Multiple machines globally being monitored and adding to the data set and predicts failure across multiple failure points.  ||  Best In Class: Prescriptive maintenance. Leverage advanced software, statistical methods and AI to for pattern identification to identify root cause issues and to recommend precise and timely counter actions.

items.control_description: 29. Through which tools do you support your maintenance crew?
items.remarks: Basic: Maintenance crews have access to historic maintenance records and work instructions through desktop based maintenance systems.  ||  Emerging: Remote experts in place, Maintenance can call / communicate with other team members as well as suppliers.  ||  Advanced: All maintenance instructions and tasks are steered by a central, integrated system. Maintenance crew uses smart devices to receive and confirm tasks.  ||  Differentiated: All instruction, maintenance history, performance parameter of equipment can be retrieved via smart device. Smart device recognizes unique ID of the equipment.  ||  Best In Class: Maintenance crew uses digital work instructions displayed through smart glasses. All information are displayed based on employee’s needs, all tasks are digitally recorded.

items.control_description: 30. How do you visualize and manage performance?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Rudimentary, manual tracking of select performance KPIs with a predefined cadence.  ||  Emerging: Rudimentary, manual tracking of select performance KPIs with a predefined cadence. Historic KPIs are displayed on digital dashboards that are visible on the shop floor.  ||  Advanced: Semi-automated data collection and report creation at a predefined cadence for a comprehensive KPI set; visualization in excel-like sheets.  ||  Differentiated: Automated data collection and report creation on demand and at a predefined cadence for a balanced scorecard. Visualization in an interactive dashboard that allows to dynamically view the data; visual and email alerts inform staff about deviations from targeted performance level  ||  Best In Class: Real-time, automated tracking of a balanced KPI scorecard; displayed in interactive “dashboards that matter” which are tailored to the user needs and behavior and allow to drill down into the information and issues. Automated alerts immediately inform staff about deviations from targeted performance levels and recommend counter actions.

items.control_description: 31. How do you manage your data and secure your operations?
items.remarks: Basic: There is no policy or process in place to guide data collection and management for OT related data; The IT / OT cyber security strategy is purely based on security through obscurity.  ||  Emerging: Data is being collected in an opportunistic way, the influx of data causing information overload and an inability to derive actionable insights. Unclear strategy for managing and storing the data. A multitude of systems and data sources exist that are not harmonized or integrated. Cyber security is considered primarily an IT topic with limited involvement of the plants.  ||  Advanced: Select data is being collected. Strategy for managing and storing the data is in place. A multitude of systems and data sources exist that are not harmonized or integrated. Cyber security is driven by IT topic with some plant level awareness and initiatives.  ||  Differentiated: Data is only collected if a need for this data has been identified; data management is done in line with IT policies. Data can reside in multiple systems that are not integrated but data quality and accuracy is regularly tested. IT / OT cyber security risks have been identified and understood and are being addressed through the development of a governance framework. IT and OT teams collaborate but operating model is not yet fully defined.  ||  Best In Class: A clearly formulated strategy is in place and executed on how, where (edge, cloud on prem, cloud) and which data should be collected and managed. Regularly tested IT / OT cyber security governance frameworks are in place with clearly defined roles and responsibilities across the organization. The data governance process ensures there is single source of truth and systems are integrated.

items.control_description: 32. How and where do you store your asset data?
items.remarks: Basic: Incidences are stored locally, no company wide data collection.  ||  Emerging: Incidents automatically stored in common, company / plant database.  ||  Advanced: Data historian exists in the plant that stores production and asset data.  ||  Differentiated: Data is stored in a plant wide cloud.  ||  Best In Class: Relevant data is stored in one common cloud. Data is automatically linked with production data. Certain analysis happens right at the edge and is not send to the cloud.

items.control_description: 33. How integrated are your systems?
items.remarks: Basic: No integration of field devices / sensors, SCADA / DCS / SFAC, MES and ERP transferring selected information.  ||  Emerging: Limited connectivity of field devices, SCADA / DCS / SFAC, MES and ERP systems.  ||  Advanced: Full data integration across functions.  ||  Differentiated: Cross company integration of field devices, SCADA / DCS / SFAC, MES and ERP Data integration across plant.  ||  Best In Class: Complete, real time vertical and horizontal data integration as basis for optimizations.

items.control_description: 34. To which degree does your factory embrace lean?
items.remarks: Basic: Lean training exists but limited implementation of lean on the shop floor.  ||  Emerging: Leadership alignment towards a lean culture but limited employee involvement due to focus on day to day operations.  ||  Advanced: Leadership alignment and employee involvement through a problem solving approach.  ||  Differentiated: Leadership alignment and employee involvement in problem solving; employees trained in process improvement techniques such as 7QC, 5S, lean overview.  ||  Best In Class: Leadership alignment and employees actively involved in problem solving. Employee skills are mapped and have enterprise level visibility. Plans in place for upskilling teams and training them for new responsibilities in a smart factory setup across all skill levels and age groups.

items.control_description: 35. To which degree is work standardized?
items.remarks: Basic: Work is not standardized across the operation.  ||  Emerging: Work is standardized and all necessary information is displayed at the work stations.  ||  Advanced: Work instructions are standardized and dynamically updated as per the takt time. This provides ability for operators to work on additional stations or let the shift in charge know when extra manpower is required.  ||  Differentiated: Paperless stations with operators equipped with electronic devices that provide the necessary input to the operator to perform the job.  ||  Best In Class: Paperless stations with operators equipped with electronic devices that are dynamically updated when there is a change required or with voice of downstream stakeholder (internal as well as external). The device hosts the necessary information about the station such as quality standards, work instructions, parts required as per the SKU for quick reference.

items.control_description: 36. Through which visualizations do you support planning and production execution?
items.remarks: Basic: Paper based display and documentation of information on e.g. Gemba boards. E.g. used for daily stand up meetings, and knowledge, information transfer.  ||  Emerging: Advanced user interfaces e.g. tablets and monitors are implemented to e.g. guide operators through critical process steps. Digital recording of issues and performed tasks.  ||  Advanced: Advanced user interfaces e.g. tablets are implemented to increase efficiency of all production personnel. Failure proof solutions are integrated for critical process steps.  ||  Differentiated: Provided information are tailored to the specific needs / skills / education level of the dedicated workforce. Visualizations have been created with a human-centric design and are meaningful to the end user. Confirmation of tasks via smart device.  ||  Best In Class: Provided information are tailored to the specific needs / skills / education level of the dedicated workforce. Visualizations have been created with a human-centric design and are meaningful to the end user. Confirmation of tasks via smart device. Innovative means of displaying information, such as augmented reality, are used where appropriate.

items.control_description: 37. How are plant layouts designed?
items.remarks: Basic: New work cells / machines are added without evaluating man / material movement optimization.  ||  Emerging: New work cells / machines are added without evaluating man/material movement optimization most of the times.  ||  Advanced: New work cell / machine is added considering optimal man / material movement most of the times.  ||  Differentiated: New work cell / machine is added after running a simulation to identify optimal man / material movement.  ||  Best In Class: Plant layout follows a modular design of flexible and mobile machines that can flexibly reorganize themselves based on the requirements of a specific order.

items.control_description: 38. To which degree are your machines connected?
items.remarks: Basic: The work cells / machines either don't communicate or only partially communicate with each other.  ||  Emerging: The work cells / machines are connected across the shop floor and share information one way.  ||  Advanced: The work cells / machines are connected across the shop floor and share information two-ways.  ||  Differentiated: The work cells / machines are connected across the enterprise, share information two ways.  ||  Best In Class: A full digital twin of the production exists that reflects data flows in real-time.

items.control_description: 39. Which role does health, safety, and the environment play in your operation?
items.remarks: Basic: The factory is pursuing OHSAS 18001 and ISO 45001 certifications. Unsafe situations are managed ad hoc when they occur and limited documentation exists.  ||  Emerging: The factory is OHSAS 18001 and ISO 45001 certified, with preventative approach to hazards and safety is delegated to the safety department. Unsafe situations are manually captured on a daily basis within paper based logs.  ||  Advanced: Some safety critical machines and equipment are monitored via sensors to identify when safety tolerances are breached and warn operators via an alert. Data is being captured but not analyzed for predictive maintenance and correlations. Safety logs are captured within a central business system.  ||  Differentiated: All safety critical machines and equipment are monitored via sensors. Failure nodes are known and edge / cloud based analytics are used to predict failures and warn staff well before failure occur. Data from sensors across sites are collated centrally and correlated to determine new failure nodes and insights. Safety logs automatically update CAPA documents and assign actions to safety teams and staff.  ||  Best In Class: The safety portal is visible enterprise wide and all unsafe situations are captured and logged in by the employees. The solution implemented for these situations are detailed and the best practices are shared across teams. Safety is ingrained in the work culture of the company. Additionally, the facilities are equipped with smart lighting and condition monitoring.

items.control_description: 1. How is your network strategy developed?
items.remarks: Basic: No clear strategy for network design.  ||  Emerging: Network design was created in isolation from corporate strategy.  ||  Advanced: Network strategy is developed in conjunction to corporate strategy.  ||  Differentiated: Collaborative effort established in designing and maintaining the network with cross-functional teams.  ||  Best In Class: Network design strategy is fully integrated to the corporate strategy and requirements support planning term forecasts and requirements.

items.control_description: 2. What is the scope and key dimensions of the network distribution strategy?
items.remarks: Basic: Based on historic patterns of the network to conduct center of gravity level analysis. Little considerations for future products or demand.  ||  Emerging: Product flows are based on historical patterns and include logical product and location aggregations. Limited modeling of all supply chain costs and service requirements (e.g. facility costs, transportation costs, inventory or service levels)..  ||  Advanced: Product flows include historical and future demand. Model incorporates and optimizes costs across transportation and warehousing (e.g. operational costs, facility costs, transportation costs). Model is constructed in a repeatable manner.  ||  Differentiated: Product flows include historical and future demand. Model incorporates and optimizes costs and service levels across transportation, warehousing, and inventory (and production / capacity if applicable). User is able to calculate end to end product and / or customers costs. Model is constructed in a repeatable manner using standard templates and contains standard output visualizations.  ||  Best In Class: Product flows include historical and future demand. Model incorporates and optimizes costs and service levels across transportation, warehousing, inventory, and planning (and production / capacity if applicable). User is able to calculate end -to-end product and/or customers costs. Model is updated and refreshed using standard reports from a client's data warehouse and contains standard output visualizations.

items.control_description: 3. How are risks considered in your network design philosophy?
items.remarks: Basic: Risk is not considered.  ||  Emerging: Risk is considered in modeling scenarios.  ||  Advanced: Risk is tested as a sensitivity when running down-selected scenarios.  ||  Differentiated: Risk is tested as a sensitivity when running downselected scenarios. Model outputs are saved in case of an event.  ||  Best In Class: Risk assessment embedded into corporate planning and strategic process. Scenarios and sensitivities are modeled to determine potential impact of risk event to supply chain and customers. Outputs are leveraged for operations contingency planning.

items.control_description: 4. How are tax implications incorporated in your network design analysis?
items.remarks: Basic: Tax implications are not considered.  ||  Emerging: Tax implications are evaluated after analysis has been conducted.  ||  Advanced: Tax stakeholders are consulted throughout the network modeling process to identify impact to duties / tariffs / taxes.  ||  Differentiated: Collaboration between tax and network modeling team to create a tax efficient supply chain.  ||  Best In Class: Collaboration between tax and supply chain teams at the strategy development and network design stages to optimize tax structure within supply chain.

items.control_description: 5. What are the triggers for design modification?
items.remarks: Basic: No regular evaluations. Ad hoc as supply chain runs into issues or receives cost pressures.  ||  Emerging: Evaluations when significant market shifts occur (e.g. when some geographic market grows or shrinks significantly).  ||  Advanced: Regular network analysis occurs on a regular cadence every 2-3 years to evaluate changes in the business and market.  ||  Differentiated: Network and asset optimization processes seen as an area of continuous improvement and occurs on an annual or quarterly basis. Future scenarios are considered from strategic perspective and the impact of making changes vs. maintaining status quo.  ||  Best In Class: Network modeling and analysis skilled position as part of supply chain organization. Continuous review of network performance and regular evaluation of scenarios using modeling tools are integrated in business planning.

items.control_description: 6. What cost information is utilized for network design?
items.remarks: Basic: Only aggregate costs of the network are known. There is no allocation by business unit, customer, or product.  ||  Emerging: Costs are known for warehouses, transportation, and production but there are no allocations made for business units, customer, or product.  ||  Advanced: Costs are known for warehouses, transport and production and there are allocations made for business units, customer, or product.  ||  Differentiated: Costs are known and trends are predicted for warehouses, transport, and production. Allocations are made for BUs, customer, or product.  ||  Best In Class: Costs are know at the line item level and can be aggregated for reporting. Forecasted costs are incorporated into and vetted via corporate level budgeting cadence.

items.control_description: 7. What methods and tools do you leverage for network design?
items.remarks: Basic: Use of spreadsheet based modeling tools with no simulation capabilities.  ||  Emerging: Use of spreadsheet based modeling tools with limited simulation capabilities.  ||  Advanced: Use of network modeling and simulation tools. Limited scenario modeling capabilities and output visualizations.  ||  Differentiated: Use of sophisticated network modeling and simulation tools. Optimization technology with robust solvers, graphical modeling and scenario management capabilities.  ||  Best In Class: Use of sophisticated network modeling and simulation tools. Optimization technology with robust solvers, graphical modeling and scenario management capabilities. Optimization tools integrated seamlessly with operational and tactical / execution tools.

items.control_description: 8. What level of data access is available for network design?
items.remarks: Basic: Product flow data is not available.  ||  Emerging: Product flow data has to be compiled from many sources.  ||  Advanced: Product flow data can be pulled from one or a few sources.  ||  Differentiated: Real time product flow data is available via single source (e.g. ERP / Data Warehouse).  ||  Best In Class: Real time product flow data from single source is easily imported into visualization software (e.g. Tableau) for regular analysis.

items.control_description: 12. What is your transportation systems strategy?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Ad hoc, short-term, paper-driven transportation requirements planning approach.  ||  Emerging: Stand-alone transportation management system.  ||  Advanced: Transportation management system integrated with logistics partners / carriers.  ||  Differentiated: Transportation management system integrated across supply chain partners.  ||  Best In Class: Supply chain control tower leveraged for supply chain planning and visibility. Emerging technologies such as IoT and blockchain used for real-time visibility and chain of command assurance..

items.control_description: 92. What is your transportation systems strategy?
items.remarks: Basic: No electronic tools for transportation management.  ||  Emerging: Offline excel - or access - based tools to assist in routing.  ||  Advanced: TMS in place to manage moves for a particular mode or within a region.  ||  Differentiated: TMS integrated to manage planning and execution of moves across all modes and locations.  ||  Best In Class: Best-in-class TMS utilized across the network for transportation planning and execution, continuous improvement using modeling functionality and procurement. TMS seen as conduit to harmonize processes, optimize and automate the transportation function.

items.control_description: 93. What is your technology strategy?
items.remarks: Basic: No defined vision or strategy for transportation IT systems. Home-grown and small applications used on an ad hoc basis.  ||  Emerging: Individual business units make TMS software selections without coordination.  ||  Advanced: TMS is implemented across the businesses based on need and strategic vision for transportation.  ||  Differentiated: Logistics IT strategy is integrated into corporate IT and business vision strategy.  ||  Best In Class: Logistics IT strategy and business vision include long-term strategic goals and investment targets.

items.control_description: 94. Is your TMS integrated internally?
items.remarks: Basic: TMS is managed as stand-alone system separate from ERP / MRP systems.  ||  Emerging: Links between ERP / MRP and TMS are unidirectional periodic transfers.  ||  Advanced: ERP / MRP system and TMS are continuously linked.  ||  Differentiated: ERP / MRP system and TMS are continuously linked and used to provide information back and forth.  ||  Best In Class: ERP / MRP system is using TMS in dynamic decision-making process.

items.control_description: 95. Is your TMS external integrated?
items.remarks: Basic: Carrier information is gathered manually, then entered by logistics team. Communication is done over traditional channels (phone, e-mail, etc.).  ||  Emerging: Carriers log into portal to enter shipments and updates to the TMS manually.  ||  Advanced: TMS system is linked via periodic transfers to carrier management system for updates.  ||  Differentiated: TMS system is linked into carrier TMS systems for real-time interface via EDI.  ||  Best In Class: Communication is completely digitized as it's done mainly over integrated systems and platforms (API). Visibility vendors provide real-time updates across carriers and modes.

items.control_description: 96. How is technology optimized?
items.remarks: Basic: Manual “optimization” based on basic rules and individual knowledge.  ||  Emerging: Optimal load building and container plans for regularly scheduled moves.  ||  Advanced: Load plans built and updated based on real-time data including window pickup times in facility.  ||  Differentiated: Dynamic realtime mode selection and load building to maximize utilization.  ||  Best In Class: Sophisticated algorithms embedded in technology's optimization engine to make optimized decisions on loads, routes, carriers, and modes.

items.control_description: 97. How automated are your transportation processes?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Limited or no automated data gathering and distribution.  ||  Emerging: Bar-code scanners or similar technology used to ensure proper data capture.  ||  Advanced: Automated systems capture the data but not integrated into the TMS.  ||  Differentiated: Automated systems captured data and periodically "push" data to TMS.  ||  Best In Class: Data captured and disseminated to the TMS in near real-time.

items.control_description: 98. How are metrics and performance data recorded, maintained and accessed?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Limited definition of logistics metrics. Each metric is stored and retrieved independently.  ||  Emerging: Standard reports are documented and maintained across the business.  ||  Advanced: All key metrics are compiled into a key performance report that is published regularly.  ||  Differentiated: All metrics are published and available on integrated common supply chain dashboards. Metrics coordinated with supplier management organization.  ||  Best In Class: All metrics and published and available via in real-time dashboards that include drill down metrics in TMS / BI intelligence system.

items.control_description: 99. How are rate requests and communicated and serviced?
items.remarks: Basic: Requests monitored manually through ad-hoc processes.  ||  Emerging: Lead time of request to required time monitored by mode.  ||  Advanced: Short-lead-time and premium requests tracked relative to their impact on rates and throughput.  ||  Differentiated: Impact of late requests documented and tied back to identify the cost of late requests.  ||  Best In Class: Requests are submitted and tracked through a integrated webportal. Costs and operational impact are systematically recorded based on calculations and user input.

items.control_description: 100. How is carrier performance managed?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Carriers provide tracking information that is aggregated and monitored.  ||  Emerging: Only aggregated high-level carrier performance monitored.  ||  Advanced: Carriers tracked for load-by-load performance on arrival, delivery, and documentation.  ||  Differentiated: Data gathered from the carrier performance used in evaluation and award scenarios.  ||  Best In Class: Regularly scheduled business reviews completed with core carriers to review results and drive improvement.

items.control_description: 101. How is ship and delivery on-time performance tracked and measured?
items.remarks: Basic: On-time delivery only tracked as a “pass / fail” characteristic.  ||  Emerging: On-time performance metrics are expanded to include early, on-time and late delivery.  ||  Advanced: Window times for pickup and delivery are coordinated and tracked with carriers.  ||  Differentiated: Delivery performance at both pickup and delivery for early, ontime, late with defined reason codes are tracked via TMS.  ||  Best In Class: Delivery performance at both pickup and delivery for early, on-time, late with defined reason codes and root-cause identification processes in place.

items.control_description: 102. How are new developed and generated?
items.remarks: Basic: Data must be manually downloaded and aggregated into reports.  ||  Emerging: The system compiles the data and calculates, but reports must still be downloaded for review.  ||  Advanced: Online system in place for reviewing the current state and KPIs.  ||  Differentiated: New reports and scoreboard criteria can be easily developed and deployed by users through online tools.  ||  Best In Class: BI reporting technology is in place and supported by in-house "super users". Company wide, site and function specific reporting views are configurable by user. Requests for new reports are submitted and managed through an online portal.

items.control_description: 103. What level of granularity to BU / site specific data is provided by your reporting system?
items.remarks: Basic: Metrics are tracked at aggregated corporate level.  ||  Emerging: Metrics tracked at individual business unit or P&L level.  ||  Advanced: Metrics can be tracked down to specific location.  ||  Differentiated: Metrics can be assigned to a specific activity within a business unit or plant.  ||  Best In Class: Drill down metrics are available and can be easily filtered and segmented to a specific BU / location.

items.control_description: 104. What level of granularity to part # / customer specific data is provided by your reporting system?
items.remarks: Basic: Metrics can be tracked generally at aggregated number of parts.  ||  Emerging: Metrics can be tracked to a particular part family.  ||  Advanced: Metrics can be tracked down to specific part number level.  ||  Differentiated: Metrics can be tracked down to specific part number and customer level.  ||  Best In Class: Dashboard exists with drill down BI reporting enable filtering to a specific part # / customer / shipping location.

items.control_description: 105. How does your company manage environmental / sustainability metrics?
items.remarks: Basic: No sustainability impact data collected (e.g., greenhouse gas, energy, water, waste). No sustainability communications.  ||  Emerging: Sustainability impact data estimated at an aggregate level using standard emission factors and public impact data. Sustainability achievements communicated through annual corporate sustainability report.  ||  Advanced: Sustainability impact data estimated at aggregate level. Performance targets set, tracked, and reported. Company responds to sustainability rankings (e.g., Carbon Disclosure Project).  ||  Differentiated: Impact tool used that estimates sustainability impact down to the trip level and used to drive continuous improvement. Performance targets set, tracked, reported and used in transit decisions / solutions. Sustainability achievements communicated through annual corporate sustainability report. Company strives to become or is a leader on sustainability rankings. Carbon footprint tool made available to the public.  ||  Best In Class: Logistics route efficiency, mode selection, MPG performance and dwell time are tracked through IoT sensors and the impact to fuel consumption, CO2 emissions and added costs are automatically calculated. Sustainability goals and achievements are centrally defined and communicated across the organization. KPIs and BI performance dashboards are in place to drive sustainability and track performance.

items.control_description: 106. How is reporting utilized to make broader supply chain decisions, determine financial impact and drive operational improvements?
items.remarks: Basic: Logistics alignment is purely a happenstance in organizational hierarchy. Logistics and supply chain given low level of importance in org. Weak linkages between logistics and cost, customer service.  ||  Emerging: Logistics function aligned within operations for budget reasons. Modest recognition of logistics within supply chain structure. Logistics budgetary performance is first; cust. service is secondary.  ||  Advanced: Alignment decision driven by relative importance of cost or service. Enterprise initiating holistic supply chain strategy view. Logistics performance assessed on multiple business aligned factors.  ||  Differentiated: Logistics alignment is driven by business strategy objectives. Logistics / supply chain importance driven by objective strategy factors.  ||  Best In Class: Logistics service delivery and performance are viewed as a differentiator for the company. Logistics reporting integrated into enterprise decision making.

items.control_description: 107. How does the logistics org manage processes,requirements and overall quality?
items.remarks: Basic: No defined quality process. Limited understanding of customer requirements. No carrier involvement in quality process. Rudimentary customer segmentation. Internal and external customer distinctions are not clear.  ||  Emerging: Limited TQM applications. Basic understanding of customer requirements with many gaps. Limited carrier participation in quality process. Some confusion over who are the customers. Customer segmentation is cursory but available.  ||  Advanced: Initiating TQM certification. Well understood customer requirements with periodic update. Carriers participation in quality process when requested. Customers are more defined and segmented. Customer requirements are generally well understood.  ||  Differentiated: Complete understanding of customer requirement continuously updated. Carriers involved in quality process. All customers are clearly defined and segmented with documented requirements.  ||  Best In Class: ISO 9000 certified quality process. Complete understanding of customer requirement continuously updated. Full proactive carrier involvement in quality process. All customers are clearly defined and segmented. Requirements are well known and understood to a high degree.

items.control_description: 108. What is the level of experience and skillset of the logistics function?
items.remarks: Basic: Local functions staffed by temps and low-skill hourly workers. Management has little expertise in logistics. No formal training program exists.  ||  Emerging: Position staffed by hourly workers experienced in distribution. Management has experience in distribution but split w/ other duty. Training extends to execution of basic transactional tasks.  ||  Advanced: Positions staffed by salaried, experienced, and knowledgeable personnel. Management has logistics span of control. Logistics specific training exists.]  ||  Differentiated: Positions staffed by salaried, experienced, and knowledgeable personnel. Management has logistics span with some supply chain focus. Training is broad and robust.  ||  Best In Class: Key positions are top performers cross trained in supply chain tasks. Logistics managed as integrated portion of entire supply chain. Comprehensive cross-functional training programs in place.

items.control_description: 58. How are strategic provider relationships managed?
items.remarks: Basic: Has large carrier base with no defined carrier management strategy.  ||  Emerging: Each business unit / division manages its own carrier base—fragmented and decentralized.  ||  Advanced: Has an enterprise core-carrier program with multiyear focus on mutual benefits.  ||  Differentiated: Consistently achieves benefits of shared vision, goals, and mission with carriers.  ||  Best In Class: Collaborates with key set of vendors to implement cost reduction programs / continuous improvement projects.

items.control_description: 59. What is your process for carrier requirements development?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Minimal standards of operation (insurance, licensing, and certification).  ||  Emerging: Measurement of carrier capabilities (size, financial stability, safety rating); particular requirements are specific to individual locations and not universally articulated.  ||  Advanced: Carrier requirements include defined service-level requirements, driver qualifications, etc.  ||  Differentiated: A single set of detailed carrier requirements is available and consistently communicated to each vendor; performance against these requirements is monitored and improved on a regular basis.  ||  Best In Class: Comprehensive carrier operational excellence exists (program for continuous improvement and issue resolution).

items.control_description: 60. What processes are in place to manage provider performance?
items.remarks: Basic: Has limited carrier performance information.  ||  Emerging: Has some performance information—but fragmented, incomplete, and not user-friendly.  ||  Advanced: Performance metrics and dashboard used to monitor each carrier and compare to expectations.  ||  Differentiated: Standardized metrics used to compare all carriers. Meetings regularly scheduled to review performance and discuss improvement initiatives.  ||  Best In Class: Automated compliance and performance reports are transmitted to carriers on a scheduled cadence or available through portal. Carriers view their performance and proactively raise issues..

items.control_description: 61. How is provider communication managed?
items.remarks: Basic: Has informal lines of communication for day-to-day operation.  ||  Emerging: Has established lines of communication within transportation management.  ||  Advanced: Has formal lines at all carrier management levels. Has automated information exchange.  ||  Differentiated: Has formal communication with other supply chain constituents in addition to carrier management. Has integrated automated information exchange among all supply chain constituents. Certain communications (freight tendering, invoice audit and payment) are automated and do not require intervention.  ||  Best In Class: Formalized milestones are established triggering automated communications to relevant internal and provider parties as they occur. Information input from external parties is integrated into centralized repositories as a unique field displaying text updates or standard code input. System logic is able to interpret these inputs and automate communication to relevant internal stakeholders..

items.control_description: 62. How are disputes resolved?
items.remarks: Basic: Has no formal programs to resolve disputes.  ||  Emerging: Defined dispute resolution process.  ||  Advanced: Published and agreed-to escalation procedure provided to carrier.  ||  Differentiated: Resolution and corrective action tracking integrated into overall carrier performance management and supplier quality.  ||  Best In Class: Resolution and corrective action tracking are automated through TMS / other transportation system.

items.control_description: 63. How are 3PL providers managed?
items.remarks: Basic: No formal 3PL management processes.  ||  Emerging: 3PLs managed through regular purchasing supplier management process.  ||  Advanced: Logistics organization actively monitors and tracks 3PL performance with a standard scorecard across are partners. Reviews completed on an as-needed basis.  ||  Differentiated: Specific management plan developed for each 3PL balancing frequency of meetings with level of partnership. Business reviews discussing performance, opportunities, etc. are held at regularly scheduled intervals (monthly, quarterly).  ||  Best In Class: Specific management plan developed for each 3PL balancing frequency of meetings with level of partnership. Business reviews discussing performance, opportunities, etc. are held at regularly scheduled intervals (monthly, quarterly).

items.control_description: 64. How do you collaborate with your suppliers?
items.remarks: Basic: No policies or procedures for new vendor set up or communication.  ||  Emerging: Informal vendor profiles. Limited supplier collaboration (some emails, not integrated into other systems) and occurs primarily when problems occur.  ||  Advanced: Has collaboration program established with well-defined strategy on target vendors. Vendor participates in core carrier conferences.  ||  Differentiated: Integrated vendor profile and communications with SC constituents. Vendors are integrated with logistics systems (TMS, WMS) to allow for more rapid communication and decision making.  ||  Best In Class: Vendor profiles and communications are standardized and integrated with TMS and other supply chain technology to automate data exchange. RPA or web based portals are in place to submit and intake data for new suppliers or suppliers unable to integrate directly with platforms due to a lack of IT sophistication. Vendors manage and update rates within TMS in a timely manner.

items.control_description: 65. How are rate structures established and managed?
items.remarks: Basic: Many carrier tariffs exist. Spot quotes are often used. Complicated, numerous rate structures exist for the same mode.  ||  Emerging: Most rates are contracted. Few rate structures exist for each mode..  ||  Advanced: Standardized rate structure exists by mode. Multiple fuel and accessorial programs exist by mode.  ||  Differentiated: Standardized rate structure exists by mode. Standard fuel and accessorial programs exist by mode.  ||  Best In Class: Multi-model rates are captured at the segment level and separate accessorials from base line haul.

items.control_description: 66. How are rates managed and accessed?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: No rate access—calls carriers for rates.  ||  Emerging: Corporate and various local shipping locations maintain individual rate files.  ||  Advanced: Standardized corporate-level reporting available for some modes.  ||  Differentiated: Standardized corporate level reporting available of 80%+ of all rates.  ||  Best In Class: Ad hoc reporting features available across the enterprise for 95%+ of all rates. Rates are regularly maintained and updated in TMS.

items.control_description: 67. How are rates tracked?
items.remarks: Basic: No rate retrieval functions.  ||  Emerging: Paper records or on individual PCs.  ||  Advanced: Automated rate retrieval database on company shared network.  ||  Differentiated: All modal rates / contracts integrated to TMS and payment system.  ||  Best In Class: Rate adjustments are recorded in TMS system and historical rates are saved for trend analysis.

items.control_description: 68. How are rates published?
items.remarks: Basic: Buyers or sales reps have no rate knowledge.  ||  Emerging: Manual lookup of rates by clerk. Current rate matrices distributed to users.  ||  Advanced: Rate publication system in place  ||  Differentiated: Users and carriers access same rate database.  ||  Best In Class: TMS and integrated technologies maintain a centralized repository of rates. Carrier access to the database can be limited to selected fields for security and privacy requirements.

items.control_description: 69. How are rates modified?
items.remarks: Basic: Negotiates rate changes with carriers without “testing” the market.  ||  Emerging: Negotiates rate changes with carriers after “testing” the marketplace.  ||  Advanced: Clearly defined rate escalation policies with carriers. Rates benchmarked prior to increase acceptance.  ||  Differentiated: Target rates identified for existing and new traffic lanes.  ||  Best In Class: TMS is able to compare "target" rate to existing rates under contract, bids from recent sourcing event and benchmark called from linked freight intelligence 3rd party. Analysis summary is presented to compare increase and make a decision to accept or reject.

items.control_description: 70. How are rates benchmarked?
items.remarks: Basic: No benchmarking activities.  ||  Emerging: Limited use of benchmarking - conducted on new lane or when receiving an increase. Source of benchmarks come from incumbents.  ||  Advanced: Benchmarking activities conducted prior to sourcing events and ad hoc to determine savings opportunities.  ||  Differentiated: Benchmarking activities completed on a regular basis using a freight intelligence resource. Analysis is manually conducted.  ||  Best In Class: TMS performs an quarterly or annual benchmarking assessment of transportation rates on top lanes against BIC, average, and high benchmarks. Savings opportunities are identified by the system and reported to management in a standardized report.

items.control_description: 71. How are your fuel surcharge peg determined?
items.remarks: Basic: Set by carrier / 3PL without tie to government published pricing. No clear update cycle.  ||  Emerging: Set by carrier / 3PL without tie to government published pricing. Updated monthly or less.  ||  Advanced: Set as global rate pegged to government publication. Updated annually. Different fuel program for different carriers.  ||  Differentiated: Set as regional / Intraregional zoned rates pegged to government/industry publication. Updated quarterly. All carriers on a single, standardized fuel program.  ||  Best In Class: Intra-regional zoning rates pegged to government publication. Updated monthly or less.

items.control_description: 72. How is fuel surcharge pricing structured?
items.remarks: Basic: Percent of linehaul cost. No differentiation by mode.  ||  Emerging: Percent of linehaul cost. Amount differentiated by mode.  ||  Advanced: Structure differentiated by mode and determined through a peg to a government publication. (TL - cost/mi.; LTL percent of linehaul cost).  ||  Differentiated: Based upon actual spend ($ / mile), truly a passthru charge  ||  Best In Class: IoT sensors and GPS data enable fuel surcharges to be based upon actual fuel consumption and fuel rate within truck route. Fleet management sensors capture idle time and fuel consumption to provide a real cost for each shipment.

items.control_description: 73. How are stop charges managed?
items.remarks: Basic: Included intransit cost (not itemized).  ||  Emerging: Single fixed fee per stop.  ||  Advanced: Increasing fixed fee with increasing stops. Amount of charge may vary by carrier.  ||  Differentiated: Increasing fixed fee with increasing stops that is actively negotiated. Stop charge amount standard across all carriers as part of a standardized accessorial program.  ||  Best In Class: IoT sensors and GPS data enable stop charges to be based on actual time and mileage impact for each stop incurred during a shipment.

items.control_description: 74. What is your LTL weight break strategy?
