items.remarks: Basic: Few dictated by carrier or 3PL.  ||  Emerging: Few set by shipper without break-point reasoning. No concept of deficit weight applied.  ||  Advanced: Set by shipper optimized against historic shipping patterns and conducting analysis using actual freight class. Use of deficit weighting is manually applied.  ||  Differentiated: Set by shipper optimized against historic shipping patterns and conducting analysis using actual freight class. Deficit weighting benefits are systematically calculated and the selection of the optimal weight break is automatic.  ||  Best In Class: Set by shipper optimized against historic shipping patterns and aligned with customer order size incentives.

items.control_description: 75. How are accessorials standardized and reviewed?
items.remarks: Basic: No accessorial management program—pay all or pay none.  ||  Emerging: Standardized accessorial schedules defined and used with all carriers.  ||  Advanced: Integrated accessorial charge schedule into the rate negotiation process.  ||  Differentiated: Logistics systems automatically audit freight invoices to monitor adherence to standardized accessorial program.  ||  Best In Class: Scheduled reviews and adjustments of accessorial schedule based on market.

items.control_description: 76. How are accessorial charges managed?
items.remarks: Basic: No monitoring and documentation of charges.  ||  Emerging: Fragmented internal groups responsible for managing charges.  ||  Advanced: Cross-functional responsibility for managing charges.  ||  Differentiated: Defined team with carrier involvement with responsibility for managing charges.  ||  Best In Class: A defined team utilizes standardized and automated reports to coordinate with carriers and manage accessorials.

items.control_description: 77. How are accessorial backcharges managed?
items.remarks: Basic: No accountability of expenses.  ||  Emerging: Assessorials are charged back on general business P&L basis.  ||  Advanced: Assessorials are charged back to specific driving departments or business units.  ||  Differentiated: Charges and targets shared with leadership on ongoing basis.  ||  Best In Class: Analysis is conducted to determine root causes and opportunities to reduce charges (e.g. work with customer to reduce detention).

items.control_description: 78. What is your strategy for accessorial reduction?
items.remarks: Basic: Little or no focus on accessorial management or reduction.  ||  Emerging: Establishes accessorial authorization rules.  ||  Advanced: Measures accessorials and identifies ways to reduce costs.  ||  Differentiated: Harmonized accessorial schedule defined in carrier contracts with robust documentation verification process.  ||  Best In Class: Visibility data / IoT sensors leveraged to validate and determine accessorials (e.g. wait time, demurrage, etc.).

items.control_description: 79. What is your carrier management program?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: No coordination of carrier usage. Carriers are selected on ad hoc basis.  ||  Emerging: Preferred carriers in place for all regular lanes.  ||  Advanced: Corporate carrier group developed to cover all shipments on all lanes including provisional coverage for undefined lanes.  ||  Differentiated: Corporate carrier group is regularly reviewed and revised based on performance and business needs.  ||  Best In Class: Corporate carrier group is updated annually with at least 10-20% turnover in carrier base demonstrated to ensure continuous improvement in performance.

items.control_description: 80. How is carrier allocation / awards managed to each carrier?
items.remarks: Basic: Awards made to carriers in the routing guide based purely on cost.  ||  Emerging: Within the preferred carrier population, certain carriers are awarded priority status on certain lanes or zones.  ||  Advanced: Award allocations defined to balance cost, service, and carrier development goals. Typical 50% / 30% / 20% or 60% / 40% of volume on a lane.  ||  Differentiated: Allocation awards are regularly evaluated and adjusted as needed to manage capacity. Reviews happen at least once/year.  ||  Best In Class: Allocation awards managed and tracked by TMS system.

items.control_description: 81. How is preferred carrier usage tracked and managed?
items.remarks: Basic: All regularly scheduled shipments being carried by a corporate carrier.  ||  Emerging: Awards allocation utilized to determine carrier awards for particular moves.  ||  Advanced: >85% of all moves including premium and spot with corporate carriers according to award allocation.  ||  Differentiated: >95% of all moves including premium and spot with corporate carriers according to award allocation.  ||  Best In Class: 100% utilization of core carriers at negotiated rates according to award allocation.

items.control_description: 82. How often are you shipping without using an already contracted rate?
items.remarks: Basic: Some contracts in place for some modes but gaps in coverage  ||  Emerging: Contracted rates in place for corporate carriers on most moves.  ||  Advanced: All transactions are verified against contracts to ensure compliance rate agreements.  ||  Differentiated: Documentation exists for moves not shipped using contracted rates (exception based only).  ||  Best In Class: Shipment authorizations are provided to FPP to validate transactions were authorized prior to payment.

items.control_description: 83. How are transportation and customs compliance documents managed and maintained?
items.remarks: Basic: All compliance documentation completed on an ad hoc basis.  ||  Emerging: Standardized documents and requirements tracked.  ||  Advanced: Compliance performance managed and centrally stored on internal company shared drive.  ||  Differentiated: Compliance performance managed through integrated electronic TMS / fleet system / GTM.  ||  Best In Class: Fully certified and audited compliance performance with self-certification of all paperwork.

items.control_description: 84. What compliance processes / programs exist?
items.remarks: Basic: No compliance programs since no guidelines or rules exist.  ||  Emerging: Compliance is monitored periodically using manually developed reports.  ||  Advanced: Compliance is monitored regularly using automated reports.  ||  Differentiated: Compliance is monitored regularly using automated reports. Exceptions are regularly reviewed with management and resolution actions taken.  ||  Best In Class: Compliance is monitored continuously providing online exception reporting.

items.control_description: 85. How is the logistics organization structured within the broader ops organization?
items.remarks: Basic: Logistics organization managed as a sub-department to material planning or purchasing.  ||  Emerging: Organization viewed as subordinate business unit to other indirect areas (sourcing, material management, IT).  ||  Advanced: Logistics is a stakeholder within a manufacturing organization.  ||  Differentiated: Logistics is a core stakeholder within an integrated supply planning organization.  ||  Best In Class: Logistics is a core stakeholder across the entire supply chain organization.

items.control_description: 86. How is logistics integrated into broader business decision making?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Transportation decision-making process is completed independent of rest of business.  ||  Emerging: Input is sought from logistics organization on an ad hoc basis.  ||  Advanced: Business rules and processes include notification of logistics organization.  ||  Differentiated: Logistics organization has input in decision making process for supply chain organization.  ||  Best In Class: Logistics organization is involved in strategic business planning and product development.

items.control_description: 87. What level of influence does logistics have with broader ops planning and process improvement?
items.remarks: Basic: Logistics organization has no influence on supply chain—tail of the dog.  ||  Emerging: Logistics organization has some / moderate influence in purchasing decisions related to inbound freight management.  ||  Advanced: Logistics organization has influence with sales organization related to freight cost recovery.  ||  Differentiated: Logistics organization is involved by manufacturing organization to drive end to end supply chain improvements.  ||  Best In Class: Logistics organization identifies upstream drivers of increased costs and leads driving end-to-end supply chain improvements.

items.control_description: 88. How are upstream costs impacted by logistics managed?
items.remarks: Basic: No metrics tracked related to upstream drivers of logistics costs.  ||  Emerging: Expedite costs are tracked and assigned reason codes.  ||  Advanced: Expedite costs are tracked and recovered from upstream supply chain functions.  ||  Differentiated: Multiple cost factors (expedites, truck utilization, inventory, etc.) are tracked and recovered from upstream supply chain functions.  ||  Best In Class: Regular meetings occur to review metrics and conduct root cause analysis. Actions are tracked and managed and improvements measured.

items.control_description: 89. How is freight variance tracked and billed back?
items.remarks: Basic: Freight variance from corporate policies unknown (free freight, expedited, etc.).  ||  Emerging: Freight variance known and greater then 10% of annual freight spend.  ||  Advanced: Freight variance is known, tracked, and charged back to responsible party with some success.  ||  Differentiated: Freight variance is known, tracked, and charged back to responsible party.  ||  Best In Class: Freight policies designed and developed on a strategic customer-by-customer basis.

items.control_description: 90. How does the org determine ability to give away freightfor any reason?
items.remarks: Basic: No formal processes.  ||  Emerging: Cost of giving away freight documented and total amount is tracked.  ||  Advanced: Cost of giving away freight documented and determined based on general guidelines.  ||  Differentiated: Cost for each giveaway identified on a specific shipment or contract basis and used with stakeholders before decision is made.  ||  Best In Class: Appropriate logistics team member must be consulted and authorize all free freight. Formal crediting processto track logistics costs.

items.control_description: 91. How does the logistics org work with packaging to optimize shipping costs?
items.remarks: Basic: No integration between the packaging engineering and logistics.  ||  Emerging: Packaging information provided to logistics for use in optimization, mode selection, and transportation management.  ||  Advanced: Logistics organization consulted and given input in packaging design selection.  ||  Differentiated: Logistics organization actively involved with packaging design team identifying improvements and cost savings opportunities.  ||  Best In Class: Logistics organization actively involved with packaging design team during product design to identify opportunities prior to launch.

items.control_description: 34. How are import / export costs and documents currently managed?
items.remarks: Basic: Import/export operations decentralized with no alignment on strategic activities.  ||  Emerging: Reports and metrics available to select transportation contacts (normally at origin ship points).  ||  Advanced: Import / export operations managed centrally, with matrix responsibility to regions. Central and regional operations measured with global scorecards.  ||  Differentiated: Integrated activities with purchasing to assess total landed costs. Formal duty drawback program in place with technology support.  ||  Best In Class: Use of cloud-based technology-enabled end-to-end global trade management tool including landed cost calculation, product classification, restricted party screening and license determination. Automated duty management identifies preferential free trade programs, manages FTZs and duty drawback programs.

items.control_description: 35. How is transportation spend aggregated within or across regions?
items.remarks: Basic: No aggregation of spend for ocean / air freight.  ||  Emerging: Multiple customs brokers used within regions, ad hoc consolidation.  ||  Advanced: Spend leveraged regionally across customs brokers.  ||  Differentiated: Spend leveraged across most geographic regions through centralized procurement activities.  ||  Best In Class: Spend leveraged globally through centralized procurement activities within transportation.

items.control_description: 36. What level of visibility do you have to material flows?
items.remarks: Basic: No visibility of freight in-transit. Documentation and tracking of shipments is manual.  ||  Emerging: Freight track and trace available via carrier portals in no standardized formats.  ||  Advanced: Single broker used on corporate basis, provides single portal for global status of in-transit freight.  ||  Differentiated: Integrated visibility dashboard across supply chain to track shipments via TMS or APT tool.  ||  Best In Class: Integration of IoT sensors and GPS locator technology provides real-time updates of freight location and ETA based on locations at milestones.

items.control_description: 37. How are global trade contracts and documents managed?
items.remarks: Basic: Contracts managed and maintained by local offices.  ||  Emerging: No formal audit standards established for transportation contracts and history.  ||  Advanced: Verified carrier certifications - NAFTA: C-TPAT, FAST; EU: AEO.  ||  Differentiated: Technology supports compliance routing, track, price and shipments (all modes).  ||  Best In Class: Centralized repository for contracts and documentation including automated expiry and certification alerts. Technology supported compliance tracking and incident reporting.

items.control_description: 38. How much, if any, of your shipments are pre-cleared by customs?
items.remarks: Basic: No integration to carriers / customs.  ||  Emerging: Clearance as available. Little / no variation in customs classifications, documentation requirements.  ||  Advanced: At least 90% of shipments pre-cleared. Duty classifications consistent and reviewed for accuracy by CB.  ||  Differentiated: 95%+ of shipments precleared. Inhouse customs compliance with licensed brokers on staff.  ||  Best In Class: 98%+ of shipments pre-cleared. In-house customs compliance with licensed brokers on staff and technology enabled duty management.

items.control_description: 39. How is route planning optimized?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Field shipping personnel make modal, carrier, and routing decisions on an ad-hoc basis, based on experience.  ||  Emerging: System-enabled route planning performed with part-level mode, shipment quantity, shipment frequency, and delivery schedule optimization on a quarterly or biannual basis.  ||  Advanced: System-enabled route optimization on a monthly basis within defined constraints. Considers inventory constraints, parts value, and holding costs.  ||  Differentiated: Advanced route planning system with weekly route optimization. Upstream / downstream integration with plants, suppliers, and shippers. Control tower capability with enhanced visibility for tracking and reporting.  ||  Best In Class: TMS and integrated technologies intake upstream and downstream data inputs in real-time and continuously and automatically optimize route plans and reporting systems. Integrated IoT sensors and GPS technology can re-direct shipments enroute to a final location to avoid traffic congestion and weather delays. Route planning technology for freight requiring special handling requirements (e.g. long-haul reefers, explosives that must avoid routes with tunnels, etc.) analyzes conditional routing criteria to integrate compliance and safety management into automated planning.

items.control_description: 40. How is freight / shipment consolidation managed?
items.remarks: Basic: No attempt is made to consolidate shipments.  ||  Emerging: Shipments are consolidated on an ad hoc basis when possible.  ||  Advanced: Shipments are consolidated based upon defined shipment policies and routing guides.  ||  Differentiated: Shipments are consolidated on a regular cadence using load planning software based on partlevel dim / weight data.  ||  Best In Class: Shipments are dynamically consolidated using load planning software based on part-level dim / weight data.

items.control_description: 41. How is master data quality managed?
items.remarks: Basic: Part-level dim / weight data not maintained  ||  Emerging: Part-level dim / weight maintained in multiple systems and is inconsistent or incomplete. Low confidence in data quality.  ||  Advanced: Centralized dim / weight data management in place but not consistently applied or updated across the organization. Increasing trust in data accuracy.  ||  Differentiated: Single, comprehensive source of partlevel dim / weight data serves the entire organization providing high data integrity.  ||  Best In Class: Centralized dim / weight data is updated by vendors and transmitted to the networks master data repository. Audits are conducted to identify variances and flag receipts for cubiscan and dim / weight validation upon receipt. Wrong or missing dims results in chargebacks to vendors and is incorporate in vendor compliance management.

items.control_description: 42. Is cube / weight utilization integrated into planning processes?
items.remarks:
Basic: Utilization %—either cube or weight is not tracked.  ||  Emerging: Materials grouped within shipments specifically for utilization
Utilization % >80%.  ||  Advanced: Packaging and material flow adjustments evaluated in terms of utilization. Utilization >90%.  ||  Differentiated: Volume metric cargo optimized with weighout cargo to maximize both weight and cube. Utilization >95%.  ||  Best In Class: Load building is automated by transportation planning systems. Lanes with a utilization under target are evaluated the following week and analyzed for root causes. Utilization >95%.

items.control_description: 43. Are sustainability considerations incorporated in transport mode selection processes?
items.remarks: Basic: No consideration for environmental impact.  ||  Emerging: Minimal understanding of the environmental impact by different mode choices. No active management to try to select less impactful mode types.  ||  Advanced: Clear understanding of environmental impacts within transportation department. Minimal selection of mode choice and environmental impacts.  ||  Differentiated: Clear understanding of environmental impact across executive staff. Active management and decisions to select modes with lower environmental impact.  ||  Best In Class: Sustainability parameters are incorporated into transportation planning systems to reduce environmental impact. Associated cost reduction from environmentally conscious transportation decisions are also integrated into reporting systems.

items.control_description: 44. What is your methodology for tender execution?
items.remarks: Basic: All loads are tendered by phone / email.  ||  Emerging: 50%+ loads are tendered electronically (via EDI, API, web-portal).  ||  Advanced: 95%+ loads are tendered electronically (via EDI, API, web-portal).  ||  Differentiated: 99%+ loads are tendered electronically.  ||  Best In Class: Almost all load tendering is executed using an integrated TMS platform. Automated systems prioritize tendering sequencing to "best" carrier (cost / service) and subsequent "next best" carriers if a load is unable to be serviced. Trends for ""tender acceptance" are analyzed by the TMS and integrated systems and communicated to internal management for carrier evaluation and follow up.

items.control_description: 45. How is short-term planning managed?
items.remarks: Basic: Makes no assessment of future transportation requirements or estimated requirements <2 days prior to need.  ||  Emerging: Transportation requirements are estimated at least 2 days prior to need.  ||  Advanced: Transportation requirements are estimated 1–2 weeks prior to need.  ||  Differentiated: Transportation requirements are estimated >2 weeks prior to need.  ||  Best In Class: Short-term planning is facilitated through a system or AI based technology to provided more complete visibility to planning requirements and continuously improve forecasting accuracy.

items.control_description: 46. How is mid-term planning managed?
items.remarks: Basic: No formal transportation requirement planning process.  ||  Emerging: Transportation requirements are estimated by transportation group.  ||  Advanced: Transportation requirements are calculated based upon sales and production forecasts.  ||  Differentiated: Transportation requirements are generated from integrated logistics, sales and production plans.  ||  Best In Class: Mid-term planning is facilitated through a system or AI based technology to provided more complete visibility to planning requirements and continuously improve forecasting accuracy.

items.control_description: 47. Who is primarily responsible for tracking and tracing shipments?
items.remarks: Basic: No assigned responsibility for tracking shipments. No defined procedure for tracking shipments.  ||  Emerging: Relies on carriers to track shipments on an as-needed basis and measure service to designated contact points.  ||  Advanced: Transportation organization has lead responsibility and access for tracking on behalf of company.  ||  Differentiated: Transportation has lead but tracking results fully integrated into material and production management systems for use across the business.  ||  Best In Class: Centralized control tower has lead responsibility for tracking and tracing shipments. Deviations from plan (delays, routing changes, etc.) are raised to responsible region / function with responsibility to course correct and proactively communicate with impacted supply chain functions.

items.control_description: 48. How do you provide / receive tracking and tracing information with vendors / carriers / customers?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Telephone tag team. Manual offline.  ||  Emerging: Carrier tracking capability leveraged as needed across organization. Company access to carrier system but not linked. EDI integration with some modes, some modes missed.  ||  Advanced: EDI is a standard requirement of core carriers. EDI data status reporting used to support planning, scheduling, and receiving functions.  ||  Differentiated: EDI with carriers and vendors. EDI for tracking shipments internally and by supply chain partners. Integrated threeway interchange with vendors and carriers.  ||  Best In Class: Carriers and vendors integrated with visibility systems to provide tracking and tracing updates. IOT and GPS sensors enabled for real-time tracking and location information.

items.control_description: 49. How are issues or potential issues identified and resolved?
items.remarks: Basic: No solutions—always a symptom, never a cure.  ||  Emerging: Containment needs evaluated for other shipments in field and addressed as required.  ||  Advanced: Detailed root-cause evaluation completed to ensure failure mode doesn’t come back.  ||  Differentiated: Best practice prevention techniques shared across the modes and business units.  ||  Best In Class: System-enabled alerts or push messages to identify potential issues prompting preventative actions or pro-active communication. Automated escalation rules to raise significant issues to the appropriate level of attention.

items.control_description: 50. How frequently are shipments being tracked / traced?
items.remarks: Basic: Manual offline.  ||  Emerging: Tracking system periodically updated through driver calls or other manual system.  ||  Advanced: Tracking system automatically updated through integrated electronic system.  ||  Differentiated: Equipment tracking and status available realtime.  ||  Best In Class: IOT sensors enabled for continuous, real-time shipment and equipment tracking.

items.control_description: 51. What are your capabilities for understanding the location of a shipment at a given point in time?
items.remarks: Basic: No future containment process.  ||  Emerging: Only monitored at “touch” points (pickup, cross-dock, deliver, etc.).  ||  Advanced: Location-based point in time.  ||  Differentiated: Live location details.  ||  Best In Class: Live geo-fenced location details on network-wide basis with ability to view all shipments simultaneously on "dashboard".

items.control_description: 52. Once you identify an issue with a shipment, what is the process for resolving that event systematically?
items.remarks: Basic: Responsive crisis tracking not proactive monitoring.  ||  Emerging: Defined communication standards and procedures for notification of problems.  ||  Advanced: Automated tracking and identification of “at-risk” loads on event basis.  ||  Differentiated: Real-time monitoring of intransit for real-time identification of issues.  ||  Best In Class: Real-time identification of issues combined with computer learning-enabled event resolution recommendations.

items.control_description: 53. How do you "rate" a shipment (i.e. determine how much it should cost) prior to execution?
items.remarks: Basic: Manual freight rating. Incomplete, infrequently updated rate files.  ||  Emerging: Manual freight rating supported by computer-based rate file.  ||  Advanced: Automated freight rating, pre-audit, match and pay.  ||  Differentiated: Automatic “self invoicing,” direct pay—no auditing on ones or more modes. Ability to handle rate structures from multiple carriers.  ||  Best In Class: Automatic “self-invoicing,” direct pay with ability to audit actuals post-shipment. Multiple carrier rate structures and ability to handle additional complexity in rates like fuel surcharge pads, accessorials, etc.

items.control_description: 54. How do you validate the information on carrier documents such as BOLs?
items.remarks: Basic: Manual bill of lading / freight bill match.  ||  Emerging: Automated match.  ||  Advanced: EDI by carrier to eliminate data reentry.  ||  Differentiated: Direct electronic messaging to carrier—no data reentry.  ||  Best In Class: Technology enabled verification of all transaction details and ability to automatically verify and pay freight bills.

items.control_description: 55. What is your freight payment process?
items.remarks: Basic: Post-payment manual auditing, if any. Paper invoices / payment.  ||  Emerging: Electronic auditing with data reentry. Some freight bill data and freight history retained. Macro reports.  ||  Advanced: Automated review and processing of >85% of all invoices (inclusive of small-package line-item detail). Standard report & summaries.  ||  Differentiated: Automated review and processing of >95% of all invoices (inclusive of small package line item detail). Standard report & summaries.  ||  Best In Class: No invoices. Electronic funds transfer. Monthly roll-up of invoices or staged payments.

items.control_description: 56. How do you resolve billing issues or other invoice discrepancies with your carriers?
items.remarks: Basic: No payment records or freight history captured or retained.  ||  Emerging: Outside post-audit and overcharge claim process. Some freight bill data and freight history retained. Process for problem resolution—mainly involves phone / email.  ||  Advanced: Freight payment accuracy reports integrated to carrier reviews. Well-defined database updated regularly from freight payment data. Errors and problems managed via auto-approval and escalation.  ||  Differentiated: Freight payment accuracy reports integrated to carrier reviews. Billing errors occur on <2% of shipments.  ||  Best In Class: Freight payment accuracy reports integrated to carrier reviews. Billing errors occur on <1% of shipments.

items.control_description: 57. What are you invoice processing costs (i.e. cost per invoice)?
items.remarks: Basic: Invoice processing cost (per B/L) >$10.  ||  Emerging: Invoice processing cost (per B/L) $4–6  ||  Advanced: Invoice processing cost (per B/L) ±$1.50.  ||  Differentiated: Invoice processing cost (per B / L) <$.50.  ||  Best In Class: §Invoice processing cost (per B / L) <$.35.

items.control_description: 9. How is transportation integrated within the overall supply chain strategy?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Transportation is seen as an enabler of the organization's supply chain, but is managed as a standalone business function. Strategy alignment with other supply chain departments occurs on an ad-hoc basis with daily tactical coordination with suppliers, operations and downstream customers.  ||  Emerging: Strategic integration to other supply chain functions occurs at a regional or BU level with segmentation by mode. Transportation strategy success is measured on service level attainment within budgeted cost. Individual technology solutions required to enable strategy are considered on a forward looking strategic "roadmap".  ||  Advanced: Transportation strategy is globally harmonized within the corporation. This includes standardized best practices by mode category for processes & technology.  ||  Differentiated: Transportation strategy is globally harmonized across the value chain (e.g. suppliers, production, warehousing & distribution) with regional geographic ownership and special considerations for BU level requirements. This includes globally harmonized processes & technologies. An integrated technology approach which enables the overall strategy is part of an integrated roadmap.  ||  Best In Class: Transportation is seen as a differentiator and a value driver within the corporate strategy. Investment in people, technology and strategic partnerships enable global visibility, standardized processes and eliminate redundant and paper based processes.

items.control_description: 10. Who establishes strategy for and owns the transportation function?
items.remarks: Basic: No formal organization exists across the business for transportation. Transportation strategy is developed and owned by local facility leadership (e.g. Transportation Manager at Plant). How technology can be used to enable the strategy is given little or no consideration.  ||  Emerging: Transportation strategy is developed and owned by regional or BU specific leadership.  ||  Advanced: Transportation strategy is developed and owned by global leadership and harmonized with the corporate transportation strategy.  ||  Differentiated: Transportation strategy is developed and owned by global leadership and integrated with strategic alliances and external partner initiatives  ||  Best In Class: Transportation strategy development is harmonized with the corporate strategy and seeks to enable people, processes and technologies of the future. This includes forward looking investments in solutions and platforms that connect internal and external resources and data. Digital solutions such as IoT sensors and blockchain are integrated to strategic initiatives with external partners (e.g. suppliers / carriers).

items.control_description: 11. What are the guiding principles for transportation budgeting?
items.remarks:
Basic: No formal transportation budgeting process. Previous year spend and fuel cost drive annual budgeting.  ||  Emerging: Transportation budgeting process are formalized.
YoY spend analysis and market trends are the primary basis for budgeting. Transportation initiatives are managed separately and expected results are not incorporated into budgetary targets..  ||  Advanced: Transportation budgeting processes are formalized and harmonized across supply chain and corporate functions. Business growth, product launches and other in-flight initiatives are translated into transportation requirements to create a "bottoms up" budget. Digital logistics tools are leveraged to conduct spend analysis and provide forward looking projections.  ||  Differentiated: Transportation budgeting processes are formalized and harmonized across supply chain and corporate functions. External partner and macro / micro factors are integrated into budgeting forecast. Internal corporate and external partner initiatives are factored into annual budgets to ensure that planned savings are realized and reach the "bottom line".  ||  Best In Class: Digital solutions and technologies are incorporated and prioritized by into annual and long term budgeting. Executive compensation budgets are tied to efficiencies realized through continuous improvements and digital initiatives.

items.control_description: 13. How are performance measures incorporated with your transportation strategy?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Transportation performance is loosely monitored via ad hoc inputs from key stakeholders / supply chain partners.  ||  Emerging: Transportation organization measures performance to via defined transportation metrics and goals. Improvement initiatives focused on areas within the control of the transportation organization. Data available is recent and accurate but has to be manually extracted from various systems and manipulated.  ||  Advanced: Transportation organization measures performance to via defined transportation metrics and goals. Improvement initiatives are coordinated with upstream and downstream supply chain stakeholders. Data available and can be refreshed on demand through data warehouse / business intelligence tool.  ||  Differentiated: Transportation performance measured as part of overall supply chain performance. Improvement initiatives include those areas outside of transportation group’s span of control. Data available is recent and accurate, with dashboards updated regularly (daily / weekly).  ||  Best In Class: Transportation performance is seen as a integral part to supply chain decision making and performance differentiation. Culture of continuous improvement exists and includes upstream and downstream partners in the supply chain.

items.control_description: 14. How is strategic outsourcing viewed by your organization?
items.remarks:
[Rapid DOMA] Basic: Ad-hoc outsourcing decisions are determined by local leadership on an as needed basis  ||  Emerging: Outsourcing decisions are made at a corporate level. Determination for outsourcing of particular transportation functions is to support expanded distribution or new capability requirements.  ||  Advanced: Outsourcing decisions are made considering core / non core activities to divest that will improve functional performance, increase capabilities and decrease cost.  ||  Differentiated: Outsourcing of activities assessed across the supply chain to serve strategic needs / opportunities. Strategic partnerships with vendors are established and serve to support external supplier and customer requirements.  ||  Best In Class: Outsourcing decisions are made to support long term corporate strategies and enable trust and partnership throughout the Supply Chain. 
  Integration to strategic outsourcing partner systems is a key enabler to support visibility and 3PL partner management. 
  Outsourcing partner selection includes evaluation of their digital technology capabilities' an ability to support in place or planned initiatives.

items.control_description: 15. Does your company manage expedites?
items.remarks:
Basic: There are no options to manage expedited shipments. Stakeholders can expedite without approval.  ||  Emerging: Expedited shipments accepted with no integration into existing shipment schedule. Execution, approval, and communication is managed by local site contacts. Limited ability to systematically prevent / monitor expedited shipments.  ||  Advanced: Expedited shipments have some integration into existing shipment schedule. Adjustments to shipment schedule are made after decision to accept expedited shipment are made. Expedite database exists and tracks expedite shipment reason, cost,lane, and responsibility.  ||  Differentiated: Expedited shipments are integrated into existing shipment schedule. Necessary adjustments to shipping schedule can be seen prior to acceptance of expedited shipment. Need for expedites can be forecasted through advanced scheduling capabilities and recommendations (transportation event scenario modeling) can be made using data. Expedite database is analyzed for continuous improvement opportunities.  ||  Best In Class: Expedite shipment requests are managed through a standalone tool used for end-to-end process including tracking shipment status.
Shipment schedule adjustments and production planning approval requests are auto transmitted and received. Potential expedites are systematically identified using machine learning or advanced milestone tracking and proactive messages are triggered to alert planner of exception.

items.control_description: 16. What is your strategy for consolidating spend?
items.remarks: Basic: Spend is not leveraged or analyzed - many carriers / partners are used and multiple contracts per single carrier may exist across BU's / regions.  ||  Emerging: Spend is leveraged at local site across strategic set of carriers / partners.  ||  Advanced: Supply base management is conducted at the corporate level—plants / regional locations use preferred carriers.  ||  Differentiated: Supply base rationalization and carrier partnerships are used for strategic advantages.  ||  Best In Class: Vendors codes and alias are analyzed across the enterprise to identify "parent vendor" spend and consolidation opportunities and unfavorable terms for duplicate contracts across regions, BU's or "child vendors".

items.control_description: 17. How are supplier relationships viewed and managed?
items.remarks:
Basic: Suppliers are selected based on lane-by-lane price competition and only transactional relationships exist.  ||  Emerging: Carriers selected based on geographic locations and shipping lanes; business directed to those carriers
 Relationships are at the local level.  ||  Advanced: Core carrier program by mode established. Partnerships built with core carriers used as basis for awarding future business. Volumes committed to each carrier as well as tendering history are maintained systematically to ensure core carrier program is executed properly.  ||  Differentiated: Core group of carriers within each mode leveraged for strategic partnership and growth. System automatically recommends the carrier / rate combination for a given lane or shipment based on core carrier program.  ||  Best In Class: Strategic carrier partnerships are in place with seamless data integration. Carriers collaborate with shipper on continuous improvement programs and identify ways to pass through cost savings.

items.control_description: 18. What is the frequency and driver of rebidding?
items.remarks:
Basic: Supply market understanding is based on recent experience. Rebidding is done on an ad hoc basis.  ||  Emerging: The supply market is monitored for select modes to track price and capacity trends against.
 Current transportation needs and bids are executed when price triggers are reached..  ||  Advanced: The supply market is monitored in order to anticipate macro-level change and identify opportunities across modes for rebidding.  ||  Differentiated: The supply market is continuously monitored; insights that may affect the overall distribution strategy are shared across the company for rebidding decisions.  ||  Best In Class: Supply market knowledge and external rate benchmarks are used to segment transportation lanes for sourcing event. Sourcing occurs on a regular cadence and during optimal market timing depending on the mode (or at a minimum rates are reviewed each year to determine need for sourcing event). Sourcing events leverage volume and spend across the enterprise.

items.control_description: 19. How are bid events executed?
items.remarks:
Basic: No formal bidding process; focus is on limiting price increases for existing contracts. Bidding limited to transportation execution activities, e.g., spot quotes on lanes.  ||  Emerging: Ad hoc competitive bidding applied only on very high purchasing volumes with limited or no savings validation
 Bidding primarily with existing carriers only..  ||  Advanced: Competitive bidding process used in most cases, with common system to track savings. Informal process for including new carriers in sourcing event.  ||  Differentiated: Comprehensive bidding process used in all cases with highly accurate savings tracking. Established process to research, identify, and qualify new carriers for sourcing event.  ||  Best In Class: Carriers participate using an e-procurement / TMS tool. Approved carriers submit and are awarded bids for lanes in system.

items.control_description: 20. What is your strategy for bid event participation?
items.remarks: Basic: Only include existing carriers.  ||  Emerging: Existing carriers and a limited number of carriers that have recently inquired about hauling (e.g. 15% or fewer new carriers participate).  ||  Advanced: Database of potential carriers is maintained and used for bid events. 15–35% new carriers participate.  ||  Differentiated: Available databases such as DOT and analytic scoring used to identify potential carriers. >35% new carriers participate in bid event (or at a minimum, 3 carriers for every $1M in spend).  ||  Best In Class: Bid event participation is supported by a large network of carriers (existing and new) who are pre-integrated with best of breed TMS technology to ease on-boarding and support of transportation lanes.

items.control_description: 21. What is the buyer expertise strategy for the company?
items.remarks: Basic: Large number of field-level buyers with little experience.  ||  Emerging: Large number of informally coordinated buyers with only general transportation experience. Transportation not a separate spend category.  ||  Advanced: Medium number of experienced buyers, formalized coordination across plants, regions, and modes. Transportation is a dedicated spend category with specific sourcing events.  ||  Differentiated: Small number of buyers with background in transportation and purchasing, coordinated through formal processes and technology based tools.  ||  Best In Class: Buyers are coordinated with operations to understand carrier performance and opportunity to expand carrier's existing set of business. Volumes are aggregated and strategically leveraged globally for inclusion in sourcing events.

items.control_description: 22. What are your processes for bid optimization?
items.remarks: Basic: No optimization tools.  ||  Emerging: Manual excel / access-based scenario analysis without optimization.  ||  Advanced: Excel / access-based scenario analysis with optimization.  ||  Differentiated: Bid optimization tools with scenario based trade offs used.  ||  Best In Class: Bid optimization tool integrated with execution tools (e.g. TMS). Scenario analysis conducted to layer operation constraints, run savings scenarios and conduct negotiations.

items.control_description: 23. How are tariff structures utilized?
items.remarks: Basic: No tariff structure strategy.  ||  Emerging: Tariff strategy discussed but not fully implemented.  ||  Advanced: Tariff strategy fully implemented, not fully integrated into transportation strategy and business planning.  ||  Differentiated: Tariff strategy full implemented and integrated into transportation strategy and business planning; pricing according to a specific tariff (e.g. czarlite) is required by all vendors to ensure comparability between rates and discounts.  ||  Best In Class: Tariff strategy and structure is aligned and integrated across the enterprise during sourcing cycle for comparative analysis and implemented into TMS execution system to calculate tariff prices and utilize information to determine "best" carrier selection for each shipment.

items.control_description: 24. How is purchasing aligned to transportation sourcing?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Transportation and purchasing not aligned.  ||  Emerging: Transportation group provides data analysis to purchasing as needed.  ||  Advanced: Transportation aligned with purchasing. Data analysis completed on a regular basis.  ||  Differentiated: Transportation is vital part of supply chain and purchased / total cost methodology.  ||  Best In Class: Combined analysis establishes freight terms to minimize transportation cost of the supply chain.

items.control_description: 25. What is your freight payment strategy?
items.remarks: Basic: Payment and documentation managed via manual / paper based processes. Avoids collect freight. Little or no purchased goods invoiced as prepaid and add.  ||  Emerging: Payment and documentation managed via standalone transportation system. Has collect freight terms with some vendors (20–30%). Less than 25% purchased goods invoiced as prepaid and add..  ||  Advanced: Payment and documentation integrated with corporate ERP systems and centrally managed by region. Maintains inbound freight collect with up to 50% of suppliers. 25–40% purchased goods invoiced as prepaid and add.  ||  Differentiated: Payment and documentation integrated with corporate ERP systems and EDI transmission to carriers, suppliers and customers. 70% or more inbound freight collect. All remaining non-purchased goods invoiced as prepaid and add.  ||  Best In Class: IoT sensors technology provide chain of custody assurance and real-time notification for freight arrival and departure, which triggers payment processing and accessorials. Payment and invoice matching and dispute resolution are carried out through a decentralized ledger "blockchain" that increase the speed and efficiency of transactions and free cash flow traditionally tied up in AP.

items.control_description: 26. How do you manage cost calculation?
items.remarks: Basic: No visibility to inbound freight costs.  ||  Emerging: Freight costs estimated based upon a % of invoice (either on invoice or internally).  ||  Advanced: Inbound transportation costs clearly and accurately identified on supplier invoices. Costs able to be broken down by unit weight and / or volume for comparison.  ||  Differentiated: Assigned actual freight costs identifiable at SKU and supplier level. Contracted freight terms are maintained centrally and accuracy is monitored on a normal cadence.  ||  Best In Class: Inbound and outbound freight cost calculated utilizing contracted rates, and SKU / vendor level cost agreements.Tolerance levels trigger alerts when excess freight charges occur and send automated request to agents / carriers for variance justification.

items.control_description: 27. How are delivery estimation initially determined and updated?
items.remarks: Basic: Uses macro estimates of transit times—no differentiation by mode, supplier or service.  ||  Emerging: Uses macro time estimates by mode.  ||  Advanced: Maintains all historical transit times by mode, service, and network channels to calculate expected delivery date.  ||  Differentiated: Uses highly automated process to manage transit times by lane based on historical data and future trends.  ||  Best In Class: Use of machine learning to continuously update estimated transit times in system.

items.control_description: 28. What level of visibility do you have to inbound material flows?
items.remarks: Basic: No visibility of inbound freight—shipments “arrive” at destination.  ||  Emerging: Limited advance notification "ASN" integration with existing management systems. Burden of setup on carrier.  ||  Advanced: Fully automated inbound transportation management with clear visibility of ASN data provided to the business.  ||  Differentiated: Automated threeway communication link for material visibility: carrier, vendor, and company. Formal procedure in place for new vendor setup and EDI integration globally.  ||  Best In Class: Integration of IoT sensors and GPS locator technology provides real-time updates of freight location and ETA based on locations at milestones. Integration of weather forecasting and road condition monitoring provides proactive visibility to potential delays and alternative routing options. Geofencing and automated yard check in technology alert operations and inform inbound receiving schedules and yard management systems of freight location and priority.

items.control_description: 29. What is the overall fleet strategy?
items.remarks: Basic: Fleet trucks added on ad hoc basis for site specific needs.  ||  Emerging: Fleet strategy based on expansion of historical usage to drive utilization.  ||  Advanced: Strategy based on integration with existing common carrier capacity and footprint.  ||  Differentiated: Fleet strategy based on optimal performance of fleet integrated with internal and vendor demurrage commitments (e.g. dwell time management at origin and destination to reduce fleet size requirements).  ||  Best In Class: Technology such as GPS tracking devices enables the strategy through real-time visibility to assets and provide a competitive differentiation in the market.

items.control_description: 30. How is fleet size determined?
items.remarks: Basic: Undefined target, organically grown without specific planning.  ||  Emerging: Size based on peak utilization. Power units and trailer managed independently.  ||  Advanced: Fleet size includes future requirements developed based on strategy. Equipment types optimized for usage. Home grown model used to determine fleet size.  ||  Differentiated: Fleet size managed proactively to grow and contract to meet the strategic requirements – focus on agility and cost. For leased assets, market analyzed to determine timing for leases. Rail / fleet planning system used to model fleet size.  ||  Best In Class: Company models risk into determining optimal fleet size and quantifies any incremental cost associated with carrying additional assets. Demurrage policies are enforced with substantiated evidence of excess dwell provided by GPS location and a digital trail of automated notification for "return of asset" request and responses for equipment dwelling at customer locations.

items.control_description: 31. What is your fleet deployment strategy?
items.remarks: Basic: Individual pieces of equipment distributed through network on ad hoc basis.  ||  Emerging: Adjustments to fleet deployment made on a manual basis locally.  ||  Advanced: Equipment deployment across the network centrally monitored and managed.  ||  Differentiated: Fleet deployment monitored and adjusted on an ongoing basis. External supply chain partnerships in place to coordinate fleet deployment alignment to planned maintenance schedules.  ||  Best In Class: Fleet deployment evaluated and adjusted on an on-going basis utilizing data insights from asset tracking and maintenance monitoring technology. Predictive and scheduled maintenance activities are centrally managed, informing fleet deployment adjustments proactively when a capacity risk from maintenance activities is identified.

items.control_description: 32. How do you view integration with common carriers?
items.remarks: Basic: Dedicated fleet and common carrier managed independently.  ||  Emerging: Dedicated fleet and common carrier routed using same routing center. Dedicated or common carrier by lane defined on an ad hoc basis.  ||  Advanced: Dedicated fleet and common carrier responsibilities coordinated. Dedicated or common by lane defined statically.  ||  Differentiated: Dedicated fleet and common carrier fully integrated which lanes are carried by common carrier and which are dedicated fleet is determined dynamically.  ||  Best In Class: Dedicated fleet parameters and asset availability are integrated into the transportation management systems and managed centrally; were excess capacity for dedicated fleet assets is identified, market needs are matched to fleet assets to increase utilization.

items.control_description: 33. Are backhaul / utilization optimization programs in place?
items.remarks: Basic: Equipment backhauls not managed.  ||  Emerging: Utilization improved through coordination of inbound / outbound and internal usage.  ||  Advanced: Backhauls picked up through load boards or 3PL / broker relationship to improve utilization.  ||  Differentiated: Fleet utilization and lane usage managed through freight alliances to maximize utilization. Backhaul operations used as revenue generation operations.  ||  Best In Class: Strategic freight alliances with backhaul candidates are identified on common lanes and enabled through visibility from GPS coordinate transmissions for assurance and traceability. Were remaining excess capacity for dedicated fleet assets is identified, "profitable" market needs are matched to fleet assets for planned empty transit through an automated freight booking system.

items.control_description: 1. How do you manage receiving of goods and QM related tasks?
items.remarks: Basic: Traditional receiving of goods. Delivery notes / slips are checked and quality checks are done based on a statistical failure models.  ||  Emerging: New technologies such as RFID in place - Automated counting of goods.  ||  Advanced: Suppliers use warehouse specific labelling and packaging. Seamless storage of goods possible. Packaging enables seamless quality controls. Automated feedback to suppliers.  ||  Differentiated: Automated / Touchless receiving of goods of internal suppliers. Packaging meets warehouse standards. QM is done before shipment or and sensors ensure that no damages occurred during transportation or Qchecks are automatically integrated in the receiving process.  ||  Best In Class: Automated / touchless receiving of goods for certified suppliers. Suppliers deliver goods following clear packaging rules. Goods are received and stored automatically.

items.control_description: 2. How do you monitor inventory levels?
items.remarks: Basic: Automatically in ERP system (near time and based on top down recipe).  ||  Emerging: Automatically in ERP system, BOM data updated manually through bottom up feedback loop.  ||  Advanced: In ERP system, BOM data updated automatically through bottom up feedback loop.  ||  Differentiated: Inventory levels from suppliers to customers including scheduled orders and in transit goods automatically are used.  ||  Best In Class: Also includes real time track and trace of deliveries / products, customer's actual demand / consumption. AI also manages inventory of customers and suppliers – allows e.g. shift of inventory form one customer to another.

items.control_description: 3. How is the Warehouse replenished with finished goods?
items.remarks: Basic: Order based replenishment signal, two inventory locations.  ||  Emerging: Picking reactive to order entry, in case of several orders, priority is defined by experience rules. Automation: barcoding, forklifts.  ||  Advanced: Mainly one inventory location, replenishment based on continuous replenishment principle.  ||  Differentiated: One inventory location, replenishment based on VMI principle, information flow about inventory movements are processed continuously.  ||  Best In Class: One inventory location, replenishment based on VMI principle, information flow about inventory movements are fully automated.

items.control_description: 4. How do you manage your raw and semi-finished inventories?
items.remarks: Basic: ERP based tracking. Not delivered parts pop-up in the system one day after planned arrival day.  ||  Emerging: Inventory levels are digitally visible with some automation in re-ordering processes. Still some manual work is required..  ||  Advanced: Complete visibility of inventories across plants and integration into demand and supply planning.  ||  Differentiated: Touchless consigned inventories. Key suppliers are integrated via EDI to ensure seamless information transfer. Inventory levels are digitally measured and available in real time.  ||  Best In Class: Digital Kanban automatic reordering process. Suppliers are 100% integrated in planning process (connectivity) and are able to react in (near) real time.

items.control_description: 5. How do you optimize your batch sizes and inventory levels?
items.remarks:
Basic: Optimized batch sizes, safety stock, based on e.g. inventory vs. Manufacturing costs, calculated safety stocks, at least quarterly updated.  ||  Emerging: Optimized, batch sizes, safety stock, based confirmed orders regularly adapted and assessed.  ||  Advanced: Optimized, batch sizes, safety stock, based on vertical inputs from across the plant. Safety stock algorithms are regularly updated
 TCO is one driving factor.  ||  Differentiated: Optimized batch sizes, safety stock, based on horizontal inputs (forecasts based on big data analytics)
 TCO is one driving factor.  ||  Best In Class: Automatically optimized batch sizes, safety stock. TCO is one driving factor.

items.control_description: 6. How automated is your warehouse?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Kanban and supermarkets are defined. Clear rules and automatism are in place. Traditional transportation of goods.  ||  Emerging: Advanced automated warehousing. Goods are Automatically picked from the warehouse. Manual steps are still necessary.  ||  Advanced: AGV in place. Key goods are transported with no human interaction. Storage position is adapted based on demand to reduce waste in transportation. Augmented reality picking, pick by light to increase efficiency and avoid mistakes.  ||  Differentiated: Workforce and robots work alongside. Human and robot teammates swap tasks to learn each others preferences. Robots performing tiresome and repetitive tasks lead to improved ergonomics for employees. Robots support flexible deployment depending on the unit volumes and production scopes. Automated optimization of location, Kanban sizes etc.  ||  Best In Class: Automated disposition of goods. Smart Robots, AGVs and warehouse management systems ensure "touchless" disposition and allocation of goods.

items.control_description: 7. How do you assure picking quality?
items.remarks: Basic: Picking reactive to order entry, according to first-in-first out principle. No barcodes, some forklifts.  ||  Emerging: Picking reactive to order entry, in case of several orders, priority is defined by experience rules. Automation: barcoding, forklifts.  ||  Advanced: Picking reactive to order entry, in case of several orders, priority is defined by documented rules. Automation: barcoding, automatic picking.  ||  Differentiated: Integrated solution of wave picking (where possible) and other warehousing logic, according to maximization of reactivity and efficiency. Automation: RFID, automatic picking and packing, automatic delivery note on shipment.  ||  Best In Class: Advanced checks based on data analytics and plausibility assessments across the whole warehousing system. E.g. Inventory crosschecks,.

items.control_description: 9. How is your production logistics organized?
items.remarks:
Basic: Lean management optimized production logistics (e.g. predefined routes, processes, etc.).  ||  Emerging: Partially automated material handling systems. E.g. automated rack system
Robotic attachment on vehicles for automated material handling.
Augmented picking autonomous and packing in use.  ||  Advanced: Connected warehouse logistics systems facilitate cross-warehouse visibility and optimization within the company. Digital inventory management is integrated in detailed production planning.  ||  Differentiated: E2E: Connected warehouse logistics systems, crosswarehouse visibility and optimization
 Last mile notification (improved slot booking) to optimize inbound logistics.  ||  Best In Class: Fully autonomous and self-optimizing transport system integrated in e.g. MES / ERP systems. Automated receiving quality control tagging and storing. Use of smart robots in close proximity with warehouse staff.

items.control_description: 11. How do you manage employee training and process development and adherence?
items.remarks:
Basic: Best practices isolated by BU, site, mode, and / or region. Training and development performed for new hires through "tribal" knowledge sharing from trainer. Formalized re-training only occurs if a major process change occurs. Adherence to policies managed through visual observations or retroactively.  ||  Emerging: Internal best practices shared across BU's, sites, modes and regions based upon available capabilities
Quarterly training provided to ensure adherence to current and revised processes
Business controls are well defined and documented.
Systemic limitations and various user profiles utilized to control access and enforce policies
Processes reviewed quarterly or annually to evaluate effectiveness.  ||  Advanced: Training and processes developed and managed to harmonize activities within system limitations and to enable upstream and downstream performance and adherence
 Process changes are communicated throughout the logistics organization and training occcurs prior to implementation of change.  ||  Differentiated: Training curricula and processes developed and managed to optimize performance and adherence across functional scope.  ||  Best In Class: Utilization of virtual and augmented reality technology to provide simulated standardized training exercises for the user. 
 Lowers cost and increases efficiency of training. 
 Prevents risk of injury to the user or impact to the business from user errors.
 Policy adherence is enforced through systemic controls and warehousing and automation sensors to prevent impact to operations and safety.
 Operational process and automation changes can be tested through simulation software to identify impact to operations in advance of implementation.

items.control_description: 12. How often is the warehouse configuration evaluated and optimized?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: No optimization of the warehouse. Material is moved only when space requirements drive, or when earlier such actions are reversed.  ||  Emerging: Ad-hoc and infrequent rearrangements of the warehouse..  ||  Advanced: Frequent, periodic rearrangements of the warehouse (SKU static slotting) when movement patterns of stock change significantly.  ||  Differentiated: Dynamic SKU slotting is used to continually optimize warehouse space. Rearrangements are based on changing stock movement patterns.  ||  Best In Class: AI / Machine learning modules used to track past demand patterns and autonomously adjust warehouse slotting layout to minimize distance traveled for operators.

items.control_description: 27. How is inventory stored in the warehouse?
items.remarks: Basic: Floor storage is utilized in for bulk stacking of product.  ||  Emerging: Racking and / or shelving is utilized to minimize product damage. No cubic modeling of storage need is conducted.  ||  Advanced: A variety of static storage is utilized to maximize storage capacity and reduce replenishment labor. Storage modeling is utilized to match the demand with the proper storage medium.  ||  Differentiated: A variety of storage is utilized to maximize storage capacity and reduce replenishment labor. Storage modes potential include automated solutions such as AS / RS, miniloads, and carousels. Storage modeling is utilized to match the demand with the proper storage medium.  ||  Best In Class: Storage control systems are integrated with the digital control tower to minimize waste in the process.

items.control_description: 28. How do you plan material handling equipment requirements?
items.remarks: Basic: Lift truck decisions made on historical usage and driver familiarity.  ||  Emerging: Lift truck decisions based on cost and historical usage.  ||  Advanced: Lift truck decisions modeled to maximize flexibility, cost, and productivity.  ||  Differentiated: Lift truck decisions modeled to maximize flexibility, cost, and productivity. Impact of storage density and facility costs due to aisle width such as VNA factored into decision making process  ||  Best In Class: Material handling equipment is fully automated and integrated with the digital control tower.

items.control_description: 29. How is your warehouse security organized?
items.remarks: Basic: No clearly defined security procedures.  ||  Emerging: No clearly defined security procedures but some visual management.  ||  Advanced: Basic security procedures and compliance is monitored.  ||  Differentiated: Fully documented site security procedures with full visual management and regular updating, training and auditing. Compliance is enforced.  ||  Best In Class: Facility access is controlled according to role with digital simulations identifying possible risk points.

items.control_description: 30. How do you handle delivery exceptions?
items.remarks: Basic: Customer, DC, or MFG Site not sure of what, when and where to expect delivery.  ||  Emerging: Time-lag in providing delivery information but shipping issues are eventually communicated.  ||  Advanced: Automatic alerts to warn customer of potential shipping issues.  ||  Differentiated: Automatic alerts and automatically triggered remedial actions to manage delivery exceptions.  ||  Best In Class: Delivery exception simulations are generated in real time to reduce the occurrence of a customer service issue.

items.control_description: 31. How do you plan workload for distribution teams?
items.remarks: Basic: Receiving / shipping warehouse has limited visibility on expected inbound / outbound flows and no visibility on expected workload.  ||  Emerging: Receiving / shipping warehouse has visibility on expected trucks, but not on the expected handling volumes or special logistics needs.  ||  Advanced: Receiving / shipping warehouse has visibility on expected inbound / outbound handling volumes per hour and can estimate related workload.  ||  Differentiated: Receiving / shipping warehouse has full visibility on inbound / outbound volumes and can calculate related workload.  ||  Best In Class: Workload and tasks are driven by the integrated control tower with visibility to inbound, internal and outbound movement.

items.control_description: 36. How is labor forecasted for the warehouse?
items.remarks: Basic: Minimal labor forecasting; determined based on “gut-feel” on a function by function basis.  ||  Emerging: Distribution center employees have assigned fixed job responsibilities. High level historical productivity measures used to forecast labor.  ||  Advanced: Distribution center has flexible job responsibilities and staffing procedures; labor floats across functions as needed. Task specific historical productivity measures used to forecast labor.  ||  Differentiated: Distribution center has flexible job responsibilities and staffing procedures; labor floats (dynamically directed) across functions, as needed labor planned based on forecasted demand.  ||  Best In Class: Distribution labor is planned by the integrated control tower considering current and future volumes, staffing and expected constraints.

items.control_description: 37. How is labor scheduled for the warehouse?
items.remarks: Basic: No labor balancing across functions.  ||  Emerging: Labor balanced across functions based on managers’ discretion.  ||  Advanced: Pre-shift manual balancing of labor across functions.  ||  Differentiated: System directed pre-shift and intra-shift labor balancing.  ||  Best In Class: Distribution labor is fully directed by the integrated control tower.

items.control_description: 38. How is peak season labor planned for the warehouse?
items.remarks: Basic: No use of temp labor during peak seasons.  ||  Emerging: Some use of temp labor during peak seasons.  ||  Advanced: Temp labor used for scalability during appropriate seasons throughout the year.  ||  Differentiated: Need for temp labor during peak seasons is understood and utilized for scalability.  ||  Best In Class: Digital simulations project needs and expected over-runs / shortfalls for action by management teams.

items.control_description: 39. How is labor performance tracked?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Productivity is tracked at the operational level (e.g. orders shipped, labor cost, etc.). No associate accountability.  ||  Emerging: Productivity is tracked at the process level (e.g. lines / pieces picked per labor $, etc.) No associate accountability.  ||  Advanced: Productivity is captured and reported via WMS at the task and operator level. Associate productivity level accountability is tracked.  ||  Differentiated: Productivity is captured and reported via WMS at the element, travel time, task, and operator level and linked with productivity incentives.  ||  Best In Class: Labor performance is tracked at a element level with digital simulations recommending improvement opportunities to management in real time.

items.control_description: 8. How are your capabilities to track and trace parts in your factory?
items.remarks: Basic: Operators manually insert completion of major process steps. Status and position of parts are visible but accuracy in terms of time dependent on the operator input.  ||  Emerging: Status of parts/ batches (standard parts excluded) is automatically reported though the use of scanners (handhelds) after the completion of key manufacturing steps.  ||  Advanced: Status of parts / batches is automatically reported. E.g. RFID chips enable a touchless status update. after the completion of key manufacturing steps.  ||  Differentiated: Integrated tracking system enables seamless tracking of "all" parts. E.g. part passed automatic scanner, machine is now running at that point of the program, therefore, this production step will be finished in 30 minutes.  ||  Best In Class: Across functions (sales, production, connection to online platform for customers to check status) exact status of parts can be tracked.

items.control_description: 14. What factors are used to determine how/where a cycle count takes place?
items.remarks: Basic: Static cycle counting rules counting equally amongst all SKUs based on time.  ||  Emerging: Cycle counting rules based on A,B,C velocity classifications..  ||  Advanced: Cycle counting rules based on A,B,C velocity classifications as well as shrink history and inventory value.  ||  Differentiated: Cycle counting rules based on recent location frequency history, as well as shrink history and inventory value.  ||  Best In Class: Counting rules dynamically determined based on historical frequency, past shrink / overage data, and inventory value with consideration for forward looking forecasting.

items.control_description: 15. How do you plan for demand differences across various SKU offerings?
items.remarks: Basic: Slow and fast moving SKUs have same planning models used. No differentiation.  ||  Emerging: Some manual differentiation of slow moving planning. Use normal replenishment routines. MTO parameters set..  ||  Advanced: Single Echelon Poisson in use, automatic selection of algorithms.  ||  Differentiated: Multi Echelon Poisson (nonstandard) distributions are used for managing of slow moving skus. Algorithms automatically selected. Lead time optimized.  ||  Best In Class: No touch system used to manage all skus. Machine learning capabilities enabled to manage exception process.

items.control_description: 22. What parameters are used for inventory planning?
items.remarks: Basic: Inventory is planned by manual evaluation of historic data using experience and “gut” feel.  ||  Emerging: Order points, order quantities and safety stock are calculated by a system according to common methods.  ||  Advanced: Order points, order quantities and safety stock are calculated with rudimentary decision support data to analyze tradeoffs.  ||  Differentiated: Space, service level, Investment based optimization of order quantities, order points and safety stocks by item category.  ||  Best In Class: AI / machine learning digital twin simulations recommend inventory positioning changes to reduce overall capital requirements and reduce out-of-stocks.

items.control_description: 23. How do you manage inventory lifecycle events?
items.remarks: Basic: Limited or no changes during the product lifecycle.  ||  Emerging: External events force ad-hoc service levels changes.  ||  Advanced: Lifecycle events are considered in taking service level actions.  ||  Differentiated: Lifecycle events (stage changes) automatically trigger service level actions.  ||  Best In Class: AI / machine learning modules used to predict service failures and adjust procedures to prevent occurrence.

items.control_description: 24. How is your materials management strategy planned?
items.remarks: Basic: No clear materials management strategy evaluation.  ||  Emerging: A materials management evaluation strategy exists; uses largely manual techniques (e.g., reports newly written each time).  ||  Advanced: A documented materials management strategy evaluation exists and is performed upon significant shift in markets or the business.  ||  Differentiated: There is a defined and numerically rigorous process for executing a control loop between strategy and execution, root cause analysis.  ||  Best In Class: Materials management is fully automated including AI driven configuration recommendations.

items.control_description: 25. What is your basis for inventory redeployment decisions?
items.remarks: Basic: Redeployment decisions are manual and sporadic.  ||  Emerging: Redeployment decisions are typically manual but frequent.  ||  Advanced: Redeployment decisions by the system continuously optimize the inventory in the network.  ||  Differentiated: Lifecycle events (stage changes) automatically trigger changes to replenishment and deployment.  ||  Best In Class: Deployment management is fully automated including AI driven configuration recommendations.

items.control_description: 26. How do you determine service / cycle stock optimization?
items.remarks: Basic: Manual Calculation of safety stocks and EOQ by location.  ||  Emerging: Manually optimized safety stock and EOQ for network.  ||  Advanced: Automatically optimized safety stock and EOQ by location.  ||  Differentiated: Multi-echelon network safety stock and order quantity / logistics / slotting quantity optimization in place.  ||  Best In Class: Safety stock and ordering levels are fully automated including AI driven configuration recommendations.

items.control_description: 10. How do you manage reporting and KPI's?
items.remarks:
[Rapid DOMA] Basic: KPI's and reporting are measured and reviewed on an ad-hoc and / or retrospective basis as logistical issues become apparent. 
 Manual data input required to calculate metric performance.  ||  Emerging: KPI's and reporting are standardized across an organization and reviewed on a scheduled cadence. 
Data collected through systemic processes is utilized to calculate performance.
LMS technology provides scheduled or "end-of-shift" summarization of employee performance.  ||  Advanced: KPI's and reporting provide end to end visibility from raw materials / finished goods sources, inbound logistics, distribution / manufacturing sites and outbound shipments to customers. 
 Upstream and downstream KPIs are utilized to predict and prevent supply and service constraints.  ||  Differentiated: KPI's and reporting provides visibility across each function of the enterprise to enable management of functional performance and identify production / transportation mode capacity constraints  ||  Best In Class: Business intelligence fully automates KPI and reporting management and provides standardized dashboards for users. 
 Predictive analytics identify constraints and exceptions in advance to enable event management and upstream / downstream communication.
 IoT sensors and automation equipment integration provides real time visibility and updates for KPI and reporting management.
 LMS and automation integration provides on-standard and efficiency measurements for individuals in real time.

items.control_description: 13. What methods and tools (spreadsheets, simulation models, etc.) are used to assess and optimize the network?
items.remarks: Basic: Spreadsheet based modeling tools with no simulation capabilities.  ||  Emerging: Spreadsheet based modeling tools with limited simulation capabilities..  ||  Advanced: Use of network modeling and simulation tools with limited graphical modeling or scenario management capabilities.  ||  Differentiated: Use of sophisticated network modeling and simulation tools leveraging Optimization technology with robust solvers, graphical modeling and scenario management capabilities with integration into execution systems.  ||  Best In Class: Automated and continuous review process of network using complex, multi-scenario simulations optimizing stock and location capacity across the network.

items.control_description: 16. How do you plan and adjust the distribution cost structure?
items.remarks: Basic: Distribution cost is planned annually by finance teams and provided / updated to operations monthly.  ||  Emerging: Formalized process exists with financial teams to create a "bottoms-up" operations budget with a review process focused on adjusting to quarterly agreed upon changes..  ||  Advanced: Multi-year distribution budget developed and adjusted monthly and integrated with all logistics functions.  ||  Differentiated: Multiyear distribution budget developed and adjusted monthly and integrated with all supply chain functions.  ||  Best In Class: Distribution cost structure is understood as a total cost to serve the business based upon flow channel, is integrated with corporate planning processes and is updated daily / weekly with flow specific analysis..

items.control_description: 17. How are operational processes managed or changed?
items.remarks:
[Rapid DOMA] Basic: Operational processes are changed only when the services provided change.  ||  Emerging: Processes are improved only when major inefficiencies are obvious
.  ||  Advanced: Data is used to identify and measure process improvements.  ||  Differentiated: Processes are improved regularly based on 6 Sigma measures and workflow simulations.  ||  Best In Class: AI / learning digital twin simulations recommend process changes to reduce overall workload.

items.control_description: 18. How are outsourcing decisions made for distribution?
items.remarks:
Basic: Determination for outsourcing of particular function completed on ad hoc basis.  ||  Emerging: Determination for outsourcing made to maintain current state and manage capacity
.  ||  Advanced: Outsourced activities determined by logistics organization based on core / non-core evaluations.  ||  Differentiated: Determination of outsourcing activities done across the supply chain to serve strategic needs.  ||  Best In Class: Outsourcing is considered a strategic investment to broaden the digital capability of the organization.

items.control_description: 19. What is the role of 3PLs in logistics?
items.remarks: Basic: No use and/or strategy for 3PL / 4PL warehouse operations.  ||  Emerging: Use of outside warehouses and 3PLs are ad hoc and without strategy.  ||  Advanced: Clear use and strategy for 3PLs and contracted warehouse capabilities across the network.  ||  Differentiated: 3PL Strategy include participation of 3PL management in broad supply chain improvement initiatives with incentives designed to achieve multi-organizational goals.  ||  Best In Class: 3PLs are considered strategic partners and provide digital solutions to reduce cost.

items.control_description: 20. How are 3PL providers managed?
