items.remarks: Basic: No or minimal performance management of 3rd party partners.  ||  Emerging: 3rd party partners are managed on an ad hoc basis with no standardized performance measures across providers.  ||  Advanced: 3rd party partners are managed on standardized metrics on a regular basis.  ||  Differentiated: 3rd party partners are managed on standardized metrics on a regular basis. The standards are updated regularly in accordance with corporate goals.  ||  Best In Class: 3PLs are incentivized to provide continuous improvement solutions that reduce workload through systemic automation.

items.control_description: 21. How are warehouse operations started up and closed down?
items.remarks: Basic: Start-up and close down based on perceived need. Use of a project plan for move and installation of warehouse resources, equipment and stock. Ad-hoc close-down.  ||  Emerging: Start-up and close down based on perceived need. Use of a detailed project plan for start-up and close-down of operations to ensure seamless customer service.  ||  Advanced: Start-up and close-down based on quantitative network model that determines optimal warehouse location based on trade-off between operational costs, facility costs, transportation costs, inventory investment and customer service.  ||  Differentiated: Startup and closedown based on continually updated quantitative network model that determines optimal warehouse location based on tradeoff between operational costs, facility costs, tax incentives, transportation costs, inventory investment and customer service.  ||  Best In Class: AI / machine learning digital twin simulations recommend network changes to reduce overall cost.

items.control_description: 40. What warehouse management systems (WMS) are in place?
items.remarks: Basic: Mainly manual systems due to inability of current systems to support user’s needs.  ||  Emerging: PC based functionality with no optimization capacity. Minimal WMS complexity with concentration on simple storage and retrieval - basic need for locating inventory for putaway and picking  ||  Advanced: Custom technology solution with functionality based on past requirements Greater emphasis on core WMS capabilities from receive through ship Focus on improving operating efficiencies –labor management, dock scheduling, and yard management. WMS should have ability to adapt to process changes.  ||  Differentiated: Holistic solutions supporting optimization across the extended supply chain. Configurable best of breed packaged supply chain execution systems that link WMS/TMS/LMS. Accurate, historical and forecasted, realtime, shared, and filtered information used to drive decisions. May also integrate with automated warehouse equipment.  ||  Best In Class: Warehouse systems are integrated with the control tower.

items.control_description: 41. What is the distribution IT strategy?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: No defined vision or strategy for transportation IT systems Home-grown applications used on an ad hoc basis.  ||  Emerging: Individual business units make WMS software selections without coordination.  ||  Advanced: WMS is implemented across the businesses based on need and strategic vision for warehousing.  ||  Differentiated: Logistics IT strategy is integrated into corporate IT and business vision strategy.  ||  Best In Class: Logistics IT is integrated into the overall corporate digitization strategy with an emphasis on reducing cost and improving customer service.

items.control_description: 42. How is the warehouse system integrated with internal infrastructure?
items.remarks: Basic: WMS is managed as stand-alone system separate from other logistics systems.  ||  Emerging: Links between ERP / MRP and TMS are unidirectional periodic transfers.  ||  Advanced: ERP / MRP / TMS system and WMS are continuously linked and used to provide information back and forth.  ||  Differentiated: ERP / MRP / TMS system is using WMS in dynamic decision making process.  ||  Best In Class: Warehouse systems are integrated with the control tower.

items.control_description: 43. How is the warehouse system integrated with external providers / customers?
items.remarks: Basic: Information is managed internally and not integrated with external partner (insourced) 3PL manages their own WMS system with minimal integration.  ||  Emerging: Basic integration exists between internal systems and 3PLs (Some EDI with key suppliers).  ||  Advanced: WMS system is linked via periodic transfers to ERP system for updates EDI with most 3PLs.  ||  Differentiated: WMS system is dynamically linked into 3PL & TMS systems for realtime interface.  ||  Best In Class: Warehouse systems are integrated as needed with external parties via the control tower.

items.control_description: 44. How are assets tracked and managed in the warehouse?
items.remarks: Basic: Asset utilization is not tracked. Operational processes are changed only when the services provided change.  ||  Emerging: Asset utilization is estimated. Operational processes are improved only when major inefficiencies are obvious.  ||  Advanced: Asset utilization is tracked and regularly reviewed. Operational processes are improved when inefficiencies become apparent.  ||  Differentiated: Daily asset utilization is tracked and processes are improved based on 6 Sigma process measures and workflow simulations.  ||  Best In Class: Assets are tracked via equipment mounted automation and integrated with the control tower to determine best use / placement.

items.control_description: 45. What is the availability of metrics to business teams?
items.remarks: Basic: Metrics are not captured.  ||  Emerging: Metrics are available via IT systems, however are not reported or reviewed.  ||  Advanced: Metrics are charted and reviewed on a regular basis.  ||  Differentiated: KPIs are shared between departments with focus on continuous improvement.  ||  Best In Class: KPIs are customized to the individual role while building to the total business strategy.

items.control_description: 46. What types of metrics are available to gauge performance?
items.remarks: Basic: Productivity is tracked at the operation level (e.g. orders shipped, labor cost).  ||  Emerging: Productivity is tracked at the process level (e.g. lines received / putaway).  ||  Advanced: Productivity is tracked at the operator / associate level.  ||  Differentiated: Productivity is tracked at the operator / associate and task level.  ||  Best In Class: Performance is tracked at the element level through automated methods without requiring manual entry.

items.control_description: 47. How is individual performance tracked and incented?
items.remarks: Basic: No associate productivity accountability.  ||  Emerging: Productivity is tracked manually through combining system reports.  ||  Advanced: Productivity is captured and reported via WMS at the task and operator level Productivity based incentive structure.  ||  Differentiated: Productivity is captured and reported via WMS at the task and operator level and linked with productivity incentives.  ||  Best In Class: Performance is captured within the warehouse management system and simulated to drive performance / task changes on a real time basis.

items.control_description: 32. How are returns managed?
items.remarks: Basic: Returns systems not documented, systematized or managed.  ||  Emerging: Accept returns without any tracking or resolution. No analysis performed to determine root causes for returns.  ||  Advanced: Spread-sheet based tracking and analysis of issues.  ||  Differentiated: Collaboration between vendor and buyer to resolve issues. Use of case-based reasoning tools.  ||  Best In Class: Return procedures are automated with little manual interaction systemically.

items.control_description: 33. What systems do you use to manage returns?
items.remarks: Basic: No systematic way to process returns.  ||  Emerging: Returns processing handled entirely by customer service department representatives, sometimes causing large backlogs in processing. Customers perceive the process as cumbersome and unfriendly.  ||  Advanced: Electronic processing of returns but requiring significant amount of information because of lack of integration with sales and delivery records. Complexity of the process discourages customers from processing returns.  ||  Differentiated: Electronic (web based) processing of returns rather than through a customer service organization, resulting in significant savings of processing cost for both the customer and returns organization.  ||  Best In Class: Returns systems are automated with little manual interaction outside of the initial receipt.

items.control_description: 34. What is your reverse logistics network strategy?
items.remarks: Basic: No special consideration is made to reverse logistics network strategy.  ||  Emerging: Disconnected sub-chains exist for processing of returns between customer and dealer, dealer and distributor, and distributor to OEM, creating inventory accumulation at many nodes.  ||  Advanced: Reverse logistics management is integrated with the overall supply chain strategy, although the majority of reverse logistics distribution and network decisions mirror the structures used for the forward supply chain.  ||  Differentiated: Reverse logistics are considered an integral part of strategy; considered in all scenarios.  ||  Best In Class: Reverse logistics requirements are simulated alongside standard operations on an ongoing basis with recommendations provided automatically to reduce occurrence and cost.

items.control_description: 35. What is the focus of operations management with respect to reverse logistics?
items.remarks: Basic: Returns processing dismissed off most agendas. Not measured or managed.  ||  Emerging: Returns processing exists but is not actively managed or measured. Management considers returns a “null” business.  ||  Advanced: Returns processing is considered an integral part of the supply chain management business.  ||  Differentiated: Returns processing is considered an integral part of the supply chain management business. Return, repair, and normal order systems have some level of management integration.  ||  Best In Class: Reverse logistics is a very important item in management’s agendas. Areas like repair yield, repair cycle time, utilization of recycled parts as a source of supply / revenue, service / asset optimization receive a lot of attention.

items.control_description: 1. How does your innovation strategy look like?
items.remarks: Basic: Lack of a formalized process.  ||  Emerging: Sporadic approach. Innovation happens in silos. Independent teams within our company are developing digital solutions to enhance our existing product portfolio.  ||  Advanced: Innovation happens centrally coordinated covering digital products, new digital services and new digital business models. Defined process with engaged owners. Partner collaboration for selected projects.  ||  Differentiated: Co-creation of solutions together with partners Increased agility allows for recycling of ideas and reduced number of latestage project recycles.  ||  Best In Class: Open innovation platforms, internal digital Innovation lab. Digital business model team drives innovation within the company in e.g. innovation workshops. Sustained execution resulting in new products and processes that drive value.

items.control_description: 2. How do you involve your partners in the product / process improvement development?
items.remarks: Basic: Partners are not involved in product development.  ||  Emerging: Key-Account managers and product managers assure that key customer requirements are included in the next generation of products.  ||  Advanced: Prototypes are tested in an early stage together with partners and key customers. Feedback is used to enhance the product and assure customer acceptance.  ||  Differentiated: Sales team and planning teams work with partners to co-develop products.  ||  Best In Class: Partners contribute directly to product development (open innovation, co-creation of the products).

items.control_description: 3. How do you ensure to maintain a high quality standard?
items.remarks: Basic: Only few partnerships are established. No QA agreements. Quality assurance completely done internally.  ||  Emerging: Partners are selected based on geographic locations, Some individual QA agreements, QA assigned to suppliers.  ||  Advanced: Partner base management is conducted at the corporate level—plants / regional locations use preferred partners, QA agreements with all relevant suppliers, fully adhered to them.  ||  Differentiated: Digital capabilities enabled to monitor and improve quality at internal and external locations.  ||  Best In Class: Enhanced digital capabilities like sense and respond functions send automated alerts and intelligent insights to monitor and improve quality at internal and external locations.

items.control_description: 4. To what extent do you collaborate with other functions and external partners in the end-to-end supply chain planning processes?
items.remarks: Basic: Planning is done independently by each function within (S)BU.  ||  Emerging: BU internal integration in planning process across sales, SC, operations and controlling.  ||  Advanced: Full internal integration, no integration with external partners.  ||  Differentiated: Full integration of internal and partial integration of external partners with interfaces and well defined processes.  ||  Best In Class: Full integration of internal and external partners (upstream and downstream) with automated interfaces and defined processes.

items.control_description: 5. To which extent is your supply chain planning visible and connected to your partners?
items.remarks: Basic: Real time production and scheduling visibility internally.  ||  Emerging: Wide visibility of real time production and scheduling across functions and through range of devices and displays, including mobility solutions.  ||  Advanced: Full visibility to internal business partners in real time.  ||  Differentiated: Partner have visibility into current production plan and blanked purchase orders exist in line with volumes that are required to satisfy production plan. Key parts on Kanban systems with suppliers.  ||  Best In Class: Partner have near real time, full, digital visibility into scheduling systems, actual performance against schedule and any changes to the plan flow through in real time in both directions; suppliers own and manage inventory until it is pulled into production.

items.control_description: 6. How is the relationship management with partners managed?
items.remarks: Basic: Only few partnerships are established. No QA agreements. Quality assurance completely done internally.  ||  Emerging: Regular communication between the company's operating departments and the partner's operating departments have been established to simplify processes and responsiveness. Communication and relationships on operational level have been established for selective partners. To some extent simplified procurement systems are in use (supplier schedules, supplier point-of-use replenishment, etc.). Channels of communication sometimes unclear.  ||  Advanced: Direct communication between the company's operating departments and the partner's operating departments have been established to simplify processes and responsiveness. Communication and relationships on operating level are widely established. To some extent simplified procurement systems are in use. Communication and relationships between partners are limited to few people only.  ||  Differentiated: Direct communication between the company's operating departments and the partner's operating departments have been established to simplify processes and responsiveness. Communication and relationships on operating level are widely established. Simplified procurement systems are in use widely. Communication and relationships between partners are limited to few people only.  ||  Best In Class: Direct communication between the company's operating departments and the partner's operating departments have been established to simplify processes and responsiveness. Communication and relationships on all levels are widely established, but within clear communication channels. Simplified procurement systems are in use.

items.control_description: 7. To which extent is your engineering and production visible and connected to your partners?
items.remarks: Basic: Limited alignment between support functions and manufacturing strategy, functional boundaries are high and collaboration is low.  ||  Emerging: Support functions are well aligned with the manufacturing strategy within the site.  ||  Advanced: Engineering and manufacturing collaborate from the initial phases of the product life cycle, enabling Design for Manufacturing (DFM).  ||  Differentiated: Customers, engineering and manufacturing collaborate from the initial phases of the product life cycle, enabling Design for Manufacturing (DFM).  ||  Best In Class: Suppliers, customers, partners, engineering, and manufacturing (including partners) collaborate from the initial phases of the product life cycle, enabling Design for Manufacturing (DFM) and product enhancement lifecycle planning.

items.control_description: 8. To what extent can you track and trace your product across the end to end supply chain?
items.remarks: Basic: Limited track and trace capabilities using manual processes. No visibility to in transit inventory.  ||  Emerging: Minimal integration with partners. File transfer process provides track and trace capabilities.  ||  Advanced: High levels of integration with partners. Most locations provide tracking data through established standard data exchange processes.  ||  Differentiated: Robust track and trace capabilities for in transit inventory and static inventory. Technology platform provides one stop shop solution for end to end track and trace capabilities. Decision making driven by manual analytics to a large extent with limited automation.  ||  Best In Class: Near real time track and trace capabilities enabled using digital capabilities for both static and in transit inventory across manufacturing plants, DCs, retail locations, repair vendors. Prescriptive intelligence provides automation and data driven decision making capabilities.

items.control_description: 9. What digital technology is used to facilitate track and trace functionality across your supply chain?
items.remarks: Basic: Manual processes used to meet track and trace requirements.  ||  Emerging: File transfers from partners used to track and trace product across network locations.  ||  Advanced: ERP platform used to gather track and trace data. Minimal integration with transportation carriers.  ||  Differentiated: Visibility solution enabled to facilitate end to end track and trace capabilities. Minimal digital capabilities  AI / ML, RPA used to drive automation and intelligent decision making.  ||  Best In Class: Visibility platform with advanced digital capabilities used to sense and respond to missing / errored transactions.

items.control_description: 10. Do you track static inventory across all network locations?
items.remarks: Basic: Static inventory from company owned locations tracked through manual processes. Minimal integration with 3rd party owned locations.  ||  Emerging: Static inventory from company owned locations tracked through manual processes. Near real time integration with warehouses and DCs. Minimal to no integration with manufacturing plants, retail locations and returns centers.  ||  Advanced: Static inventory from all network locations tracked on a visibility platform.  ||  Differentiated: Static inventory across network locations tracked in near real time. Minimal digital capabilities to recommend inventory optimization.  ||  Best In Class: Advanced digital capabilities used to recommend inventory replenishments, safety stocks, cost benefit analysis.

items.control_description: 11. Does your infrastructure help in tracking in transit inventory across all modes of transportation?
items.remarks: Basic: In transit inventory tracked through manual processes. Minimal integration with 3rd party owned activities.  ||  Emerging: In transit inventory from parcel carriers is tracked. Minimal to no visibility to other modes of transport.  ||  Advanced: Visibility to in transit inventory across all modes of transport.  ||  Differentiated: Robust capabilities to analyze visibility information available based on digital technologies.  ||  Best In Class: Advanced digital capabilities to analyze visibility information and drive intelligent decision making.

items.control_description: 12. To what extent do you utilize digital capabilities to ensure real time tracking?
items.remarks: Basic: No real time tracking capabilities.  ||  Emerging: Near real time tracking capabilities for static inventory.  ||  Advanced: Near real time tracking capabilities for static and in transit inventory.  ||  Differentiated: Robust capabilities to support intelligent decision making using inventory data built on digital technologies.  ||  Best In Class: Advanced digital capabilities used to analyze inventory data and drive intelligent decision making.

items.control_description: 13. What level of data integration exists with your partners-contract manufacturers, 3PLs and transportation carriers?
items.remarks: Basic: Partners share data periodically. No systematic data integration.  ||  Emerging: Partial data integration with minimal data standards.  ||  Advanced: Complete data integration supported by strong data standards.  ||  Differentiated: Digital capabilities used to support intelligent decision making utilizing internal and external partner data.  ||  Best In Class: Advanced digital capabilities used to analyze partner data and drive intelligent decision making.

items.control_description: 14. Do your customers have complete visibility to their shipments?
items.remarks: Basic: Minimal internal shipment visibility based on file transfer processes with no visibility provided to customers proactively.  ||  Emerging: Visibility information provided to customers when requested..  ||  Advanced: Visibility to customers provided on select transactions as information becomes available.  ||  Differentiated: Near real time visibility provided to customers proactively.  ||  Best In Class: Advanced digital capabilities used to provide dynamic ETA along with near real time visibility to customers.

items.control_description: 15. Does your track and trace infrastructure help in sensing and responding to exceptions / errors?
items.remarks: Basic: Manual capabilities used to sense and respond to missing and errored transactions.  ||  Emerging: Minimal analytics capabilities combined with manual activities used to sense and respond to missing / errored transactions.  ||  Advanced: Analytical sense and respond capabilities used to correct missing / errored transactions.  ||  Differentiated: Automated sense and respond to capabilities used to correct missing / errored transactions.  ||  Best In Class: Advanced sense and respond capabilities used to correct missing / errored transactions.

items.control_description: 16. To what extent do you utilize prescriptive intelligence capabilities to automatically identify and correct missing shipment data?
items.remarks: Basic: Manual capabilities used to identify / correct missing and errored transactions.  ||  Emerging: Minimal analytics capabilities combined with manual activities used to correct missing / errored transactions.  ||  Advanced: Analytical capabilities used to correct missing / errored transactions.  ||  Differentiated: Digital capabilities are used to correct missing / errored transactions. Data validation rules help in automating data error identification and correction.  ||  Best In Class: Advanced digital capabilities e.g. prescriptive intelligence, sense and respond, data driven intelligence used to correct missing / errored transactions.

items.control_description: 17. To what extent do your track and trace capabilities help in reducing supply chain costs e.g. shipment expedites, excess inventory, customer experience costs?
items.remarks: Basic: Manual track and trace capabilities do not contribute to supply chain cost savings.  ||  Emerging: Partial track and trace capabilities help in meeting minimal cost savings expectations.  ||  Advanced: Good cost savings based on internal visibility of track and trace functions.  ||  Differentiated: Near real time track and trace capabilities result in significant cost savings.  ||  Best In Class: Advanced digital capabilities identify and drive cost savings across new areas of supply chain.

items.control_description: 18. What is the level of effort required to gather information from multiple systems to drive decision making?
items.remarks: Basic: Each supply chain function e.g. Planning, Sourcing, Distribution has a separate reporting / analytics team. Complex effort to gather data from multiple systems.  ||  Emerging: Centralized data analytics team across all supply chain functions. Complex effort to gather data from multiple systems.  ||  Advanced: Technology platform provides a one stop shop solution for data consolidation. Considerable effort in analyzing data.  ||  Differentiated: Digital capabilities support data analysis thereby providing intelligent insights.  ||  Best In Class: Advanced digital capabilities support intelligent decision making.

items.control_description: 19. Do you have visibility to your reverse logistics processes?
items.remarks: Basic: Reverse logistics operations are managed by 3rd parties with no visibility to supply chain activities.  ||  Emerging: Minimal visibility to activities in the returns centers but no visibility to repair activities.  ||  Advanced: Good visibility to reverse logistics operations including returns centers, repair vendors, liquidation activities.  ||  Differentiated: Digital capabilities like AI,ML and RPA are used to support reverse logistics visibility e.g. repair / liquidation decisions, evaluation of returned products.  ||  Best In Class: Advanced digital capabilities support reverse planning, intelligent repair decisions, liquidation / scrap actions.

items.control_description: 20. Do your track and trace capabilities help in improving overall customer experience?
items.remarks: Basic: Manual track and trace capabilities result in poor customer experience e.g. no real time tracking of shipments, multiple calls to learn about ETAs.  ||  Emerging: Partial track and trace capabilities help in meeting minimal customer expectations.  ||  Advanced: Good customer experience based on internal visibility of track and trace functions.  ||  Differentiated: Near real time track and trace capabilities visible to customers through an external facing interface.  ||  Best In Class: Advanced digital capabilities provide dynamic ETA information to the customer proactively.

items.control_description: 21. Do strong data standards support your track and trace capabilities?
items.remarks: Basic: Manual track and trace capabilities with no data standards.  ||  Emerging: Data standards established and followed for internal data. Minimal to no data standard for 3rd party data.  ||  Advanced: Data standards established and adhered to by partners.  ||  Differentiated: Digital capabilities support intelligent decision making using internal and partner data.  ||  Best In Class: Advanced digital capabilities support automation, prescriptive actions and intelligent decision making.

items.control_description: 22. What is the level of integration between supply chain functions from a visibility perspective?
items.remarks: Basic: Supply chain functions are not integrated.  ||  Emerging: Partial integration between supply chain functions.  ||  Advanced: Full integration between supply chain functions supported by technology platform.  ||  Differentiated: Full integration with minimal digital capabilities.  ||  Best In Class: Advanced digital capabilities support integration between supply chain functions.

items.control_description: 23. How are production schedule created and released?
items.remarks: Basic: Production schedules are created based on “tribal” knowledge using basic business tools such as excel and distributed to the shop floor manually.  ||  Emerging: Production schedules are semi-automated, created using purpose built tools and software. Supervisors can access the schedule from terminals on the shop floor.  ||  Advanced: Schedules are automatically produced at planning horizon, using tools and software that are integrated with all necessary business systems. Operators have access to the schedule at work cells and can provide feedback on the schedule.  ||  Differentiated: Schedules are generated using prescriptive intelligence from digital capabilities. Operators utilize schedule information that provides insights into next best actions.  ||  Best In Class: Schedules are automatically calculated and produced in real-time, updating the schedule and production routing to optimize the production flow.

items.control_description: 24. What is the visibility level across your supply chain?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Information about delays of deliveries are communicated using standard channels (e.g. email, phone, fax, etc.). Status and information of all key internal operations are available in near time (e.g. production status, Inventory levels) Information delays occur since information flows sequentially from one stakeholder to the following.  ||  Emerging: Status and information of all key internal operations are available in near time (production, warehousing, Intra- Inter company logistics, Inventory levels, etc.) Some suppliers provide near time visibility of key steps Limited customer data is collected online.  ||  Advanced: Status and information of all key internal operations are available in real time (production, warehousing, Intra- Inter company logistics, Inventory levels, etc.).  ||  Differentiated: Key information of suppliers and customers is available and monitored in realtime. Information is provided to all key supply chain members at the same time.  ||  Best In Class: Supply chain control tower monitors all E2E supply chain information and provides complete visibility = Logistics visibility and event handling platform “single-source of truth” in logistics. Complete visibility of capacities and stock levels of all key suppliers.

items.control_description: 25. How do you assure product quality and process quality?
items.remarks: Basic: Product and process quality assurance partially by online process analytics. Predefined actions if monitoring shows abnormalities are in place.  ||  Emerging: Standalone advanced data analytic tools in place.  ||  Advanced: Automatic real time product and process quality control through smart sensors and big data analytics.  ||  Differentiated: Process and product quality data shared and optimized across plants and along the value chain. Data shared with third parties including from smart sensors.  ||  Best In Class: Automatic real time process and product quality optimization and steering based on real time big data analytics --> predictive quality, process quality fully automated process changes are automatically integrated into the system.

items.control_description: 26. To which extent is your production visible and connected to your partners (e.g. suppliers)?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Real time production and scheduling visibility internally.  ||  Emerging: Wide visibility of real time production and scheduling across functions and through range of devices and displays, including mobility solutions.  ||  Advanced: Full visibility to internal business partners in real time.  ||  Differentiated: Visibility to major partners and suppliers.  ||  Best In Class: Full real time integration.

items.control_description: 27. Through which visualizations do you support planning and production execution?
items.remarks: Basic: Paper based display and documentation of information on e.g. Gemba boards. E.g. used for daily stand up meetings, and knowledge, information transfer.  ||  Emerging: Advanced user interfaces e.g. tablets and monitors are implemented to e.g. guide operators through critical process steps. Digital recording of issues and performed tasks.  ||  Advanced: Advanced user interfaces e.g. tablets are implemented to increase efficiency of all production personnel. Failure proof solutions are integrated for critical process steps.  ||  Differentiated: Provided information are tailored to the specific needs / skills / education level of the dedicated workforce confirmation of tasks via smart device.  ||  Best In Class: Augmented reality for advanced visualization of integrated solutions.

items.control_description: 28. Beside visibility, do you monitor and control the entire supply chain?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Limited monitoring and managing possibilities - mainly on internal flows and planned flows, e.g. inventories in own warehouses.  ||  Emerging: Selected monitoring and controlling/managing possibilities - mainly on internal flows and planned flows via internal systems.  ||  Advanced: Monitoring and managing / controlling mainly on internal flows and limited to key suppliers via EDI / API.  ||  Differentiated: Monitoring and controlling across the entire supply chain based on daily updates, but not in (near) realtime.  ||  Best In Class: (near) real-time and full flow monitoring and controlling.

items.control_description: 29. To what granularity (batch level, product level, component level, etc.) do you track your product components and quality?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: No traceability of key components and quality during manufacturing process. Data from key quality assurance tests are captured.  ||  Emerging: Key components are tracked through the entire assembly process. Detailed database of the key components and its manufacturing information is available per mouse click.  ||  Advanced: Each component has its unique ID when produced or assembled in-house and can be traced per mouse-click (automatically) to the final product and its owner along the whole product lifecycle.  ||  Differentiated: Supplier quality data are automatically integrated on part level and in the system. Data is used to improve quality through adapting process parameters based on raw material / component quality data.  ||  Best In Class: 360° data exchange to improve quality along the whole produce value chain to improve products and processes on a product and component level (raw, semi and finished goods).

items.control_description: 30. To what extent do you have alerts?
items.remarks: Basic: No usage of alerts.  ||  Emerging: Basic capabilities for alert based management (e.g. alerting for quality deviations) are in place and used by co-workers.  ||  Advanced: Improved capabilities for alert based management connected to the whole supply chain (e.g. alerting for quality deviations and impact on supply chain) are in place and used by co-workers.  ||  Differentiated: Automated alerts are generated for critical supply chain functions. Alerts provide insights to carry out prescriptive actions.  ||  Best In Class: Proactive alert based notification (e.g. for deviations, product recalls) using external unstructured data and smart algorithms.

items.control_description: 31. How much time is spent on capturing product information?
items.remarks: Basic: Co-workers spend a lot of time on firefighting (e.g. to retrieve and map relevant information in case of product recalls).  ||  Emerging: People (e.g. CSC, warehouse) have basic information available to avoid minor firefighting.  ||  Advanced: Co-workers (e.g. suppliers, CSC, warehouse) have the most important information available to avoid major fire fighting, but not in one common platform – no E2E enablement.  ||  Differentiated: Critical supply chain information is available in an E2E platform. Some noncritical information is available in siloed systems.  ||  Best In Class: E2E process for traceability is completely technology enabled and documented in the traceability platform (e.g. no manual workarounds needed).

items.control_description: 32. How much effort is required for you to provide traceability information to your customer?
items.remarks: Basic: Traceability requires a mix of manual and automatic data gathering and integration – there is no platform in place that captures, integrates and visualizes all key traceability information.  ||  Emerging: Improved automatic data gathering to minimize manual effort. Basic process implemented to streamline data gathering.  ||  Advanced: Basic information is automatically throughout the supply chain but the information mainly batch oriented and not real-time.  ||  Differentiated: Information is automatically throughout the supply chain inclusive supplier and subsuppliers but the information mainly batch oriented and not real time.  ||  Best In Class: Near real time traceability platform incl. information from external partners and systems with easy access to the „digital value chain“ of each (unique) product from raw material to customer enabling the ability to take actions only for relevant products.

items.control_description: 33. To what extent is traceability information available for you co-worker?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: Information is only available on aggregated levels. Hence, key actions such as product recalls need to be taken for more products than needed. Traceability information is stored in different systems, in different formats and cannot be easily connected to each other, information mainly batch oriented and not real-time.  ||  Emerging: Information is stored in different systems, but in aligned formats and can be connected automatically.  ||  Advanced: Information is available on multiple levels, depending on the availability in operational systems.  ||  Differentiated: Information is available on multiple levels, depending on the information provided by suppliers  Most internal product traceability information is available in an automated way – however they are not integrated into one common platform – manual integration needed to connect information across multiple systems.  ||  Best In Class: 360° product information for the product flow from raw material to customer and back available and connected to each other reflecting the relationships in an automated way on all relevant granularity levels (e.g. via graph DB). Ability to aggregate and disaggregate product information to the most granular level (e.g. unique identifier for products with possibility to drill down on part level) – differentiation based on product value and criticality (e.g. low value and non critical products might not have unique identifier).

items.control_description: 34. To what extent can you and your customer collaborate around traceability information?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: There is no technology enabled collaboration solution based on one truth in place – collaboration occurs through phone calls, email, etc.  ||  Emerging: Collaboration options for basic traceability information (e.g. who produced the product, which materials have been used) are available for internal users.  ||  Advanced: Traceability information is available for few parts of the supply chain e.g. static inventory.  ||  Differentiated: Minor collaboration options for basic traceability information are available for stakeholders in the supply chain.  ||  Best In Class: Collaboration solution across different types of application (e.g. app, chat, web page, etc.) with a workflow for key use cases (e.g. product recall, communication towards customers and other supply chain partners).

items.control_description: 35. How do you manage accessibility to traceability information?
items.remarks: Basic: No structured way to manage accessibility of traceability information.  ||  Emerging: Only selected co-workers can access the information.  ||  Advanced: Differentiated access to traceability information based on user profile.  ||  Differentiated: Differentiated access to traceability information based on user profile accessed both for internal and external stakeholders.  ||  Best In Class: All internal and external stakeholders have access to the data they need collected on a single source of truth and with a differentiated access based on user profile.

items.control_description: 36. To which extent do you use location based technologies (e.g. RFID, GPS) to improve visibility of shipments and improve fill rates?
items.remarks: Basic: No location based technology.  ||  Emerging: Location based technology in selected internal areas e.g. warehousing or production.  ||  Advanced: Location based technology across the entire company.  ||  Differentiated: Integrated location based tracking also with key partners e.g. suppliers, logistics providers.  ||  Best In Class: Every transaction does have a digital fingerprint and physical material can be traced on global level.

items.control_description: 37. What are your capabilities to track and trace your products?
items.remarks: Basic: Company internally: Mix of automatic and manual tracking (e.g. operator confirms that certain production steps are completed). All major assemblies have a unique identifier but not any single part.  ||  Emerging: Tracking of shipments is integrated in the system. Starting with the shipment of the supplier and ending with goods received at the customer. Information are available in near time.  ||  Advanced: All parts have a unique identifier after receiving from suppliers. All operations are automatically tracked. Tracking is integrated in the systems and provides total visibility in near time (company internally).  ||  Differentiated: All parts have a unique identifier at the beginning of the manufacturing steps - also including suppliers. Key product information is stored and can be traced back in per mouse click location, status (good vs. bad condition) of shipments / products is available in real time.  ||  Best In Class: All parts have a unique identifier and can be tracked across the supply chain. Final assemblies have a unique identifier and are connected (IoT) and track and trace is possible over the complete product lifecycle.

items.control_description: 38. To what extent can you ensure traceability of origin in your supply chain?
items.remarks: Basic: We only have limited overview on material and product flow and cannot follow our products along the value chain.  ||  Emerging: Overview within production and distribution, no access to supplier origin data.  ||  Advanced: Overview within company, no access to supplier origin data.  ||  Differentiated: Overview within company and on selected supplier parts and products.  ||  Best In Class: We have an end-to-end overview and can link the final product to any supplier in our value chain ensuring full traceability in the end-to-end supply chain.

items.control_description: 39. To what extent can you and your customer collaborate around a customer order?
items.remarks: Basic: The customer receives a normal order confirmation via mail without any options to adapt it (e.g. delivery date and time).  ||  Emerging: The customer receives an order confirmation and can collaborate around it. There are no/limited collaboration options around product tracking information available (e.g. collaboration around delivery status, ETA change).  ||  Advanced: Customer manual options to coordinate delivery optimization (e.g. lead time, costs, special service,..).  ||  Differentiated: The customer has automated options to coordinate delivery optimization (e.g. lead time, costs, special service,..).  ||  Best In Class: Delivery can be adjusted according to customers’ needs (exact del. time, costs, special service,...) and customer gets automated proposals. Key information (e.g. ETA, real live status, possibility for changes, questions) is accessible through all relevant applications (e.g. webpage, app, email or SMS) details through an Customer UI.

items.control_description: 40. To what extent can you and your customer gain transparency of customer orders?
items.remarks: Basic: Customers and co-workers have no transparency about the current status and the exact time of arrival.  ||  Emerging: Co-workers have limited transparency about the current status and the exact time of arrival.  ||  Advanced: Co-workers have high transparency about the current status and an exact time of arrival with only a few limitations. Customers have limited transparency.  ||  Differentiated: Customers and co-workers have high transparency about the current status and an exact time of arrival with only a few limitations.  ||  Best In Class: Customers and co-workers have full transparency about the current status and an exact time of arrival. Updates of order in near real-time level of detail to be set by customer depending on preferences (how often, which status updates).

items.control_description: 41. To what extent do you have alert based management in your supply chain?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: A lot of manual tweaks / interventions to retrieve product tracking information and provide them to customers and co-workers.  ||  Emerging: Basic capabilities for alert based management (e.g. alerting for late shipments) are in place and used by co-workers.  ||  Advanced: Information is available in an automated way. However it is not integrated into one common platform. Manual integration partially required.  ||  Differentiated: Focus on exception and alert based management of product tracking information (e.g. proactive alerting in case of deviations).  ||  Best In Class: Proactive alerts provide intelligent insights and help drive prescriptive actions.

items.control_description: 42. How much time do you spend on gathering product and order information?
items.remarks: [Rapid DOMA] Basic: A lot of time spent on firefighting (e.g. to identify shipment status).  ||  Emerging: People (e.g. CSC, warehouse) have key internal information available to avoid major firefighting.  ||  Advanced: All internal data and information is available in specific systems. Limited availability of external data and information.  ||  Differentiated: Most product tracking information (e.g. product location, timestamps, events, external information such as temperature, humidity, vibration) is captured – however, there are no gaps in external data and no utilization of unstructured data.  ||  Best In Class: People can focus on proactively optimizing the supply chain based on available information and smart algorithms (e.g. lead time optimization, logistics provider performance mgmt., route optimization).

items.control_description: 43. How are your capabilities to capture product tracking information in your supply chain?
items.remarks: Basic: Product tracking information (e.g. product location, timestamps, events, external information such as temperature, humidity, vibration) is only partially captured.  ||  Emerging: Tracking information is only available on order line level – not on unique product level.  ||  Advanced: For some products (e.g. white goods), tracking information is available on a unique product level.  ||  Differentiated: For all products, tracking information is available on a unique product level with limited intelligence.  ||  Best In Class: A track and trace platform that captures all internal (e.g. time stamps for events) and external product (e.g. traffic, weather, driver updates) tracking information (incl. structured and unstructured) in near real-time and makes the relevant information accessible to internal and external stakeholders.

items.control_description: 44. How are your capabilities to provide tracking information and ETA to your customer?
items.remarks: Basic: Tracking information (e.g. ETA) is set at the time when the order is confirmed and is not dynamically adjusted considering internal and external information; no real live status of shipment.  ||  Emerging: Product tracking requires a mix of manual and automatic data gathering and integration – there is no platform in place that captures and visualizes all key tracking information centrally.  ||  Advanced: Tracking information is put together based on shipment milestone data provided by partners - warehouse operations, transportation carriers. ETA is not dynamically calculated.  ||  Differentiated: Tracking information (e.g. ETA) is dynamically adjusted considering some basic information (i.e. a milestone model capturing time stamps, no real live visibility).  ||  Best In Class: Tracking information (e.g. ETA) dynamically and continuously adjusted based on near real-time updates (incl. external and unstructured information such as social media data) and real live status of shipment product tracking information (e.g. product location, timestamps, events, external information such as temperature, humidity, vibration) is fully captured.
